title: refactor: migrate graph engine from u64 to QualifiedId
description: The graph engine (graph.rs) uses u64 issue numbers as node keys. The architecture specifies QualifiedId (owner/repo#number) as the graph node key (ARCH §5.5). This causes silent node collision when cross-repo deps reference issues with the same number. Migration scope: (1) Add QualifiedId type to types.rs with Display/FromStr/Hash/Eq. (2) Change DiGraph<u64, ()> to DiGraph<QualifiedId, ()>. (3) Change HashMap<u64, NodeIndex> to HashMap<QualifiedId, NodeIndex>. (4) Update all graph API: build(), compute_ready_set(), compute_unblock_cascade(), would_create_cycle(), detect_all_cycles(), dependency_tree(). (5) Add IssueRef::resolve(owner, repo) -> QualifiedId. (6) Update all tool handlers to pass QualifiedId. (7) Update all tests including proptest.
acceptance_criteria: QualifiedId type exists with roundtrip parse/display test. Graph uses QualifiedId as node key. Two issues with same number from different repos are distinct nodes. All existing tests pass with QualifiedId. Cross-repo property test: graph with mixed-repo issues computes correct ready set.
notes: Deviation from spec: Phase 1 tasks 1.2.1 and 1.2.4 specified QualifiedId but implementation used u64. This is a latent bug for cross-repo deps. Blocks Epic 1.6 (Reconciliation) which assumes QualifiedId.
close_reason: QA passed. All acceptance criteria met. CI fixes committed and pushed (014832a).

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:

Root cause: Graph engine uses u64 issue numbers as node keys (graph.rs:32-38). Per ARCH §5.5, it should use QualifiedId (owner/repo#number) to prevent silent node collision when cross-repo deps reference issues with the same number. QualifiedId type does NOT exist in the codebase yet -- it is only defined in the architecture doc.

Files (unblock-core changes -- the breaking API surface):
- crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs:206-212 -- BlockingEdge uses u64 source/target, must change to QualifiedId
- crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs:37 -- Issue.number is u64, needs QualifiedId field added per ARCH (keeps number too)
- crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs:195 -- RelatedIssue.number is u64
- crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs:221 -- IssueSummary.number is u64
- crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs:259-327 -- IssueRef already has CrossRepo variant with owner/repo/number; IssueRef::resolve() -> QualifiedId needs to be added
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:29-39 -- DependencyGraph struct: DiGraph<u64,()>, HashMap<u64,NodeIndex>, HashMap<u64,Status>, HashMap<u64,IssueState>
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:75 -- build() uses Issue.number as node key
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:140 -- compute_ready_set() uses u64 for node_map lookups
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:222 -- compute_unblock_cascade(closed_number: u64) -> Vec<u64>
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:275 -- would_create_cycle(source: u64, target: u64) -> bool
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:295 -- detect_all_cycles() -> Vec<Vec<u64>>
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:323-328 -- dependency_tree(root: u64, ...) -> Vec<(u64, usize)>
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:375 -- node_map() -> HashMap<u64, NodeIndex> (pub accessor)
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:383 -- inner_graph() -> DiGraph<u64, ()> (pub accessor)
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:391 -- issue_state() -> HashMap<u64, IssueState>
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:399 -- issue_status() -> HashMap<u64, Status>
- crates/unblock-core/src/cache.rs:21-39 -- CacheEntry stores Arc<DependencyGraph> (cascading change)

Files (unblock-mcp consumer changes):
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:620-634 -- dependency_tree() call passes u64 issue_number
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:1001-1003 -- compute_unblock_cascade(issue_number, &[]) passes u64
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:1146-1148 -- would_create_cycle(source, *target_number) passes u64
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/show.rs:130 -- DependencyTreeEntry.issue_number: u64
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/close.rs:32-35 -- CloseResult.issue_number/unblocked use u64
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/depends.rs:19,33 -- DependsInput/DependsResult.source: u64
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs:136-137 -- DependencyGraph::build and compute_ready_set calls

Approach:
1. Add QualifiedId struct to types.rs with: Debug, Clone, Hash, Eq, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, Display (owner/repo#number), FromStr. Include new(), short(local_owner, local_repo), and From<&IssueRef> with repo context.
2. Add IssueRef::resolve(owner: &str, repo: &str) -> QualifiedId method.
3. Add qualified_id field to Issue struct (per ARCH). Keep number field for backward compat with GitHub API layer.
4. Change BlockingEdge source/target from u64 to QualifiedId.
5. Change all 4 HashMap fields in DependencyGraph from u64 keys to QualifiedId keys.
6. Change DiGraph<u64, ()> to DiGraph<QualifiedId, ()>.
7. Update all 6 public graph methods to accept/return QualifiedId instead of u64.
8. Update pub accessors (node_map, inner_graph, issue_state, issue_status) return types.
9. Update IssueSummary.number -- consider adding qualified_id or keeping number + adding owner/repo.
10. Update server.rs: 3 call sites need to construct QualifiedId from owner/repo context + issue number.
11. Update tool handler response types (DependencyTreeEntry, CloseResult, DependsResult).
12. Update all tests in graph.rs (35+ tests, all use u64 make_issue helper).
13. Update proptest strategies to generate QualifiedId values.
14. Update integration tests in crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs (20+ graph-related tests).
15. Add new cross-repo property test: graph with mixed-repo issues computes correct ready set.

Risks:
- BREAKING CHANGE to unblock-core public API. Every downstream crate (unblock-mcp) must update simultaneously.
- IssueSummary and Issue types are serialized to JSON for MCP responses -- QualifiedId must serialize cleanly (consider custom serializer for owner/repo#number string format).
- RelatedIssue only has number field from GraphQL fragments -- needs owner/repo added (check if GitHub API provides it in nested fragments).
- The config.rs repo field is Option<String> in owner/repo format -- needs to be split into separate owner/repo or parsed when constructing QualifiedId.
- proptest strategies need QualifiedId generation -- use fixed owner/repo with random numbers to keep tests focused on graph topology.

Related tests:
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:404-1477 -- 35+ unit tests + 2 proptest properties (all use u64)
- crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs:517-899 -- IssueRef tests (need resolve() tests added)
- crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs -- 20+ tests using DependencyGraph with u64
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs:159-211 -- execute_write_tool test uses u64

REVIEW:
Acceptance: PASS — all five criteria met.
  1. QualifiedId type exists with roundtrip parse/display test: PASS — types.rs:33-84, tests at lines 641-699.
  2. Graph uses QualifiedId as node key: PASS — graph.rs:37-44, DiGraph<QualifiedId,()> and HashMap<QualifiedId,NodeIndex>.

  4. All existing tests pass with QualifiedId: PASS — 134 core + 87 github + 49 mcp lib tests + 2 doctests green.
  5. Cross-repo property test: PASS — cross_repo_same_numbers_distinct_in_graph proptest at graph.rs:1280.

Findings:
- [SUGGESTION] graph.rs:68 — The build() doctest uses a hardcoded inline Issue literal. If Issue gains more required fields in the future, this doctest will break and need manual maintenance. Consider extracting a test helper or noting the maintenance burden.
- [SUGGESTION] types.rs:60-84 — FromStr for QualifiedId uses split_once('/') which accepts owner names containing slashes (e.g. 'org/team/repo#42' parses as owner=org repo=team/repo). Since values come from trusted GitHub API this is low risk, but worth noting for future user-facing parsing.
- [SUGGESTION] server.rs:621-622,1001-1002,1149-1154 — QualifiedId is constructed inline at each call site in server.rs using unblock_core::types::QualifiedId::new(client.owner(), client.repo(), number). Consider a helper method on the server state or a local closure to reduce repetition and ensure consistency.
- [GOOD] types.rs:86-107 — Custom Serialize/Deserialize for QualifiedId as flat string (owner/repo#number) is clean and ensures MCP JSON responses are human-readable.
- [GOOD] graph.rs:85-92 — QualifiedId clone count in build() is optimal: 3 clones + 1 move for 4 data structures that each need ownership.
- [GOOD] graph.rs:1274-1348 — Cross-repo property test is thorough: generates issues in two repos with same numbers, adds intra-repo edges, and verifies node count invariant and ready-set correctness.
- [GOOD] types.rs:372-391 — IssueRef::resolve() is well-designed: Local variant uses context params, CrossRepo ignores them. Clean pattern match.
- [GOOD] graphql.rs:585-616 — extract_blocking_edges correctly constructs QualifiedId for both source and target, with forward-looking doc comment about cross-repo extension.

Security: PASS — QualifiedId is constructed from trusted GitHub API data. FromStr validation rejects empty owner/repo and non-numeric issue numbers. No injection risk (values flow into petgraph, not SQL or shell).

Performance: PASS — QualifiedId (3 heap allocations: owner String + repo String + u64) replaces a single u64, adding memory overhead proportional to node count. For the expected scale (hundreds to low thousands of issues) this is negligible. Clone count in hot paths is minimal.

Tests: PASS — comprehensive coverage including: roundtrip parse/display, serde roundtrip, hash distinctness, IssueRef::resolve for both variants, all graph API methods updated, 3 proptests (ready-set invariants, cycle detection, cross-repo distinctness), 2 explicit cross-repo unit tests. Edge case: no test for QualifiedId with number=0 via FromStr (valid parse, but GitHub issues start at 1 — cosmetic gap).

Verdict: APPROVE

title: Design cross-repo response-shape pattern; patch spec §7/§4 and plan 01 accordingly
description:
**SPEC CONTRACT (MANDATORY):** Before implementing, read the referenced sections of `docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md` and `docs/plans/01-plan-mcp-foundation.md`. This bead description is a pointer only — NOT a spec substitute. Acceptance criteria must be verified against spec + plan files, not assumed from this description.

---

Architect task. Produce patches to docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md and docs/plans/01-plan-mcp-foundation.md for a uniform cross-repo response-shape pattern (successful tool results).

Trigger: spec §7.7 (dep_cycles) returns Vec<Vec<u64>>, but the graph can contain cross-repo QualifiedId nodes. Bare u64 is ambiguous in a cross-repo cycle. User decision (2026-04-16): option (c) — surface mixed-repo references in an explicit field (e.g., warnings/cross_repo_refs), and evaluate as universal pattern across all read tools that return u64 issue numbers.

Deliverable: patches only to docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md and docs/plans/01-plan-mcp-foundation.md. NO standalone design docs.

Acceptance:
1. Inventory: list every tool in spec §7 whose response shape returns bare u64/issue numbers over a graph that may hold cross-repo nodes (candidates: dep_cycles, dep_tree, blockers, unblocks, cascade, ready, list, stats aggregated counts).
2. Pattern: define the canonical shape (field name, type, semantics) for reporting cross-repo ambiguity in successful responses. Document rationale.
3. Spec patch: update §7.7 (dep_cycles) with the new shape; add cross-cutting section (e.g., §4.x 'Cross-repo response semantics' or §11 extension) describing the pattern once, referenced from each affected tool.
4. Plan patch: update docs/plans/01-plan-mcp-foundation.md to reflect the new acceptance criteria and, if needed, sequencing (which tools already implemented need retro-migration).
5. Coordination with sibling beads: the error-side work in unblock-29p.25 (CircularDependency/DuplicateDependency cross-repo context) and unblock-6xj (InvalidIssueRef, CrossRepoAccessDenied) should be cross-referenced in the spec section so the error + response sides form a coherent contract.
6. Retro-compat plan: for each already-implemented tool affected (e.g., dep_tree, blockers, unblocks, cascade, stats), decide migrate-now vs. defer, and log a follow-up bead for each deferred migration.
7. Spec conformity: all Phase 01 invariants (§13, §14) must still hold or be explicitly updated.

Blocks: unblock-29p.11 (dep_cycles) — cannot implement until the pattern is in spec.
Related: unblock-29p.25, unblock-6xj (both about cross-repo semantics on the error side).
close_reason: Merged to main as commit 77c4983 (PR #179). Spec §2.16 + §11.4 + Invariant 14 and plan D6 + GAP-14 + DoD item 11 landed. Unblocks unblock-29p.11 and the 3 retro-fits (cjv, fah, iov).

title: [sub-epic] Cross-repo semantics: spec + plan alignment for Phase 01
description:
Phase 01 progressively adds cross-repo dependency awareness (via QualifiedId/IssueRef). Spec §7 response shapes and §11 error contracts were written assuming single-repo scope, but the graph already holds cross-repo nodes (graphql.rs edge targets). This sub-epic groups all work needed to align spec + plan of Phase 01 with cross-repo semantics.

Scope:
- Response-shape pattern (NEW): uniform handling of cross-repo ambiguity in successful tool results (starting with dep_cycles, applied spec-wide).
- Error-side variants (EXISTING): InvalidIssueRef, CrossRepoAccessDenied (unblock-6xj); extend CircularDependency/DuplicateDependency with cross-repo context (unblock-29p.25).

Deliverable: patches to docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md and docs/plans/01-plan-mcp-foundation.md. No standalone design docs.

Source: QA/investigation of unblock-29p.11 (dep_cycles) surfaced that spec §7.7 returns Vec<Vec<u64>> but the graph can contain cross-repo QualifiedId nodes — a gap the spec does not pin down. User (2026-04-16) decided to align spec on option (c): report mixed-repo cycles via an explicit warnings/refs field, and evaluate as universal pattern.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:

# Context

Phase 01 sub-epic aligning spec + plan with cross-repo semantics via two parallel tracks:
1. Response-shape pattern (§11.4) — uniform `cross_repo_refs: Option<CrossRepoRefs>` field on successful tool results whose bare-`u64` projection drops cross-repo `QualifiedId` nodes. Spec §11.4 already exists (landed by unblock-9f7); retro-fit siblings unblock-cjv (ready), unblock-fah (prime), unblock-iov (close) are DONE; dep_cycles (unblock-29p.11) landed with contract from day one.
2. Error-side variants (§11.1) — InvalidIssueRef + CrossRepoAccessDenied (consumed by unblock-6xj), cross-repo context on CircularDependency/DuplicateDependency (consumed by unblock-29p.25).

# Current state of spec §7 / §11

**§11.4 (docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md:1755-1828)** defines CrossRepoRefs contract. Affected-tools table at :1806-1813 lists four: ready (§7.1), prime (§7.3), dep_cycles (§7.7), close (§8.2). `show` (§7.2), `stats` (§7.4), `list` (§7.5), `search` (§7.6), and the §8 write tools are explicitly EXEMPT (:1815-1826) with rationales. Invariant 14(b) at :1975-1977 locks the contract. §2.16 (:310-319) defines shared type.

**§7.7 (:1179-1207)** — DepCyclesResult ALREADY has `cross_repo_refs: Option<CrossRepoRefs>` field. Returns `cycles: Vec<Vec<u64>>` (:1187) with documented cross-repo projection rules (:1198-1204). Implemented in crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/dep_cycles.rs:148-164.

**§11.1 (docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md:1673-1712)** already lists InvalidIssueRef + CrossRepoAccessDenied variants at :1689-1690 AND the HTTP-code table at :1709-1710 — so the **spec is ALREADY patched for unblock-6xj**; only the code in crates/unblock-core/src/errors.rs lags (see Gap A below). `CircularDependency { source: u64, target: u64 }` (:1685) and `DuplicateDependency { source: u64, target: u64 }` (:1686) still carry bare `u64` and are the target of unblock-29p.25's spec revision.

**Plan §02.02 (docs/plans/01-plan-mcp-foundation.md:297-301)** lists the 13 variants (including the two new ones) — plan also already aligned for 6xj.

**Plan GAP-14 (:767-792)** scopes the §11.4 response-side retro-migration tracking. Plan GAP-14.b (:796-830) covers the ready-set scoping BREAKING CHANGE (unblock-eos.4, already landed).

# Root cause (two open gaps this sub-epic must close)

## Gap A — Code drift from spec §11.1 (consumed by unblock-6xj)

Spec lists InvalidIssueRef + CrossRepoAccessDenied. Code does not:
- crates/unblock-core/src/errors.rs:23-112 — DomainError has 11 variants; InvalidIssueRef + CrossRepoAccessDenied absent.
- Status-code map in errors.rs:120-137 also needs 400/403 arms.
- Module docblock (:7-9) lists only 11 variants — needs update.
- All-variants test (:264-313) must add the two new variants.

**Parse-failure call sites that currently collapse IssueRef FromStr failures onto untyped/validation errors (will become InvalidIssueRef):**
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/dep_remove.rs:188-196 (`parse_ref` — ErrorData hand-built with INVALID_PARAMS)
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:681-688 (show handler)
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:1229-1236 (depends handler — source)
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:1238-1245 (depends handler — target)
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:1486-1501 (create handler — blocked_by list; each element)

**403-path collapse (will become CrossRepoAccessDenied):**
- crates/unblock-github/src/graphql.rs:234-238 (fetch_issue_in_repo: null `issue` → IssueNotFound) — does NOT distinguish 404 from 403; GraphQL repository/issue access denied currently surfaces as GitHubApi/GitHubGraphQL or IssueNotFound.
- crates/unblock-github/src/graphql.rs:255-268 (fetch_issue_ref — cross-repo dispatch entry point).
- crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs:1050-1087 (resolve_issue_ref cross-repo arm — empty node_id → IssueNotFound; 403 not handled distinctly).
- Spec-table entry to examine: crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs:350 doc comment already references HTTP 403 as a real code path for cross-repo writes.

## Gap B — Spec §11.1 lacks cross-repo context on CircularDependency/DuplicateDependency (consumed by unblock-29p.25)

Current shape: `{ source: u64, target: u64 }` — ambiguous when source or target live in a foreign repo. Evidence in code:
- crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs:1504-1516 — explicit `TODO(unblock-29p.25)` pointing at exactly this: DuplicateDependency carries `*source_number` on a cross-repo source; the owner/repo is lost.
- crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs:899-911 — local add_blocked_by DuplicateDependency site (same shape; acceptable today for same-repo path, breaks once we migrate to IssueRef-typed fields).
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:1314-1321 — CircularDependency emitted from the depends handler local-local cycle-check arm, again with bare `u64`. Cross-repo endpoints skip client-side cycle detection (:1324-1330, tracing::warn! fallback only).

**Open design question to answer in the spec patch:** swap `source/target: u64` for IssueRef/QualifiedId? Or keep `u64` and add optional `source_owner`, `source_repo`, `target_owner`, `target_repo`? The bead description asks for backward-compatible Display when both sides are the configured repo — so the patch likely needs either `source: IssueRef` with Display that already collapses to `#n` for Local, or explicit optional owner/repo fields with a fallback.

# Response-shape pattern — universal evaluation (per bead scope item #1)

**Already in spec §11.4:** the four tools whose bare-u64 projection drops cross-repo nodes (ready, prime, dep_cycles, close). Spec §11.4 (:1815-1826) explicitly documents the exempt set with rationales. This sub-epic's work on the response-shape pattern is therefore largely a DOCUMENTATION clean-up task — the pattern is already uniform.

**§7 tool responses audited for u64 fields (confirmation of spec exemptions):**

| Tool | File:line | u64 fields | Cross-repo exposure? | Needs cross_repo_refs? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| §7.1 ready | tools/ready.rs:97-116 | ReadyIssueSummary.number (:125) | Sources guaranteed local by §3.3 Filter 3 (eos.4); cross-repo BLOCKERS surface via cross_repo_refs | DONE (has field) |

# QualifiedId / IssueRef / CrossRepoRefs — current modeling

- **QualifiedId** (types.rs:34-41): `{ owner, repo, number }`, Display `owner/repo#number`, FromStr, Hash/Eq. Used as graph node key (graph.rs). Serialized as flat string.
- **IssueRef** (types.rs:441-522): `Local(u64) | CrossRepo { owner, repo, number }`. `resolve(owner, repo) → QualifiedId`, `normalize(owner, repo) → Self` (collapses configured-repo CrossRepo → Local). `FromStr` and `Display` (`#n` or `owner/repo#n`). NO `JsonSchema` — that's why every MCP tool that accepts an IssueRef in params types it as `String` and parses it in the handler.
- **CrossRepoRefs** (types.rs:831-843): `{ omitted: Vec<String>, summary: Option<String> }` with `JsonSchema`. Serialized as-is (not flat). Shared helper primitives in crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/cross_repo.rs (project_cycle :77, project_all_cycles :105, project_cascade :144, build_cross_repo_refs_with_summary :190, cycles_summary :218, ready_summary :234, close_summary :256).
- **compute_ready_set(issues, configured_owner, configured_repo) -> Vec<IssueSummary>** (graph.rs, spec §3.3:369-441) — enforces Filter 3 scoping invariant.
- **compute_unblock_cascade(closed_qid, _all_issues) -> Vec<QualifiedId>** (graph.rs:283-287) — returns QualifiedIds; the close handler is responsible for projecting down (server.rs:1177-1179).

**IssueNotFoundSnafu (cross-repo collapse points — candidates for CrossRepoAccessDenied:**

So once InvalidIssueRef lands, the hand-built ErrorData sites (dep_remove.rs:188-196, server.rs:681-688/1229-1245/1486-1501) can switch to building DomainError::InvalidIssueRef and flowing through github_error_to_mcp.

A `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer is mandatory on the commit. Option B is additive but uglier; 4 extra Option<String> fields pollute the success path. Recommend user decides before 29p.25 starts.
2. **Display backward-compat.** Tests at errors.rs:215-240 lock exact strings — `"Circular dependency: adding #{source} → #{target} creates cycle"` and `"Blocking relationship already exists: #{source} → #{target}"`. Any revised Display must keep these exact forms when both sides are Local, per bead unblock-29p.25's "Keep backward-compatible Display output when the context is the configured repo" requirement. Implementation must update those tests AND add new tests for the cross-repo Display form.
3. **403 detection is non-trivial.** GitHub REST returns HTTP 403 with `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` for rate-limit 403s (already mapped via RateLimited) AND 403 for SSO/SAML/token-scope denials (which are genuine permission failures). GraphQL returns structured errors like `{ type: "FORBIDDEN", path: [...] }` rather than HTTP 403. The 6xj implementer must carefully distinguish: (a) HTTP 403 + rate-limit → RateLimited (already handled); (b) HTTP 403 not-rate-limited → CrossRepoAccessDenied; (c) GraphQL `type: "FORBIDDEN"` → CrossRepoAccessDenied; (d) null issue + no errors → IssueNotFound (current behavior). 7. **Parallel-track coordination.** Bead description says 29p.25 and 6xj are independent. But 6xj's dep_remove.rs:188-196 parse_ref change and server.rs:1229-1245 depends parse-failure change touch files adjacent to 29p.25's CircularDependency refactor in server.rs:1314-1321. Merge order doesn't matter but both beads need to rebase if the other lands first. Flag in both bead descriptions.

     c. Once a DependencyGraph is in hand, call graph.detect_all_cycles() → Vec<Vec<QualifiedId>>.
  6. For the id-scoped path (params.id.is_some()): after detect_all_cycles(), build the targeted QualifiedId (owner = state.config.owner, repo = state.config.repo, number = id) and keep only SCCs that contain it. This matches spec §7.7 flow step 2 without needing a new graph-engine API — the cost is still O(V+E) + O(cycles × avg_cycle_len). DO NOT add a new public fn on DependencyGraph in this bead (scope creep).
  7. Map QualifiedId → issue number. Policy (propose explicitly in module docs — see R1): keep only QualifiedIds whose (owner, repo) matches the configured repo; skip cycles that contain ONLY cross-repo nodes after filtering (empty). For mixed cycles, return the subsequence of local numbers per cycle — this is the closest honest reading of spec §7.7's 'scoped to configured repo' phrasing. FLAG this decision in the module //! docs and request confirmation (spec is silent on mixed cycles).
  8. Return DepCyclesResult { cycles, count: cycles.len() }.
  9. Unit tests (inside #[cfg(test)] mod tests): (a) empty graph → empty cycles + count=0, (b) no-cycle acyclic graph, (c) two-node cycle maps correctly, (d) three-node cycle maps correctly, (e) id=Some filter matches, (f) id=Some filter excludes, (g) DepCyclesResult JSON shape assertion (cycles + count keys).
  10. Integration test in crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs (mirror stats_aggregates_every_bucket_and_warms_cache): fixture with 2 issues forming a cycle (#6↔#7), one unrelated ready issue, push_fetch_graph_data once, call handle_dep_cycles twice. Assert: call 1 cycles.len()==1 AND contains {6,7}, call 2 is cache-hit (mock.calls().fetch_graph_data()==1 after both calls). Add a second integration test for the id-scoped path. Test names: dep_cycles_returns_all_cycles_from_warm_cache and dep_cycles_targeted_id_filters_to_scc.

Risks:
  - R1 (OPEN QUESTION — surface to the user before writing code): spec §7.7 comment says 'cross-repo cycle members shown as QualifiedId format in future phases'. For Phase 01, if a cycle spans cross-repo nodes, do we (a) silently drop non-local members and return only the local subsequence, (b) skip the whole cycle if any member is cross-repo, or (c) degrade the whole mixed cycle's numbers by returning only local? Simplifying this unilaterally violates the 'never simplify without asking' rule in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md — surface to user. Recommend option (b) 'skip mixed cycles entirely' for Phase 01: it matches the spirit of 'scoped to configured repo' and avoids leaking partial cycle topology. Document whatever choice is made in the module //! docs as an explicit design decision.
  - R2: Graph contains cross-repo QualifiedId **nodes** as edge targets (unblock-github/src/graphql.rs:314 extract_blocking_edges), so detect_all_cycles() may return SCCs with mixed owner/repo. See R1 above.
  - R3: Cache-empty after rebuild — spec §7.7 flow step 1 ('fetch graph data or use cache') implies a hard failure should surface. Mirror stats.rs:383-399 (warn! + direct fetch_graph_data retry + populate cache + return). Do NOT silently return empty cycles — that would be semantically false (R6-style posture per dep_remove module docs).
  - R4: Targeted cycle check — spec §7.7 uses vague 'targeted cycle check involving that node'. Filtering SCCs that CONTAIN the node (my approach) is the most defensible reading. DO NOT invent new graph traversal APIs (e.g. has_path_connecting from a to a on directed edges) — that would duplicate Tarjan's work and add unneeded scope.
  - R5: NEVER register this tool via #[tool] in server.rs — that is sibling unblock-29p.12's job (see dep_remove module docs :81-88 for the same discipline).
  - R6: The Issue struct has a pub number: u64 field (types.rs:136) but graph nodes are keyed by QualifiedId — use QualifiedId.number directly, do NOT cross-reference via issues list (unnecessary O(n) lookup).
  - R7: cycle ordering — Tarjan returns SCC nodes in reverse-finish order, which is not stable across petgraph versions. Tests MUST use set-based assertions (HashSet<u64>) not position-based — mirror graph.rs:1084-1091 detect_all_cycles_finds_two_node_cycle test style.
  - R8: params.id is Option<u64>. Deserialize default is None; no rmcp validation needed. Parameter is the local issue number only (spec §7.7 types it as u64, not IssueRef) — this is intentional. Do NOT accept cross-repo IssueRef here.

Related tests:
  - crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:1062-1122 — detect_all_cycles_* unit tests. Do NOT modify — they lock the Tarjan invariant.
  - crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs:1351-1497 — stats_aggregates_every_bucket_and_warms_cache is the closest integration test shape. Adapt, do not modify.
  - crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs:2012-2126 — dep_remove_local_edge_transitions_source_to_ready for mock stub patterns.

When both are Local, check `graph.inner_graph().contains_edge(source_idx, target_idx)` via `graph.node_map()`. If the edge is absent, return `Validation` error "edge does not exist between source and target" (400 / INVALID_PARAMS per DomainError::status_code errors.rs:125). If either endpoint is cross-repo OR the cache is cold, SKIP the guard and rely on GitHub server-side behaviour — this matches the depends handler's cross-repo strategy and keeps the tool operable when the cache has been invalidated.

The write-tool wrapper rebuilds from `fetch_graph_data` and leaves the cache empty on fetch failure (tools/mod.rs:159-175).

Three direct dependencies are already in place: (1) unblock-29p.1 aligned Status enum — Ready|InProgress|Blocked|Deferred|Closed; (2) unblock-29p.2 aligned ProjectFieldIds — status option slugs `ready`/`blocked`/`in_progress`/`deferred`/`closed`; (3) unblock-29p.5 shipped `reopen_issue()` on the `GitHubApi` trait (crates/unblock-github/src/api.rs:166; client impl at mutations.rs:1178; mock stub at mock.rs:578). Close-tool (crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/close.rs + server.rs:987-1170) is the closest structural sibling (same pattern: write-tool with `execute_write_tool` for the mutation + post-rebuild cascade). Server registration is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE — that lives in sibling bead unblock-29p.12 (which depends on this bead).

Files to create / modify:
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/reopen.rs (NEW) — the handler module. Follow the close.rs / stats.rs layout: declare `ReopenParams { id: u64 }`, `ReopenResult { issue: u64, blocked: bool, status: String }`, and `pub async fn handle_reopen(state: &ServerState, params: ReopenParams) -> Result<ReopenResult, ErrorData>`. Mirror stats.rs module-level docstring density (cache contract, spec cross-ref, R-decisions).
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs:44 area — add `pub mod reopen;` alphabetically (after `ready;` line 42, before `reconcile;` line 43). The 'Core Workflow (6)' section doc at line 23 already lists `reopen` so no docstring update needed.
- crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs — add ≥1 integration test modelled after a write-tool (there is no current write-tool handler test at the `handle_` fn level — close, depends, claim, create are only tested through the full server `#[tool]` method). Use `new_mock()` + `state_with_mock(...)` from tests/common/mod.rs. Seed `mock.push_fetch_issue(Ok(closed_issue))`, `mock.push_reopen_issue(Ok(()))`, and `mock.push_fetch_graph_data(Ok((issues, edges)))` for the rebuild. Sibling bead unblock-29p.13 tracks the broader write-tool integration sweep; the minimum here is ≥1 integration test per bead description.

Spec contract (verbatim, §8.7):
  ReopenParams { id: u64 }
  ReopenResult { issue: u64, blocked: bool, status: String }
  Validation: id positive integer.
  Flow:
    1. Fetch issue, validate IssueState == Closed → else IssueNotClosed or IssueAlreadyOpen
    2. Reopen: REST PATCH state: \"open\"
    3. Rebuild graph to evaluate blocking status
    4. If issue has open blockers: Status → blocked
    5. If no open blockers: Status → ready
    6. Update cache
  API calls: 1 (fetch) + 1 (reopen) + 1-2 (fields) + 1+ (rebuild). Cache: Invalidates.

Approach (step by step):
1. Read spec §8.7 (docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md:1372-1398), then skim the close tool's flow in crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:987-1170 — it's the closest write-tool template with the same rebuild-then-side-effect pattern.
2. Create crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/reopen.rs. Define `ReopenParams` with `#[derive(Debug, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]` — single field `id: u64`. Define `ReopenResult` with `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, JsonSchema)]` — fields `issue: u64, blocked: bool, status: String`. Serialize `status` as the lowercase slug from `status_slug()` (cf. stats.rs:166-174) — either `\"ready\"` or `\"blocked\"` depending on the flow branch, so the wire format matches the Projects V2 option names consumers already see in by_status (list.rs, stats.rs, projects.rs:317).
3. Register the module: add `pub mod reopen;` to crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs alphabetically (between `ready;` and `reconcile;`). Do NOT wire the server handler — that belongs to unblock-29p.12.
4. Implement `pub async fn handle_reopen(state: &ServerState, params: ReopenParams) -> Result<ReopenResult, ErrorData>`:
   a. Validate id: u64 is already unsigned so positivity is implicit; reject 0 with `ValidationSnafu { message: \"id must be >= 1\" }` via the same `validation_error` helper pattern used in search.rs:180-187. See R1 below — spec says \"positive integer\" so rejecting 0 is the safe read.
   b. Clone `state.github` into an Arc and call `execute_write_tool(state, || async move { ... })` (tools/mod.rs:133). Inside the closure:
      - Step 1 (fetch + validate): `let issue = client.fetch_issue(number).await?;`. If `issue.state == IssueState::Open`, return `Err(IssueAlreadyOpenSnafu { number }.build().into())`. Spec §8.7 step 1 says \"IssueNotClosed or IssueAlreadyOpen\" — both exist (crates/unblock-core/src/errors.rs:67-77). IssueAlreadyOpen is the semantically precise variant for \"fetched and it's Open\"; IssueNotClosed is appropriate for a state other than Open or Closed, but today `fetch_issue` only parses Open/Closed (graphql.rs:719-721), so effectively only IssueAlreadyOpen applies — log R2 decision.
      - Step 2 (reopen): `client.reopen_issue(number).await?;` — propagates IssueNotFound on 404 (mutations.rs:1198-1202) through the crate-internal github_error_to_mcp path (errors.rs:40-53).
   c. After `execute_write_tool` returns Ok (which also invalidated + rebuilt the cache per tools/mod.rs:158-175), read the rebuilt graph: `let graph = state.cache.get_graph().await`. If `graph.is_none()` (rebuild failed — tools/mod.rs:167-173 left cache empty), return a Validation-style error OR fall back to a fresh fetch. See R3 below for the decision.
   d. Compute blocked state against the rebuilt graph: use the existing `has_open_blockers(issue, graph)` pattern from stats.rs:187-201 and prime.rs:649. Because the rebuild re-fetches the issue, we must also re-read this issue from the cache (`state.cache.get_issues().await`) OR re-run `client.fetch_issue(number)`. Cache-first is cheaper and matches the §8.7 \"update cache\" wording. Lift the helper to a shared module under `tools/mod.rs` if the dedup is worth it, otherwise duplicate. See R4.
   e. Determine target status + slug: if blocked → `\"blocked\"`, else → `\"ready\"`.
   f. Step 3 (update Projects V2 Status field): mirror the close/claim/depends field-update ladder (server.rs:1046-1080, 1115-1157, 1329-1372). Best-effort: use `client.field_ids().await` + `client.resolve_project_info().await` + `client.get_project_item_id(&issue.node_id, &project_info.id).await` + `client.update_field(..., &FieldValue::SingleSelectOption(option_id.clone()))`. Log warnings via `tracing::warn!` on failure — do NOT propagate. The TODO unblock-b6b.79 (also tracked by unblock-29p.24) already plans to extract a shared helper — do NOT refactor in this bead.
   g. Return `Ok(ReopenResult { issue: number, blocked, status: status_slug })`.
5. Add the `#[instrument]` attribute on `handle_reopen` mirroring stats.rs:350-357 (`name = \"handle_reopen\", skip(state, params), fields(agent.kind, issue_number = params.id)`). Call `info!(\"Reopen tool invoked\")` at the top like close (server.rs:1014-1019).
6. Unit tests (#[cfg(test)] block in reopen.rs): mirror search.rs:288-409 density — cover (a) validation for id == 0 (if R1 accepted), (b) `status_slug`/`ReopenResult` serialization shape, (c) helper for computing blocked state if extracted. No network-dependent tests here — leave those to integration.rs.
7. Integration test (tests/integration.rs): two scenarios to add:
   - `reopen_closed_issue_with_no_blockers_transitions_to_ready` — push fetch_issue returning a Closed issue #42; push reopen_issue Ok(()); push fetch_graph_data returning (issues including #42 re-fetched as Open with no edges involving #42); optionally push field_ids/resolve_project_info/get_project_item_id/update_field Ok(()). Assert ReopenResult { issue: 42, blocked: false, status: \"ready\" } and `mock.calls().reopen_issue() == 1`.
   - `reopen_closed_issue_with_open_blocker_transitions_to_blocked` — same shape but with a BlockingEdge source=#42, target=#99 and issue #99 in Open state in the rebuilt fetch_graph_data. Assert ReopenResult { issue: 42, blocked: true, status: \"blocked\" }.
   - Negative: `reopen_rejects_already_open_issue` — push fetch_issue returning IssueState::Open; no reopen_issue call expected. Assert an error and `mock.calls().reopen_issue() == 0`.

Impact:
- Zero impact on existing tools — the new reopen module is additive. The tool is not yet wired into the server, so no runtime surface changes until unblock-29p.12 lands.
- No changes required in unblock-core — all types already exist (Status, IssueState, errors including IssueAlreadyOpen/IssueNotClosed).
- No changes required in unblock-github — reopen_issue already on trait and mock (unblock-29p.5).
- No cache schema changes — GraphCache already stores Arc<Vec<Issue>> + Arc<DependencyGraph> (extended in unblock-29p.8 commit 5650c58). Issue state (Open/Closed) is snapshotted in the graph at build time (graph.rs:44), so re-evaluating `has_open_blockers` post-rebuild is a pure graph lookup.
- Server registration deferred to unblock-29p.12 (which this bead BLOCKS via that relationship). lib.rs re-export also deferred — check whether any siblings (search/stats/list) added a re-export. They did not: grep of lib.rs shows only module imports through tools/mod.rs. Do not add one here.

Risks / questions to resolve BEFORE implementation:
- R1 (validation of id=0): Spec §8.7 says \"positive integer\". Rust u64 admits 0. Options: (a) reject id=0 explicitly with Validation error — matches §8.7 literal reading; (b) let fetch_issue return IssueNotFound for 0 (current behaviour — GitHub returns 404). Recommendation: (a) — fail-fast before any network call, mirroring the search `limit=Some(0)` rejection (search.rs:204-214). Document the choice in the module docstring.
- R2 (IssueNotClosed vs IssueAlreadyOpen): Spec §8.7 lists both as possible errors from the step-1 validation. `fetch_issue` only ever returns IssueState::Open or IssueState::Closed (graphql.rs:719-721 — any non-\"CLOSED\" falls through to Open). Therefore the handler can only encounter Open (\"already open\") — IssueNotClosed is dead code in practice. Recommendation: use `IssueAlreadyOpenSnafu` for the single live path; add a code comment explaining that IssueNotClosed remains defined in the error enum but is unreachable from the reopen handler today given the fetch_issue mapping. Do NOT invent a third state to trigger IssueNotClosed. Question the user if they want belt-and-braces mapping for defensive forward-compatibility.
- R3 (cache absent after rebuild): `execute_write_tool` leaves the cache invalidated (empty) if `fetch_graph_data()` fails post-reopen (tools/mod.rs:167-173). The reopen has ALREADY succeeded against GitHub at that point — the mutation is not lost. But the handler needs a graph to compute `blocked`. Two options: (a) fall back to `client.fetch_issue(number)` + inspect `blocked_by` directly without a graph — works but requires the related-issue states which may not be on the returned Issue, so falls short; (b) return a special-case Ok(ReopenResult { issue, blocked: false, status: \"ready\" }) with a warning — risks lying to the client; (c) propagate an error that makes it clear the reopen succeeded but the post-reopen evaluation failed. Recommendation: (c) — surface a `GitHubApi` 503-style error with a clear message (\"issue reopened but cache rebuild failed; re-run show to observe final status\") so the client retries `show`. This is consistent with the stats.rs R6 decision to propagate errors rather than hide them. The close tool currently warns and returns an empty cascade (server.rs:1162-1164) — but that's non-fatal for close because `unblocked: []` is semantically valid (no cascade observed). For reopen, `blocked: false` is a functional claim, not a degraded-view placeholder, so the error path is the right call. Question user if they prefer the \"default to blocked=false\" posture for agent robustness.
- R4 (code duplication of has_open_blockers): `has_open_blockers` is duplicated at prime.rs:649 and stats.rs:187, and will be a third copy in reopen.rs. Recommendation: do NOT extract in this bead — extraction belongs in a cleanup bead (analogous to unblock-29p.33 for refresh_cache_from). Duplicate with an identical impl + identical docstring cross-referencing the two siblings. The body is ~10 lines.
- R5 (Projects V2 Status=blocked vs Status=Ready semantics): Spec §8.7 prescribes these exact transitions. There is no \"keep InProgress if it was InProgress\" guard like close-cascade has (server.rs:1126). Implication: reopening an issue that was InProgress before close (rare — close normally goes Done) will downgrade to Ready/Blocked regardless of pre-close status. This is spec-correct. Call it out in the module docstring so future readers know it is intentional.
- R6 (closed-issue blind spot for fetch_graph_data): fetch_graph_data returns OPEN-only issues (unblock-a36 tracks the follow-up). Post-reopen the rebuilt graph WILL contain the just-reopened issue (since it is now Open). So this is NOT a blocker for reopen — flag it only if the reopened issue had closed blockers whose state is not reflected in the rebuilt graph; in that case `has_open_blockers` will return false because the blocker is not in the node map (stats.rs:189 returns false for orphans). If the closed blocker is later reopened the graph needs another rebuild to pick it up. Document this caveat in the reopen module doc. Same behaviour already applies to close cascade, so no new divergence.
- R7 (FieldValue import path): Close tool imports `FieldValue` via `use unblock_github::projects::FieldValue;` in server.rs. A standalone tools/reopen.rs handler needs the same import — mirror close tool usage (server.rs:47 or similar top-of-file).
- R8 (ReopenResult.status Display casing): Spec shows `pub status: String`. Close uses slug 'closed'; stats uses slug 'ready'/'in_progress'/etc. The consistent choice is lowercase slug (`\"ready\"` / `\"blocked\"`). PascalCase (Status::Display) would diverge from stats.by_status keys and list.by_status. Recommendation: lowercase slug — document in the ReopenResult doc string.

Related tests:
- crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs — closest sibling templates are stats tests at integration.rs:1351 and 1503 (both read-tool end-to-end). There is no existing write-tool `handle_*` test at the integration.rs level today. The most relevant pattern is the mock-driven sequence used by stats — push 1+ responses, then assert both the result shape and `mock.calls().*` counters.
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/reopen.rs #[cfg(test)] — mirror search.rs tests 288-409 for ReopenResult shape + validate_id (if R1 accepted).
- crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs:1555-1610 — existing reopen_issue unit tests already verify the REST PATCH body shape and 404 mapping; no changes required here.
- crates/unblock-github/src/mock.rs:863-881 — existing MockGitHubClient reopen counter/queue tests cover the mock's own machinery; no changes required.
- crates/unblock-mcp/tests/e2e_workflow.rs — not required for this bead (no real-GitHub dependency). Sibling unblock-29p.13 tracks the broader integration test sweep.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text: DECISION: Threaded the reopened issue's node_id through execute_write_tool's Ok value (Result<String, Error>) instead of a shared std::sync::Mutex. Avoids holding a sync mutex across await points (clippy await_holding_lock) and keeps data flow linear. The execute_write_tool helper is already generic over the closure's Ok type, so this is a natural fit.

REVIEW:
Acceptance: PASS
  - Spec §8.7 ReopenParams { id: u64 } / ReopenResult { issue, blocked, status } — PASS (reopen.rs:142-166).
  - Validation 'id positive integer' — PASS (R1 fast-fail at reopen.rs:214-223; u64 rejects negatives by type, 0 rejected pre-network).
  - Flow step 1 (fetch + validate state == Closed, else IssueNotClosed/IssueAlreadyOpen) — PASS with R2 caveat documented (only IssueAlreadyOpen is reachable given current fetch_issue parsing; IssueNotClosed kept in the domain enum for forward compat, module doc explicitly notes it).
  - Flow step 2 (REST PATCH state=open via reopen_issue) — PASS (reopen.rs:362).
  - Flow step 3 (rebuild graph) — PASS via execute_write_tool (tools/mod.rs:134-148).
  - Flow steps 4-5 (Status → blocked if open blockers, else ready) — PASS (reopen.rs:403-420) — lowercase Projects V2 slug per R8.
  - Flow step 6 (update cache) — PASS; rebuild happens inside execute_write_tool; cache re-read via state.cache.get_graph()/get_issues() for post-mutation classification.
  - API-call budget (spec says 1 fetch + 1 reopen + 1-2 fields + 1+ rebuild) — PASS; no extra fetch_issue for Phase 2 because node_id is threaded through execute_write_tool's Ok value (see DECISION comment).
  - ≥1 integration test with MockGitHubClient — PASS (5 added: happy-ready, happy-blocked, reject-already-open, reject-zero-id, rebuild-failure).

Findings:
- [WARNING] crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/reopen.rs:405-418 — The 'reopened issue missing from non-empty rebuilt cache' branch silently defaults to blocked=false (Status='ready') and merely logs a warn!. This conflicts with the module-level R3 posture, which argues against 'defaulting to blocked=false' because 'blocked: false is a functional claim, not a degraded-view placeholder'. The in-code comment acknowledges the choice and justifies it via the narrow race window (another agent re-closing between reopen and rebuild), but the inconsistency with the R3 docstring deserves reconciliation: either (a) strengthen the R3 doc to carve out this race-path exception, or (b) surface the same GitHubApi 503-style 'please re-run show' error used when the cache is empty. Today an agent cannot distinguish 'genuinely unblocked' from 'lost-in-race, please retry'. Not a merge-blocker — the behaviour is spec-lenient and the warn! keeps it diagnosable — but worth tightening.
- [SUGGESTION] crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/reopen.rs:386-394 — The synthetic GitHubApi { status: 503, message: ... } error is manually hand-built rather than using a dedicated 'post-mutation rebuild failed' error variant. Works correctly (status 503 → INTERNAL_ERROR through github_error_to_mcp), but a named variant (e.g. unblock_github::errors::Error::PostMutationRebuildFailed { mutation: &'static str, issue: u64 }) would be more searchable and give downstream clients structured data to branch on. Deferrable — shared with the close tool's 'cache not available after rebuild' path (server.rs:1162-1164) which just logs a warning. Consider a follow-up cleanup bead when the field-update helper extraction (unblock-b6b.79) lands.
- [SUGGESTION] crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/reopen.rs:241-291 — update_status_field duplicates the close tool's field-update ladder (server.rs:1046-1080). The TODO at line 242 already tracks the extraction against unblock-b6b.79 / unblock-29p.24, and the reviewer explicitly scoped the extraction out for this bead. Noted here so it is not lost at merge — the extraction would collapse four near-identical ladders (close, claim, depends, reopen) into one.
- [SUGGESTION] COMPLETED comment (2026-04-15 11:54) — reports '5 unit tests + 5 integration tests'. The actual unit-test count is 6 (validate_id_rejects_zero, validate_id_accepts_positive, has_open_blockers_false_when_issue_absent_from_graph, has_open_blockers_true_for_downstream_of_open_upstream, has_open_blockers_false_when_upstream_is_closed, reopen_result_serializes_status_as_lowercase_slug). Off-by-one in the report only; all tests pass. Not a code issue.
- [GOOD] crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/reopen.rs:1-119 — Module-level docs are exceptional. Every R decision (R1-R8) from the INVESTIGATION is cross-referenced with a rationale paragraph, and the three caveats (R2 dead-code IssueNotClosed, R5 intentional InProgress downgrade, R6 closed-blocker blind spot, R3 rebuild failure) are each spelled out with references to the upstream beads that will eventually address them. This is the highest-quality module doc in the tools/ directory and should be the template for future handlers.
- [GOOD] crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/reopen.rs:342-367 — Threading the node_id through execute_write_tool's Ok value (instead of a std::sync::Mutex<Option<String>> shared across the closure and the outer handler) is the right call. Avoids clippy::await_holding_lock, avoids interior-mutability hazards, keeps the data flow linear, and reuses the execute_write_tool generic parameter that was already there. The DECISION comment documents the reasoning.
- [GOOD] crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs:1879-1911 — reopen_surfaces_error_when_post_reopen_rebuild_fails asserts (a) the mock's reopen_issue counter == 1 after the failed rebuild, (b) the error message mentions both 'reopened' and 'show', and (c) the cache is invalidated. This triple invariant is exactly the agent-observable contract for the R3 posture and makes a future regression immediately visible.
- [GOOD] crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs:1851-1877 — reopen_rejects_zero_id_without_fetching deliberately leaves fetch_issue / reopen_issue unstubbed so that any accidental bypass of validate_id would surface as MockNotStubbed (a loud, non-INVALID_PARAMS failure) rather than silently pass through. Great belt-and-braces assertion.

Security: PASS
  - Input validation: id is u64 (no negatives) and zero is rejected pre-network. No injection surface — the only string produced by the handler is the lowercase slug 'ready' or 'blocked', both constants.
  - No sensitive data in logs: tracing::instrument skips params (no secrets leak), info! on invocation carries only issue_number.
  - No new dependencies added; existing GitHubApi trait methods are reused.

Performance: PASS
  - API-call budget matches spec (1 fetch + 1 reopen + 1-2 fields + 1 rebuild). Node_id threading eliminates what would otherwise be a second fetch_issue in the field-update phase.
  - has_open_blockers is O(out-degree) over the node's neighbours — same as the prime.rs and stats.rs copies. R4-tracked duplication is intentional and deferred.
  - No lock held across await points (verified by clippy::await_holding_lock + explicit DECISION note).
  - Cache writes/reads via Arc clones — O(1) lock cost; matches the rest of the tool suite.

Tests: PASS
  - Unit: validate_id (zero + positive boundary), has_open_blockers (orphan / open-upstream / closed-upstream), ReopenResult serialization shape. All three branches of the has_open_blockers helper are exercised.
  - Integration: happy ready, happy blocked, reject already-open, reject zero-id, rebuild failure — exactly the five scenarios enumerated in the INVESTIGATION comment's 'Integration test' section, plus the R3 rebuild-failure case.
  - Gap (non-blocking, for future consideration): no test covers the 'post-rebuild cache non-empty but reopened issue missing from it' race path at reopen.rs:405-418 — i.e. a fetch_graph_data that succeeds but returns an issue set that does not include the just-reopened number. Low probability in practice and explicitly documented in the code comment. A targeted unit test (seed the cache manually then call handle_reopen) would close this gap cleanly if R3 is tightened per the WARNING above.
  - All quality gates green: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings, cargo doc --no-deps --workspace, and 5 reopen integration tests + 6 reopen unit tests all pass locally (verified on branch chore/unblock-29p-9-reopen-mcp-tool).

Verdict: APPROVE

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION (Sherlock):

Root cause / entry point: This is a greenfield MCP read tool implementation, not a bug. The `stats` tool is specified in docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md §7.4 (lines 1028-1058) and docs/plans/01-plan-mcp-foundation.md task 06.03 (line 545-547). No `stats` module exists yet under crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/. The sibling list (unblock-29p.6) and search (unblock-29p.7) tools were merged in commits cd7ff89 / edf4db7 and serve as direct templates. Server registration is explicitly out of scope — that lives in sibling bead unblock-29p.12.

Files to create / modify:
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/stats.rs (NEW) — the handler module. Mirror the layout of crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/search.rs (most recent sibling, simpler than list.rs). Define `StatsParams { milestone: Option<String> }`, `StatsResult { total, by_status, by_priority, blocked_count, ready_count, cycle_count, agents }`, `AgentStats { name, in_progress, completed }`, and `pub async fn handle_stats(state: &ServerState, params: StatsParams) -> Result<StatsResult, ErrorData>`.
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs:44 — add `pub mod stats;` alphabetically (between `setup;` on line 45 and `show;` on line 46 — actually between `search;` line 44 and `setup;` line 45). Update the Query (4) section docstring at line 29 already lists stats; no change needed there.
- crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs — add at least one integration test modelled after the `search_hits_github_and_maps_to_summary_without_touching_cache` test (lines 1095-1216). Use `new_mock()` + `state_with_mock(...)` from tests/common/mod.rs and `mock.push_fetch_graph_data(Ok((issues, edges)))` to drive the handler. Use `Priority::P0..P4` and `Status::{Ready, InProgress, Blocked, Deferred, Closed}` to cover each bucket key.

Approach (step by step):
1. Read the spec §7.4 (docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md:1028-1058) and the sibling search.rs module verbatim — copy its module-level docs layout (cache bypass section replaced with cache-aware section), JsonSchema derives, and validation_error helper is not needed here (no validation for `milestone` beyond normalize_filter).
2. Declare the public types in stats.rs with `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, JsonSchema)]` on the result types and `#[derive(Debug, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]` on params. Priority keys should match the Display form (`\"P0\"`..`\"P4\"`, via `Priority::to_string()` at crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs around line 316+); Status keys should use the lowercase Projects V2 option slugs per the bead description and projects.rs:317 (`\"ready\", \"in_progress\", \"blocked\", \"deferred\", \"closed\"`) — do NOT use `Status::Display` (PascalCase) here because the bead explicitly enumerates the lowercase slugs. Pre-seed every bucket with `0` so callers don't need to null-check absent keys.
3. Implement the cache-aware read path like `handle_ready` (crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:817-861): check `state.cache.is_fresh()`; if stale, call `crate::tools::rebuild_cache(state).await`; then try `state.cache.get_graph()` and iterate issues via a fresh `fetch_graph_data()` call when counts per status/priority/agent are needed. Caveat: `GraphCache` stores `Arc<Vec<IssueSummary>>` for the ready_set and `Arc<DependencyGraph>` for the graph — it does NOT store the full `Vec<Issue>`. To aggregate by_status/by_priority/milestone/agent you need the full Issue set (status/milestone/agent live on Issue, not the graph). Two plausible designs: (a) always `fetch_graph_data()` like list.rs does (crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/list.rs:486-513), refreshing the cache as a side effect, or (b) derive what is possible from the graph (ready_count from ready_set len, cycle_count from graph.detect_all_cycles().len(), blocked_count and everything else still needs Issues). Option (a) is simpler and matches the plan wording \"Read tool, uses cache\" while list.rs already established the precedent that cache is refreshed after a fetch; the spec-level statement \"Cache: Read-only. API calls: 0 (cache hit) | 1+ (rebuild)\" in §7.4 suggests the cache-hit path should avoid a fetch. RISK/QUESTION — see below.
4. Aggregation: iterate issues once; if `milestone` filter is present, skip any issue whose `milestone != Some(filter)` using exact match (same as list.rs milestone filter — `crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/list.rs:395` area). Increment: `total`, `by_status[issue.status.<slug>]`, `by_priority[issue.priority.to_string()]`. Track `blocked_count` for `Status::Blocked` AND/OR for issues with open blockers — see RISK below for ambiguity. Track `ready_count` from `Status::Ready` count OR from the cached ready_set length (these can diverge — see RISK). For `agents`, group open issues by `issue.agent` (skip None): count `in_progress` where `status == Status::InProgress`, and `completed` where `state != IssueState::Open` (but note closed issues are NOT currently returned by fetch_graph_data — see RISK).
5. cycle_count: `state.cache.get_graph().expect(...).detect_all_cycles().len()` (graph method exists at crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:321). The graph is unfiltered by milestone — detect_all_cycles operates on the full dependency graph, not a milestone subset. Applying milestone filter to cycles is semantically fraught (an edge can cross milestones); the spec does not define a scoped cycle semantic. Proposed behaviour: cycle_count always reflects the full graph even when milestone filter is applied; document this in module docstring.
6. Stale/fetch-failure path: mirror list.rs:500-513 — if fetch fails and the cache is empty, return a \"stale\" result. Spec §7.4 does not define a `stale` field on StatsResult, so either (a) propagate the github_error_to_mcp, or (b) add a `stale: bool` field for envelope consistency with list/ready/search. The spec struct has no `stale` field — stick with error propagation unless we add the field intentionally. RISK: question the user on this.
7. Integration test: push a `fetch_graph_data` stub containing issues spanning each Status variant, each Priority variant, two distinct agents, two milestones, and a pair of issues in a cycle (via BlockingEdge pair source→target and target→source). Assert every by_status key present with expected count, every by_priority key present, blocked_count and ready_count match, cycle_count == 1, agents vector length == 2 with correct per-agent in_progress/completed counts. A second test should cover milestone filter: push a result with issues across two milestones, call with `milestone = Some(\"v1.0\")`, assert counts reflect only the v1.0 subset AND cycle_count still reflects full-graph cycles (if chosen; see RISK).

Impact:
- Zero impact on existing tools — the new module is additive.
- No core crate changes (unblock-core is unchanged; all types already exist: Status, Priority, Issue, DependencyGraph with detect_all_cycles, GraphCache with get_graph).
- No unblock-github changes (fetch_graph_data and MockGitHubClient are sufficient).
- Server registration and lib.rs re-export are deferred to unblock-29p.12 (which this bead BLOCKS via that relationship).

Risks / questions to resolve BEFORE implementation:
- R1 (agents shape): Bead description says \"agents[] (list of active agent names)\", but spec §7.4 defines `agents: Vec<AgentStats>` with `name`, `in_progress`, `completed`. These are incompatible. Per the CLAUDE.md rule \"Never do a decision to simplify the solution — question the user\" and the spec-is-source-of-truth principle for the parent epic, implementation MUST follow `Vec<AgentStats>`. Flag this mismatch to the user before coding so the bead description can be corrected.
- R2 (closed issues blind spot): fetch_graph_data returns OPEN issues only (bead unblock-a36 tracks the follow-up). Therefore `by_status[\"closed\"]` will always be 0 and `AgentStats.completed` will always be 0 until unblock-a36 lands. This must be documented in the stats.rs module-level docstring and the tool description, identical to the disclosure list.rs carries at crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/list.rs:18-25.
- R3 (blocked_count vs Status::Blocked): the spec does not define whether blocked_count means \"issues with Status == Blocked\" or \"issues that have at least one open blocker in the graph\" (these can differ after drift). prime.rs uses has_open_blockers() for its `blocked` category (crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/prime.rs:646). Recommend: blocked_count = count of open issues where `issue.status == Status::Blocked OR has_open_blockers(issue, graph)` — matches prime semantics. Document in the module docs. Question the user if unsure.
- R4 (ready_count vs Status::Ready): similarly, ready_count could mean \"Status == Ready\" or \"len(compute_ready_set)\". Recommend: ready_count = len(graph.compute_ready_set(&issues)) to match the tool's name of \"ready\" as a computed property, not a field value. Document this choice.
- R5 (cycle_count under milestone filter): applying milestone to graph cycles has no clean definition. Recommend: cycle_count always reflects the full graph; document this.
- R6 (stale envelope field): spec §7.4 StatsResult has no `stale` field, unlike ReadyResult/ListResult. Decide: propagate errors (mirror search.rs) vs add stale (mirror list.rs). Recommend: propagate errors via github_error_to_mcp — simplest, matches spec, and consistent with search.
- R7 (cache hit strictly zero API calls): spec §7.4 says \"API calls: 0 (cache hit) | 1+ (rebuild)\". This requires aggregation from cached state, but the cache only stores ready_set + graph — not the full issues vec. To honour the zero-API-call cache-hit invariant strictly, we would need to extend GraphCache to also store the issues vec (core crate change, breaking), or we accept list.rs-style always-fetch (violates the cache-hit path of §7.4). Question the user: extend the cache to carry issues, or relax the cache-hit path to \"uses graph cache for cycles, still fetches issues for aggregation\"? This is the biggest architectural decision in the bead.

Related tests:
- crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs — sibling `search_hits_github_and_maps_to_summary_without_touching_cache` (line 1095) and `list_filter_sort_paginate_end_to_end` (line 773) are the closest templates. Add new `#[tokio::test]` functions for stats: one happy-path end-to-end with mixed-status issues covering every bucket + cycle, and one milestone-filter test.
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/stats.rs #[cfg(test)] unit tests — mirror search.rs tests 288-409 for param validation (though stats has minimal validation) and type mapping. Property-type tests for aggregate arithmetic (sum of by_status.values() == total when no milestone) fit well here.
- crates/unblock-mcp/tests/dyn_dispatch.rs — not required for this bead (no new trait methods); skip unless the supervisor wants to exercise dyn-dispatch for handle_stats.

title: Implement search MCP tool: full-text search via GitHub Search API
description: Implement the search read tool per spec (docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md §7.6). Params: query (required, non-empty string), limit (default 20). Returns: issues[] (IssueSummary), count. Flow: call search_issues(query, limit) on GitHubApi trait — query format: repo:{owner}/{repo} is:issue {query}. BYPASSES CACHE ENTIRELY — each search hits GitHub directly. Depends on Issue 5 (search_issues trait method). Add ≥1 integration test with MockGitHubClient. Ref: spec §7.6, plan Epic 06 task 06.02.
close_reason: QA PASS — code review approved (Linus), QA gate passed (Quinn). Follow-up finding unblock-29p.29 tracks missing upstream-error integration test.

INVESTIGATION (Sherlock):

SCOPE
Implement the `search` MCP read tool per spec §7.6 (docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md:1098-1121) and plan Task 06.02 (docs/plans/01-plan-mcp-foundation.md:539-543). Full-text search via the GitHub REST Search API, scoped to the configured repo, BYPASSING THE CACHE ENTIRELY. New module tools/search.rs with SearchParams/SearchResult + SearchIssueSummary + pub async fn handle_search(state, params). Depends on unblock-29p.5 (DONE) which added search_issues(query, limit) -> Vec<IssueSummary> to GitHubApi. Server registration (#[tool] + ToolRouter wiring in server.rs) is EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE — owned by sibling bead unblock-29p.12.

SPEC CONTRACT (verbatim §7.6)
  SearchParams: query: String (required, non-empty), limit: Option<u32> (default 20)
  SearchResult: issues: Vec<IssueSummary>, count: usize
  Validation: query non-empty (after trim per established pattern)
  Flow: (1) call search_issues(query, limit) on GitHubApi; (2) query format is 'repo:{owner}/{repo} is:issue {query}' — ALREADY composed inside GitHubClient::search_issues at mutations.rs:1247, the tool passes the raw user query through; (3) map Vec<IssueSummary> (core) -> Vec<SearchIssueSummary> (JsonSchema-annotated wire type).
  Cache: bypassed entirely. No cache consult, no cache refresh side effect (contrasts with list which refreshes cache as a side effect).
  API calls: exactly 1.

       • Ok(SearchResult { issues, count })

  8. Wire module in tools/mod.rs: add 'pub mod search;' alphabetically. Update the // Query (4) category comment at mod.rs:28-29 — it already lists 'search', just verifying.
  9. Add ≥1 integration test in crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs following the list_returns_filtered_sorted_paginated_issues_via_mock_client pattern. Minimum test shape:
       #[tokio::test] async fn search_hits_github_and_maps_to_summary_via_mock() {
         use unblock_mcp::tools::search::{SearchParams, handle_search};
         let mock = new_mock();
         let seeded = vec![/* synthesize 2 IssueSummary with non-default labels/milestone/url */];
         mock.push_search_issues(Ok(seeded.clone()));
         let state = state_with_mock(Arc::clone(&mock));
         let result = handle_search(&state, SearchParams { query: "ship".into(), limit: Some(5) }).await.unwrap();
         assert_eq!(result.count, seeded.len());
         assert_eq!(result.issues[0].title, seeded[0].title);
         assert_eq!(mock.calls().search_issues(), 1);
         assert_eq!(mock.calls().fetch_graph_data(), 0, "search must bypass cache");

 10. Run the Quality Gate (fmt, clippy --all-targets -D warnings, test --workspace, doc --no-deps). Single commit: 'feat(mcp): implement search MCP tool for full-text issue search'. No 'API:' footer required — unblock-mcp is a binary crate (CLAUDE.md Pub API Change Tracking is scoped to library crates).

IMPACT
  • unblock-mcp only. No changes to unblock-core or unblock-github (search_issues trait method already exists via unblock-29p.5).
  • Unblocks downstream bead unblock-29p.12 (register 6 new tools in server.rs) by adding the search handler surface.
  • No cache coupling: search is the FIRST and (today) ONLY tool that bypasses cache entirely. The contract divergence must be preserved — list/ready/stats all either refresh or consult the cache, and the spec invariant 'search bypasses cache' (§7.6 + §9.1 invariant 10 at line 1823) is a supervisor-readable decision documented in spec.
  • Tests: adds a new integration test pair; no modification of existing tests.

RISKS / OPEN QUESTIONS
  R1. SearchResult shape — spec §7.6 shows Vec<IssueSummary> in the return contract (the CORE type). ReadyResult/ListResult in practice use a local JsonSchema-annotated mirror struct because core::IssueSummary does not derive JsonSchema (verified via grep on /Users/ramosmig/Public/WS-Labs/unblock/crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs — zero JsonSchema derives). RECOMMEND: follow the ReadyIssueSummary/ListIssueSummary precedent — declare SearchIssueSummary locally with JsonSchema derive and map core -> wire. This is consistent with every other MCP tool that returns summaries and was the decision taken on unblock-29p.6 (list tool). User confirmation required since the spec literally says IssueSummary.
  R2. include defer_until and story_points in the wire type? — Core IssueSummary carries both; unblock-29p.5 decision defaults them to None on search responses. Including them keeps the wire type uniform with ReadyIssueSummary and avoids confusing clients that switch between ready and search results. RECOMMEND: include them, always None from this tool. User confirmation desired.
  R3. Logging the raw query string — list logs empty-string filters openly; ready does the same. search, however, forwards an arbitrary user query to GitHub which may contain project-sensitive terms. Precedent from unblock-29p.5: #[instrument(skip(self, query), ...)] at mutations.rs:1238 is intentionally PII-safe. RECOMMEND: #[instrument(skip(state, params), fields(agent_kind = %state.agent_kind_str(), limit = params.limit, query_len = params.query.len()))] — log limit + length, NOT the query itself. Explicit user confirmation desired because ready.rs / list.rs log filter strings plainly.
  R4. limit = Some(0) behaviour — unblock-29p.19 (open, P3) explicitly defers the 0-clamp decision to either the transport layer (mutations.rs:1248) or the tool layer. Spec §7.6 defines default=20 but no explicit lower bound. Consistent pattern: list validates limit 1..=200. RECOMMEND: either reject limit=Some(0) with INVALID_PARAMS at handle_search, or silently upgrade to 1. Either is valid; pick one and DOCUMENT the choice in the module-level //! doc. Cross-link unblock-29p.19. User confirmation needed.
  R5. query must be non-empty AFTER trim — the spec says 'non-empty', which could mean 'non-empty String' or 'non-empty-after-trim'. Following normalize_filter precedent (mod.rs:64) and list.rs' filter-trim discipline, trim before emptiness check. Edge case: query = '   ' -> INVALID_PARAMS. User confirmation not required (safe default).
  R6. Cross-repo search — spec §5.6 does not list search in the cross-repo scope table; §7.6 query format pins 'repo:{owner}/{repo}'. Tool is LOCAL-ONLY. Do not attempt to parse IssueRef. Do not accept an owner/repo param. Documented.
  R7. Empty results — if GitHub returns an empty items[] (or the trimmed query matches zero issues), SearchResult { issues: [], count: 0 }. This is NOT an error. Mirrors list's empty-filter behaviour.
  R8. Error propagation — cache-bypass means network failures MUST surface. Contrast with list (stale=true fall-back) and ready (lazy-rebuild with stale=true). Search has no stale; map the GitHub error via github_error_to_mcp (ErrorData). Consumers receive INTERNAL_ERROR / INVALID_PARAMS / RATE_LIMITED as mapped. User confirmation desired: do we want a conditional 'stale: true' envelope even though spec omits it? RECOMMEND no — follow spec exactly.
  R9. IssueType mapping — SearchIssueSummary::issue_type is Option<String>. Core IssueSummary has Option<IssueType>. Use .map(|it| it.to_string()) (same as ReadyIssueSummary line 99).

title: Implement list MCP tool: filtered, sorted, paginated issue listing
description: Implement the list read tool per spec (docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md §7.5). Params: status, priority, type, milestone, agent, label, assignee, sort (priority|created|updated, default priority), limit (1–200, default 50), offset. Returns: issues[] (IssueSummary), total, stale flag. Flow: fetch graph (cache or rebuild) → filter (AND logic) → sort → record total → paginate (offset/limit). Deterministic sorts: priority ASC → created ASC; created ASC; updated DESC. Cache-aware (read tool, no invalidation). Add ≥1 integration test with MockGitHubClient. Ref: spec §7.5, plan Epic 06 task 06.01.
