comments.text:
INVESTIGATION (Sherlock):

SCOPE
Implement the `list` MCP read tool per spec §7.5 (docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md:1060-1096). Filtered, sorted, paginated view over the full OPEN issue set (not just the ready set). New module tools/list.rs with ListParams/ListResult + ListIssueSummary + a pure filter_sort_paginate helper. A handler in tools/list.rs (pub async fn handle_list) is expected; server.rs registration (#[tool] + ToolRouter wiring) is NOT in scope for this bead — it is explicitly owned by sibling bead unblock-29p.12 ("Register all 6 new tools in MCP server").

SPEC CONTRACT (verbatim §7.5)
  ListParams: status?, priority?, issue_type?, milestone?, agent?, label?, assignee?, sort? (priority|created|updated, default priority), limit? (1..=200, default 50), offset? (default 0)
  ListResult: issues: Vec<IssueSummary>, total: usize, stale: bool
  Validation: limit in 1..=200 if present; sort must be one of "priority", "created", "updated" if present; empty/whitespace filter strings treated as absent
  Flow: fetch graph data (or use cache) → filter by all params (AND) → sort (priority ASC→created ASC, or created ASC, or updated DESC) → record total → paginate (skip offset, take limit). Cache read-only.

ENTRY POINTS / FILES (all paths absolute)
  • /Users/ramosmig/Public/WS-Labs/unblock/crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/list.rs (NEW) — ListParams (JsonSchema Deserialize), ListResult (JsonSchema Serialize), ListIssueSummary (JsonSchema Serialize, re-declared from IssueSummary like ReadyIssueSummary in ready.rs:50-91), a private from_core() conversion, a pure fn filter_sort_paginate(issues: &[IssueSummary], params: &ListParams) -> (Vec<ListIssueSummary>, usize) helper, and a pub async fn handle_list(state: &ServerState, params: ListParams) -> Result<ListResult, ErrorData> orchestrator. Mirror the structure of /Users/ramosmig/Public/WS-Labs/unblock/crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/ready.rs (filter_ready_set pattern at line 118). Document the Status::Closed gotcha (see RISK R1).
  • /Users/ramosmig/Public/WS-Labs/unblock/crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs — add `pub mod list;` in the alphabetical module list at line 34-45 (after init, before prime). Leave execute_read_tool / normalize_filter as-is; list will use normalize_filter just like ready.rs:128-133.
  • /Users/ramosmig/Public/WS-Labs/unblock/crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/prime.rs:715-731 — reference implementation of issue_to_summary(&Issue) -> IssueSummary. If list needs to hydrate from &[Issue] (see APPROACH step 3), this is the copy-from pattern.
  • /Users/ramosmig/Public/WS-Labs/unblock/crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs:397-427 — IssueSummary shape. NOTE: IssueSummary has `created_at` but does NOT have `updated_at` or `assignees` — see RISK R2 and R3.
  • /Users/ramosmig/Public/WS-Labs/unblock/crates/unblock-core/src/cache.rs:87-145 — GraphCache API: get_ready_set() returns only the ready subset; get_graph() returns the DependencyGraph. Neither exposes the full Issue list. Fresh list data therefore requires either (a) a full fetch_graph_data() round trip when the cache is stale or unusable for list, or (b) extending the cache to store all issues. Option (a) is the minimal-scope path — see RISK R4 and the APPROACH.
  • /Users/ramosmig/Public/WS-Labs/unblock/crates/unblock-github/src/api.rs:155 — `fetch_graph_data() -> (Vec<Issue>, Vec<BlockingEdge>)` fetches OPEN issues only (graphql.rs:123 `states: OPEN` in FETCH_GRAPH_DATA_QUERY). This constrains list's status=Closed semantics — see RISK R1.
  • /Users/ramosmig/Public/WS-Labs/unblock/crates/unblock-mcp/tests/common/mod.rs:71-89 — new_mock() and state_with_mock(mock) helpers plus MockGitHubClient pattern for integration test with push_fetch_graph_data.
  • /Users/ramosmig/Public/WS-Labs/unblock/crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs:460-497 — ready_returns_only_open_unblocked_non_deferred_issues is the cache-seeded integration test pattern this bead should mirror with a MockGitHubClient where cache is empty (forcing rebuild) or pre-seeded.
  • /Users/ramosmig/Public/WS-Labs/unblock/crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:805-861 — ready() handler shows the cache-freshness / lazy rebuild / stale flag pattern that list must replicate. Cache is read-only for list (spec §7.5: "Cache: Read-only"), same as ready. The rebuild path uses crate::tools::rebuild_cache(state) at line 839.

APPROACH (step-by-step)
  1. DECIDE the two contract gaps before implementing (RISKS R2 + R3 below). IssueSummary lacks `updated_at` (blocks the `sort=updated` contract) and `assignees` (blocks the `assignee` filter). Do not proceed without a user decision on both. Recommended: (a) extend IssueSummary with `updated_at: DateTime<Utc>` and `assignees: Vec<String>` in unblock-core — additive, marked `API:` per CLAUDE.md — and populate in prime.rs:715, graph.rs:190, mutations.rs:1281 (search_item_to_summary). (b) Alternative: add an updated_at-carrying struct ListIssueSource or keep Issue references. The additive path to IssueSummary is the simplest and most aligned with the spec return type of `Vec<IssueSummary>`.
  2. Build ListParams (JsonSchema, Deserialize) with doc-comments, and validate at handler entry:
      - limit: Some(0) or Some(n) where n > 200 → ValidationSnafu → ErrorData::INVALID_PARAMS with message "limit must be in 1..=200". Spec §7.5.
      - sort: Some(s) where s not in {"priority","created","updated"} → ValidationSnafu → INVALID_PARAMS. Case-sensitive per spec; no normalization.
      - Empty/whitespace filter strings (status, priority, issue_type, milestone, agent, label, assignee): collapse to None via crate::tools::normalize_filter (mod.rs:62).
      - offset has no upper bound; clamp beyond total is a no-op (take 0 elements).
  3. Flow: a) check cache freshness (state.cache.is_fresh()); b) the cache stores only ready_set (IssueSummary for unblocked/open/non-deferred issues), which is NOT what list needs. list must source from the full issue set. Two options, chosen: always call `state.github.fetch_graph_data()`, rebuild the graph + ready set, update the cache (read-only promise preserved: callers do not observe the cache mutation — the data is equivalent), then build a Vec<IssueSummary> by mapping &[Issue] through a local issue_to_summary helper (copy from prime.rs:715). This matches prime.rs's comment at line 7-10: "the cache only stores the ready set — categorising requires the full Issue list". stale=true iff fetch failed AND cache is empty after attempt (mirror ready handler at server.rs:847-852).
  4. Apply filter pipeline on &[IssueSummary] (AND logic) in this order (cheapest literal comparisons first):
      - status: IssueSummary.status.to_string() eq_ignore_ascii_case (spec §7.5 says filter param is Option<String>, Status Display returns "Ready"/"InProgress"/... per types.rs:322-328).
      - priority: IssueSummary.priority.to_string() eq_ignore_ascii_case ("P0".."P4").
      - issue_type: issue_type.map(|it| it.to_string()).is_some_and(eq_ignore_ascii_case), matching ready.rs:138-143.
      - milestone: exact match on Option<&str> (matching ready.rs:149).
      - agent: exact match on Option<&str> (matching ready.rs:151).
      - label: any label eq_ignore_ascii_case (matching ready.rs:153-155).
      - assignee: any assignee eq (case-sensitive — GitHub usernames are case-insensitive per platform, but exact storage; follow ready.rs agent precedent = exact). BLOCKED until R3 decision.
  5. Sort according to `sort` param:
      - default / "priority": (as_sort_key ASC, created_at ASC) — same as compute_ready_set at graph.rs:208-225.
      - "created": created_at ASC.
      - "updated": updated_at DESC. BLOCKED until R2 decision.
      All sorts must be deterministic; tiebreak on qualified_id to ensure stable ordering for pagination (spec §7.5 doesn't mandate tiebreak, but agents will page through; add the deterministic tiebreak).
  6. Record total = filtered_sorted.len(); paginate: skip(offset).take(limit). Map to ListIssueSummary (JsonSchema shape mirroring ReadyIssueSummary at ready.rs:65-91 + updated_at + assignees).
  7. Return ListResult { issues, total, stale }.
  8. Unit tests in tools/list.rs (like ready.rs:165-569): empty-input, all-filters-combined, each filter one-at-a-time, each sort, offset=0/mid/past-end, limit=default/min/max/out-of-range, validation errors (limit=0, limit=201, sort="foo"), empty-string filter normalization for every filter field (precedent in ready.rs:373-462).
  9. Add ≥1 integration test (spec §7.5 acceptance: "≥1 integration test with MockGitHubClient"). Pattern: tests/integration.rs mirror of lines 460-497. Use new_mock() + push_fetch_graph_data with a hand-crafted mix of issues covering all filterable shapes. Invoke the handler directly (pub async fn handle_list). DO NOT invoke via server.$tool dispatch (that codepath lands in 29p.12).
  10. Quality gate: cargo fmt --check --all; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace; cargo doc --no-deps --workspace. Commit message: 'feat(mcp): implement list MCP tool for filtered/sorted/paginated issue listing'. Because this bead does NOT modify unblock-core or unblock-github public surface (assuming R2/R3 decisions agree to keep IssueSummary stable — but see those risks), no API: footer needed at this stage. If IssueSummary is extended, that must be its own earlier commit with API: footer.

IMPACT
  • unblock-mcp tool surface — 1 new read handler. No existing tool signatures change. No impact on cache contract (read-only per spec).
  • unblock-mcp JSON schema (consumed by MCP clients) — list becomes advertised in 29p.12, not here.
  • unblock-core — potentially impacted IFF R2/R3 decisions extend IssueSummary (additive; requires `API:` footer on the unblock-core commit).
  • unblock-github — no change.
  • Per-call cost: 1 GraphQL round trip per invocation unless a prior read tool already rebuilt the cache AND we can prove the cached data is exactly what we need. list needs the full issue set which the cache does NOT expose today → each list call fetches. This is acceptable for phase 01 and documented in spec §7.5 "API calls: 0 (cache hit) | 1+ (rebuild)".

RISKS / OPEN QUESTIONS (MUST confirm with user)
  R1. STATUS=CLOSED FILTER — fetch_graph_data only returns OPEN issues (graphql.rs:123 `states: OPEN` + graphql.rs:282 doc "all open issues"). A list(status="Closed") call will therefore ALWAYS return total=0. This is a silent gap against the user's mental model of 'list everything'. Two paths: (a) document the open-only scope explicitly in the ListParams::status doc-comment and tool description; (b) extend the GraphQL query (and cache semantics) to also fetch CLOSED issues. Option (b) is a multi-crate change (cache TTL semantics, compute_ready_set invariants, reconcile loop) — too big for this bead. Recommend (a) + a follow-up bead if/when agents need closed-issue listing. DECISION NEEDED before commit.

  R2. SORT=UPDATED REQUIRES updated_at ON IssueSummary — Spec §7.5 allows sort="updated" (desc). IssueSummary (types.rs:397-427) does not have updated_at. Issue does (types.rs:170). Options: (a) ADD `pub updated_at: DateTime<Utc>` to IssueSummary (additive, non-breaking in serde-deserialize-skip-missing terms, but BREAKING at the Rust struct construction level for every call site — there are 4 call sites: graph.rs:190-204 compute_ready_set, prime.rs:715-731 issue_to_summary, mutations.rs:1281 search_item_to_summary, integration.rs test fixtures). All call sites are within the workspace, so mechanical fix. Must carry `API:` footer. (b) Define a list-local source struct holding (IssueSummary, DateTime<Utc>) and sort on the pair, then drop updated_at before returning as Vec<IssueSummary>. This keeps IssueSummary stable but diverges from the spec's stated return type intent (agents receiving Vec<IssueSummary> see no updated_at in the JSON, so can't understand the sort order). (c) Extend ListIssueSummary (the JsonSchema shape) with updated_at even if IssueSummary doesn't have it — pull it from the underlying Issue when mapping. Recommend (c) IF combined with sourcing from &[Issue] (not &[IssueSummary]) in the handler — it keeps IssueSummary stable AND exposes updated_at in the public JSON response. DECISION NEEDED. (Precedent: ReadyIssueSummary at ready.rs:65-91 mirrors IssueSummary 1:1 but doesn't need updated_at because ready doesn't offer sort=updated.)

  R3. ASSIGNEE FILTER REQUIRES assignees ON IssueSummary — Spec §7.5 has `assignee: Option<String>`. IssueSummary lacks `assignees: Vec<String>` (it's only on Issue at types.rs:162). Same options as R2: extend IssueSummary OR source list from &[Issue] directly and carry assignees through ListIssueSummary. Recommend the same choice as R2 (consistency). DECISION NEEDED.

  R4. CACHE FRESHNESS vs LIST SEMANTICS — Spec §7.5 says "Cache: Read-only" and "API calls: 0 (cache hit) | 1+ (rebuild)". The cache today holds only the ready set (subset of issues). Two interpretations: (a) list lives on top of the cache when fresh — but the cache doesn't have all issues, so this is impossible without a cache schema change. (b) Treat the ready-set cache as a proxy and always fetch full issues for list — respects 'cache read-only' literally (list doesn't invalidate) even though it does rebuild. Recommend (b): list ALWAYS calls fetch_graph_data, populates both the graph + ready_set cache as a useful side effect (matches prime.rs:343-366). stale=true only when fetch fails AND cache is empty. This is consistent with spec §4.5 invariant that "every field in CacheEntry is reconstructable from GitHub with a single fetch_graph_data() call". Recommend confirming this interpretation before coding.

  R5. EMPTY STRING vs MISSING PARAMS — serde deserializes {"agent": ""} as Some("") which would silently match no results. ready.rs:128-133 + mod.rs:62 normalize_filter already collapses empty/whitespace to None. list MUST reuse normalize_filter for status, priority, issue_type, milestone, agent, label, assignee. NOT a risk — documented precedent, just ensuring it's used consistently.

  R6. STATUS INVARIANT vs LIST FILTER — ready is built atop compute_ready_set which filters out InProgress/Deferred/Closed issues (graph.rs:162-167). list does NOT apply that filter — spec §7.5 is a pure filter over ALL (open) issues regardless of Status. Therefore sourcing list from `state.cache.get_ready_set()` is DOUBLE-WRONG (a) it's already filtered by ready invariants, (b) it's already missing fields. Confirms R4: list MUST rebuild from fetch_graph_data.

  R7. SORT STABILITY — Spec §7.5 prescribes sort tiebreakers only for priority (→ created_at ASC). For sort=created or sort=updated, two issues with identical timestamps have undefined order. Agents paginating will see shuffling if the underlying sort is not stable. Add a final deterministic tiebreak on qualified_id (Display string or number). Minor, but prevents pagination bugs. Not a blocker — confirm preference.

  R8. sort VALIDATION STRICTNESS — spec says sort must be one of priority/created/updated if present; empty string? normalize to None (default priority) or reject? Recommend: normalize empty/whitespace to None (consistent with filter normalization), reject any other non-matching value.

  R9. limit/offset TYPE — spec uses usize; schema derives to `integer`. JsonSchema won't enforce 1..=200 in the schema — server-side validation is mandatory. Return INVALID_PARAMS with a human message.

  R10. offset BEYOND total — not an error; just yields empty issues[] with total > 0. Document in doc comment. No spec guidance; this is the least-surprising Postgres/SQL-style behavior.

RELATED TESTS
  • /Users/ramosmig/Public/WS-Labs/unblock/crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/list.rs — new unit tests (pattern of ready.rs:165-569): empty/all-filters/each-filter/each-sort/pagination-edges/validation-errors/empty-string-normalization. Expect ~30 unit tests to cover the matrix.
  • /Users/ramosmig/Public/WS-Labs/unblock/crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs — add at least one test `list_returns_all_issues_with_paging_and_filtering` using MockGitHubClient (new_mock + push_fetch_graph_data). comments.text: DECISION: For search_issues Projects V2 fields (status, priority, agent, pipeline_stage, claimed_at, story_points, defer_until) are not returned by REST /search/issues. comments.text: DECISION: For cross-repo source duplicate pre-check, only run the comparison when the blocker resolves to the SAME owner/repo as the source. Per GitHub's documented behavior (see graphql.rs:663), the trackedByIssues connection only returns blockers in the same repository as the queried issue, so blocked_by entries on a cross-repo source can only ever contain refs in the source's own repo. Matching on just number (as the local-source path does) would create false positives when a blocker in a different repo has the same number. For non-matching-repo blockers we skip the pre-check and rely on GitHub's server-side rejection — mirroring the existing asymmetric cross-repo blocker behavior.

This collapses "42" and "#42" into the same identity and also rejects a Local ref vs a CrossRepo ref pointing at the configured repo's issue with the same number. Mapped via ValidationSnafu → HTTP 400 → INVALID_PARAMS JSON-RPC code.

The correct approach is to normalize source_ref against client.owner()/client.repo() before branching — if CrossRepo resolves to the configured repo, treat it as Local for all three guards. Same applies to target_ref for the cycle-detection arm. Recommend adding a helper like IssueRef::normalize(&self, owner, repo) -> IssueRef or just pattern-matching on 'resolves to configured repo' everywhere the code currently dispatches on IssueRef::Local(_).

The investigation flagged this as acceptable follow-up (tied to spec §11.1 error variant shape), but the comment thread does not record a tracking bead. Recommend a TODO pointing to the future bead that extends CircularDependency/DuplicateDependency to carry cross-repo context, otherwise this will leak into user-visible error messages without a trace.
- [SUGGESTION] crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/depends.rs:28-30 — 'source: String' schema has no validation (regex/length). The investigation acknowledged this ('precedent in show.rs and create.rs.blocked_by uses plain String. Do not deviate.'). Noting here so future hardening is tracked: a JsonSchema regex enforcing the IssueRef grammar (^(\d+|#\d+|[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+#\d+)$) would reject malformed inputs at the JSON-RPC layer before the handler runs, improving error clarity.

- AuthZ: relies on GitHub server-side authorization — correct design for cross-repo (client cannot unilaterally validate access).
- No secrets, no sensitive logging: source/target are rendered via the existing Display impl, consistent with prior tool handlers.

Performance: CONCERNS (minor)
- Cross-repo source path performs fetch_issue_ref + resolve_issue_ref + mutation = up to 3 GraphQL round-trips (matches spec §8.4 budget: '0-2 (resolve) + 1 (mutation)').
- [CONCERN] Under the aliasing case (CrossRepo pointing at configured repo), the code takes the cross-repo arm of add_blocked_by_refs (mutations.rs:1402) — meaning a caller passing 'acme/widgets#42' for the configured repo incurs an extra fetch_issue_ref round-trip compared to '42'. Same root cause as the [WARNING] above; fixing normalization fixes the perf delta.

Tests: PASS
- dyn_dispatch tests updated and extended (19 pass, +2 new): covers local/local happy path, cross-repo source, and self-reference rejection. Counter-based assertions prove the branching (e.g. field-update path zero calls for cross-repo source).
- [GAP] No test for the aliasing case: source = "acme/widgets#42" where acme/widgets IS the configured repo. This would surface the [WARNING] findings above.
- [GAP] No test for target = cross-repo + source = local (previously the only supported cross-repo config, still valid). Regression risk is low, but explicit coverage would help.
- [GAP] No unit test on add_blocked_by_refs itself (mutations.rs); only through the MCP handler via the mock. Mock-level test of the CrossRepo source arm — especially the duplicate-match-same-repo branch — would lock the DECISION into the codebase.
- Integration tests for depends are explicitly TODO'd to unblock-29p.13; not a blocker for this bead.

Verdict: NEEDS-REFACTORING

Rationale: Spec §8.4 acceptance criteria are met and the cross-repo happy paths are correct, but the aliasing of CrossRepo-pointing-at-configured-repo exposes three silent regressions (cycle detection skipped when it shouldn't be, Projects V2 field update skipped when it shouldn't be, inconsistent result rendering) plus an avoidable performance tax. None of these block a caller who uses the canonical form, but they are real correctness issues for any caller who happens to spell the configured repo explicitly. Recommend the refactoring-supervisor normalize source_ref/target_ref against client.owner()/client.repo() at the top of the handler and switch all three guards + the result renderer to use the normalized form. The remaining SUGGESTIONs are non-blocking and can be tracked as follow-ups.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION (Sherlock):

== D6: Refactor dependency_tree() return type ==

ROOT CAUSE: dependency_tree() at graph.rs:337 returns Vec<(QualifiedId, usize)> — a flat list of (id, depth) tuples. The spec (§2.14 + §3.7) requires structured TreeNode { id, status, state, depth, children: Vec<TreeNode> } with DependencyTree { root, upstream, downstream } separating directional results. Current impl uses a single BFS mixing both directions.

CURRENT SIGNATURE: pub fn dependency_tree(&self, root: &QualifiedId, direction: TraversalDirection, max_depth: usize) -> Vec<(QualifiedId, usize)>
TARGET SIGNATURE: pub fn dependency_tree(&self, root: &QualifiedId, direction: TraversalDirection, max_depth: usize) -> DependencyTree

NEW TYPES NEEDED (in types.rs):
  pub struct TreeNode { pub id: QualifiedId, pub status: Status, pub state: IssueState, pub depth: usize, pub children: Vec<TreeNode> }
  pub struct DependencyTree { pub root: QualifiedId, pub upstream: Vec<TreeNode>, pub downstream: Vec<TreeNode> }

ALGORITHM CHANGE: Current impl does single BFS for all directions. New impl must do SEPARATE BFS passes — one for Upstream (Outgoing) and one for Downstream (Incoming) — and build recursive TreeNode trees instead of flat tuples. The graph already stores issue_status and issue_state maps (populated at build time, lines 85-94) so TreeNode fields can be populated.

SHOW TOOL IMPACT: The spec ShowResult (§7.2) uses separate upstream/downstream fields instead of single dependency_tree field:
  Current: pub dependency_tree: Option<Vec<DependencyTreeEntry>> (show.rs:58)
  Target:  pub upstream: Option<Vec<TreeNode>>, pub downstream: Option<Vec<TreeNode>>
  The DependencyTreeEntry type (show.rs:157) becomes obsolete.
  Server.rs consumer at lines 725-749 maps (qid, depth) tuples to DependencyTreeEntry — must be rewritten.

  - crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs — lines 255-415: 3 tests reference Vec<(QualifiedId, usize)> return type

== G4: Fix compute_ready_set() Status filter ==

ROOT CAUSE: compute_ready_set() at graph.rs:148 only checks IssueState::Open (line 153) but does NOT filter by Status field. Per spec §3.3 pseudocode (lines 368-374), it must also skip InProgress, Deferred, and Closed statuses as 'preserved states'. Status::Blocked is intentionally NOT filtered — the Key note at line 401 confirms Blocked issues with all blockers closed WILL be in the ready set.

CURRENT CODE (graph.rs:151-154): Only checks issue.state != IssueState::Open.
MISSING: After the IssueState::Open check, add:
  if issue.status == Status::InProgress { continue; }
  if issue.status == Status::Deferred { continue; }
  if issue.status == Status::Closed { continue; }

Note: Status::Blocked must NOT be filtered — the spec explicitly says 'Issues with Status::Blocked that now have all blockers closed WILL be in the ready set'. The update_status_fields algorithm (§10) syncs Status afterwards.

Note: The ready tool layer (ready.rs:159) currently does InProgress filtering as a post-filter. After G4, this becomes defensive/redundant but should remain for safety.

Note: The existing TODO at graph.rs:143 references unblock-45a.4 and ARCH §6.2 — this should be removed when implementing G4.

Files:

- crates/unblock-github/src/client.rs:88-94 — Default X-GitHub-Api-Version header is 2022-11-28. REST calls to /projectsV2/*/views and /projectsV2/*/fields MUST override to 2026-03-10. The reqwest Client sets 2022-11-28 as default_headers, so new REST calls need per-request header override.
- crates/unblock-github/src/client.rs:25-42 — GitHubClient struct holds owner field. detect_owner_type() must determine if owner is an org or user to route between /orgs/{org}/ and /users/{user}/ endpoints.

Approach:
1. Add OwnerType enum (Org, User) and detect_owner_type() to client.rs or projects.rs. This calls GET /users/{owner} REST endpoint and checks the 'type' field (Organization vs User).
2. Add ViewLayout enum (Board, Table, Roadmap), RestField struct (id: u64, name: String, data_type: String, options: Vec with nested name.raw parsing), CreateViewParams struct (name, layout, filter, visible_fields), ProjectView struct (id, number, name, layout, node_id, filter, visible_fields, etc.) to projects.rs.
3. Implement list_rest_fields() in projects.rs: GET /orgs|users/{owner}/projectsV2/{n}/fields with X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2026-03-10 header override. Parse options[].name as {raw, html} nested object — extract .raw. Returns Vec<RestField> with integer IDs.
4. Implement create_view() in projects.rs: POST /orgs|users/{owner}/projectsV2/{n}/views with 2026-03-10 header. Body: name, layout, filter, visible_fields. Returns ProjectView.
5. Implement list_views() in projects.rs: Uses GraphQL query (NOT REST — no GET /views endpoint exists). Query: node(id: projectId) { ... on ProjectV2 { views(first: 50) { nodes { id name number layout filter } } } }. Returns Vec<ProjectView>.
6. Add integration tests to tests/integration.rs following existing patterns (skip if no GITHUB_TOKEN).
7. Add doc comments on all pub items.

- API version header override: reqwest default_headers include X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28. Per-request .header() call should override the default for the same header name — verify this works (reqwest appends vs replaces). If it appends, need to build a separate reqwest::Client or use RequestBuilder::headers() with a new HeaderMap.
- options[].name nested object: The REST API returns options[].name as {raw: string, html: string} not a plain string. Must use custom deserialization — either a wrapper type or serde(deserialize_with).

title: 1.4.4 setup tool — expanded (views + field discovery)
description:
Implement the expanded 'setup' MCP tool in crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/setup.rs — configures a Projects V2 project with all required fields AND 5 pre-configured views.

NOTE: The previous bead (unblock-45a.3) delivered basic field creation only. This bead covers the full setup spec including views, field discovery via REST, and owner type detection.

#[tool] macro on struct SetupTool
Input: SetupParams {
  project: Option<u64>,   // project number (auto-detect if absent)
  dry_run: Option<bool>,  // report only, no mutations
}
Output: SetupResult {
  fields_created: Vec<String>,    // names of fields that were newly created
  fields_existing: Vec<String>,   // names of fields already present
  views_created: Vec<String>,     // names of views that were newly created
  views_existing: Vec<String>,    // names of views already present
  project_number: u64,
  fields_missing: Vec<String>,    // field names not resolved (warn only)
  dry_run: bool,
}

Tool logic (matches ARCH §10.7 flow):
1. Resolve project (auto-detect or use param). If no project found → error with hint to run init
2. Query existing fields (GraphQL: setup_fields flow)
3. Create missing fields — 7 total, skip existing (idempotent):
   Priority (single_select), Status (single_select), IssueType (single_select),
   Agent (text), StoryPoints (number), DeferUntil (date), ReadyState (single_select)
4. Detect owner type: GET /orgs/{owner} → org, 404 → user
5. Query existing views via GraphQL list_views()
6. Discover all field IDs via REST list_rest_fields() — needed for visible_fields in view creation
7. Create missing views via REST POST /views (idempotent — skip if name already exists):
   - ://ready    → layout: board, filter: 'Ready State:ready'
   - ://team     → layout: board, filter: ''  (all open)
   - ://pipeline → layout: table, filter: ''
   - ://roadmap  → layout: roadmap, filter: ''
   - ://timeline → layout: roadmap, filter: ''
8. If dry_run: skip all mutations, return what WOULD be created
9. Return SetupResult with full report

API calls: 1 (query fields) + 0-7 (create fields) + 1 (owner type) + 1 (query views) + 1 (list fields REST) + 0-5 (create views)
Idempotent: safe to run multiple times.
design: Reference: ARCH §10.7, ARCH §8.5. Owner type detection routes view/field REST calls between /orgs/{org}/projectsV2/... and /users/{user}/projectsV2/... endpoints. The REST API version 2026-03-10 must be sent for all view/field endpoints. View visible_fields must use integer IDs from list_rest_fields(), NOT global node IDs. The idempotency check for views compares by name — if a view with the same name exists, skip it. Dry run must not make any mutating API calls (query-only). The ProjectNotConfigured error with a hint to run init must be returned when no project is found.

Must be expanded: add views_created, views_existing, project_number to SetupResult; change project type from Option<u32> to Option<u64>; remove fields_skipped (bead calls it fields_existing); add fields_missing for dry-run.
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:365-440 — Current setup handler. Must be expanded with steps 4-7: detect_owner_type, list_views, list_rest_fields, create missing views. Dry-run path must also query views.

- crates/unblock-github/src/projects.rs:1129-1243 — list_views() already implemented (GraphQL query through org/user).
- crates/unblock-github/src/projects.rs:206-222 — CreateViewParams struct: name, layout, filter (Option), visible_fields (Option<Vec<u64>>).
- crates/unblock-github/src/projects.rs:148-171 — ViewLayout enum (Board, Table, Roadmap) with Display impl.
- crates/unblock-github/src/projects.rs:224-243 — ProjectView struct returned by list_views/create_view.
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs:101-115 — execute_write_tool pattern: runs op, then rebuilds cache. Setup handler already uses this for field creation.
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/errors.rs:72-82 — github_error_to_mcp() for error conversion.
- crates/unblock-github/src/errors.rs:72-73 — ProjectNotConfigured error variant (status 412).

Approach:
1. Update SetupParams: change project from Option<u32> to Option<u64>; keep dry_run.
2. Update SetupResult: rename fields_skipped to fields_existing; add views_created (Vec<String>), views_existing (Vec<String>), project_number (u64); keep fields_created, fields_missing. Remove project_id (bead spec uses project_number instead).
3. Expand server.rs setup handler - after field creation (step 3), add:
   Step 4: call client.detect_owner_type() to get OwnerType.
   Step 5: call client.list_views(owner_type) to get existing views.
   Step 6: call client.list_rest_fields(owner_type) to get all field integer IDs.
   Step 7: for each of the 5 required views, check if name exists in existing views. If not, build CreateViewParams with name, layout, filter, visible_fields (all field IDs from step 6) and call client.create_view(owner_type, &params).
4. Define the 5 view specs as a const array: ://ready (board, filter Ready State:ready), ://team (board, no filter), ://pipeline (table, no filter), ://roadmap (roadmap, no filter), ://timeline (roadmap, no filter).
5. Update dry-run path: also query views via list_views() and report what WOULD be created vs existing. Must call detect_owner_type() even in dry-run (it is a read-only GET). Do NOT call create_view or setup_fields in dry-run.
6. For view visible_fields: collect all integer field IDs from list_rest_fields() result. Note: roadmap views may not support visible_fields per ARCH doc. Check if visible_fields should be None for roadmap layout.
7. Handle the 'no project configured' case: if resolve_project_info() fails with ProjectNotConfigured, return error with hint to run init.
8. The setup handler currently uses execute_write_tool for field creation. The view creation step happens AFTER field creation. Consider: either (a) run field creation through execute_write_tool, then do view creation separately (views don't affect the dependency graph cache), or (b) wrap the entire sequence in a single execute_write_tool. Option (a) is cleaner since view creation doesn't need cache rebuild.

- Type mismatch: bead spec says project: Option<u64> but current code has Option<u32>. Must update to u64 for consistency with GitHubClient.project_number().

comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: Feature implementation — new 'init' MCP tool that bootstraps a Projects V2 project. No existing init.rs file; must be created from scratch. The tool creates a project container via the createProjectV2 GraphQL mutation, with idempotency via title matching.

Files:
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/init.rs (NEW) — main tool implementation: InitParams, InitResult, InitTool registration
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs:34 — must add 'pub mod init;' and the init tool is a read-pattern tool (no cache invalidation per bead spec)
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:126-202 — tool_router impl block where init tool must be registered (follow setup tool pattern)
- crates/unblock-github/src/projects.rs:889 — detect_owner_type() already exists, returns OwnerType::Org or OwnerType::User
- crates/unblock-github/src/projects.rs:348-399 — resolve_project_info() shows the GraphQL pattern for querying projects by number
- crates/unblock-github/src/graphql.rs:329 — graphql() method for making GraphQL calls
- crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs — existing mutation patterns to follow for createProjectV2
- crates/unblock-github/src/client.rs:25-42 — GitHubClient struct (owner, repo, project_number fields)
- crates/unblock-github/src/errors.rs — Error enum with all variants needed (GitHubGraphQL, GitHubApi, ProjectNotConfigured, etc.)
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/errors.rs:72 — github_error_to_mcp() converter

Approach:
1. Add new methods to GitHubClient in projects.rs:
   a. resolve_owner_node_id(owner_type: OwnerType) -> Result<String, Error> — GraphQL query for org { id } or user { id }
   b. list_owner_projects(owner_type: OwnerType) -> Result<Vec<(u64, String, String)>, Error> — query organization/user { projectsV2(first:20) { nodes { number title url } } }
   c. create_project(owner_node_id: &str, title: &str, description: Option<&str>, public: bool) -> Result<(u64, String), Error> — createProjectV2 mutation returning (number, url)
2. Create crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/init.rs with:
   - InitParams struct (scope, title, description, public — all Option) with JsonSchema + Deserialize
   - InitResult struct (project_number: u64, url: String, created: bool, scope: String, hint: String) with JsonSchema + Serialize
   - Tool logic: detect_owner_type (or use scope param) -> resolve_owner_node_id -> list_owner_projects -> match title -> create if not found -> return result with hint message
3. Add 'pub mod init;' to crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs
4. Register init tool in server.rs tool_router impl (follow setup pattern but use execute_read_tool since no cache invalidation needed per bead spec)
5. Write integration tests in the init.rs module or a separate test module
6. Title default: '{repo} Tasks' per bead spec; scope auto-detection via detect_owner_type()

Risks:
- Bootstrap mode: bead says init must work when no project is configured (project_number is None). The current resolve_project_info() requires a project_number and returns ProjectNotConfigured if absent. Init must NOT call resolve_project_info() — it creates the project from scratch using owner/repo only.
- The createProjectV2 mutation requires ownerId (node ID), not owner login. Must resolve org/user node ID via separate GraphQL query: query { organization(login: X) { id } } or query { user(login: X) { id } }.
- detect_owner_type() currently uses GET /users/{owner} and checks the 'type' field. The bead description says 'GET /orgs/{owner} -> 200=org, 404=user' but the existing implementation uses /users/{owner} and checks account_type. Either approach works; recommend using the existing detect_owner_type() to avoid duplication.
- PRD default title is 'Unblock — {repo}' but bead description says '{repo} Tasks'. Bead spec takes precedence.
- The init tool should NOT use execute_write_tool (which does cache invalidation + graph rebuild). Per bead: 'Use execute_read_tool() pattern' since init does not affect the dependency graph.
- Idempotency: projectsV2(first:20) may miss projects if >20 exist. Consider pagination or document the limitation.

Related tests:
- crates/unblock-github/tests/integration.rs — existing integration test patterns (CloseIssueGuard, test client setup)
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs:142-360 — unit test patterns for tool execution helpers
- New tests needed: unit tests for InitParams/InitResult, integration tests for the 6 acceptance criteria

title: Add GITHUB_URL config for GHE git remote auto-detection
description: parse_github_url() is hardcoded to github.com hostnames, so auto-detecting owner/repo from .git/config fails for GitHub Enterprise. The API URL (GITHUB_API_URL) cannot be reliably used to derive the web/remote URL because github.com uses api.github.com while GHE uses host/api/v3. Add a new GITHUB_URL env var (default https://github.com) that parse_github_url uses instead of hardcoded prefixes.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: parse_github_url() in crates/unblock-github/src/client.rs:232-252 hardcodes 'github.com' as the hostname in both HTTPS prefixes (https://github.com/, http://github.com/) and the SSH prefix (git@github.com:). For GHE users whose remote origin points to e.g. ghe.corp.com, the function fails with 'not a GitHub URL'. The GITHUB_API_URL env var cannot be reverse-engineered into a web hostname because github.com uses api.github.com while GHE uses host/api/v3 -- different patterns.

Files:
- crates/unblock-github/src/client.rs:232-252 -- parse_github_url() with hardcoded github.com prefixes (the bug)
- crates/unblock-github/src/client.rs:236-238 -- HTTPS prefix strip (needs to use configurable host)
- crates/unblock-github/src/client.rs:244 -- SSH prefix strip (needs to use configurable host)
- crates/unblock-github/src/client.rs:177-209 -- resolve_repo() calls parse_github_url at line 208 but does not pass any host/config
- crates/unblock-core/src/config.rs:40-80 -- Config struct needs new github_url field
- crates/unblock-core/src/config.rs:168-234 -- Config::load_from() needs to read GITHUB_URL env var

- docs/unblock-prd-github.md:720 -- env var table in PRD
- docs/unblock-architecture-github.md:1245 -- Config struct in arch doc

Approach:
1. Add github_url: String field to Config in crates/unblock-core/src/config.rs (default: https://github.com). Add DEFAULT_GITHUB_URL constant. Read GITHUB_URL env var in load_from() with trailing-slash stripping (same pattern as api_base_url).
2. Change parse_github_url() signature to accept github_url parameter: fn parse_github_url(url: &str, github_url: &str) -> Result<(String, String), Error>. Build HTTPS prefixes dynamically from github_url (e.g. https://ghe.corp.com/ and http://ghe.corp.com/) and SSH prefix (e.g. git@ghe.corp.com:) by extracting the host from github_url.
3. Update resolve_repo() to pass config.github_url to parse_github_url(). resolve_repo already receives &Config so this is straightforward.
4. Update all existing tests in client.rs (lines 319-378) to pass the default github_url value. Add new GHE-specific tests (e.g. parse_github_url with https://ghe.corp.com host).
5. Add config.rs tests for GITHUB_URL loading, default, and trailing-slash stripping.
6. Update README.md env var table and relevant docs.

Risks:
- parse_github_url is pub (public API). Changing its signature is a breaking change for any external caller. Consider adding a parse_github_url_with_host variant or making the old one a wrapper with default host. However, since this is an internal workspace crate, the breaking change is acceptable.
- SSH prefix construction: need to extract just the hostname from the github_url (which is a full URL like https://ghe.corp.com). Use url::Url parsing or simple string manipulation to get the host.

title: 1.4.13 E2E workflow integration test
description:
Implement a full end-to-end integration test in crates/unblock-mcp/tests/e2e_workflow.rs that exercises all 10 Phase 1 MCP tools in sequence against a real GitHub repository.

Test sequence:
1.  init — create (or reuse) a Projects V2 project for the test repo
2.  setup — create 7 fields + 5 views on the test project
3.  create — create issue A (no deps) with priority P1
4.  create — create issue B (blocked by A) with priority P2
5.  create — create issue C (no deps) with priority P3
6.  ready — verify: A and C in ready set, B not in ready set
7.  depends — add B blocked by C explicitly (B now blocked by A and C)
8.  claim — claim issue A for agent 'test-agent'
9.  ready — verify: A no longer in ready set (claimed), C in ready set
10. update — update A's priority to P0, add label 'urgent'
11. comment — post comment on A
12. show — show A, verify comment and label appear
13. close A — verify: A closed, B still blocked (still has C)
14. close C — verify: C closed, B now in ready set (cascade)
15. ready — final verify: B in ready set, A and C not present
16. Cleanup: close B

All assertions use re-fetches or ready results to confirm state.
design: Reference: PRD §8. This test requires a real GITHUB_TOKEN and UNBLOCK_REPO pointing to a test repository (can be the unblock repo itself with a test label). Gate with #[cfg(feature = 'e2e')] or #[ignore] with environment variable check. The test creates and closes real GitHub Issues and may create a real GitHub Project — ensure cleanup runs on both success and failure (use a guard/defer pattern). The init step is idempotent so re-running against the same repo is safe. Setup step 2 creates views — also idempotent.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] All 10 tools called in sequence without error
- [ ] init (step 1) succeeds or returns existing project (idempotent, created or created: false)
- [ ] setup (step 2) creates fields and views without duplicates on rerun
- [ ] ready set is correct at each check point (steps 6, 9, 15)
- [ ] claim sets correct fields (Status=InProgress, Agent='test-agent')
- [ ] cascade works: close A → B still blocked; close C → B unblocked
- [ ] B appears in ready set after both A and C are closed
- [ ] comment appears on issue A
- [ ] update changes priority and adds label
- [ ] show returns correct data including comment
- [ ] Cleanup: all created issues closed at end (guard/defer pattern)
- [ ] Test runs in CI with GITHUB_TOKEN set (gated by feature flag or env var check)
close_reason: Closed

5. claim: ClaimParams{id, agent?} -> ClaimResult{issue_number, agent, claimed_at}
6. close: CloseParams{id, reason?} -> CloseResult{issue_number, unblocked: Vec<u64>}
7. show: ShowParams{id, include_comments?, include_deps?} -> ShowResult{issue, body_sections, blocking, blocked_by, dependency_tree, comments}
8. depends: DependsParams{source, target: String} -> DependsResult{source, target, message}
9. comment: CommentParams{id, body} -> CommentResult{issue_number, comment_url}
10. update: UpdateParams{id, priority?, status?, labels_add?, labels_remove?, assignees_add?, assignees_remove?, body_section?, milestone?, story_points?, defer_until?} -> UpdateResult{number, url, fields_updated, hint}

Approach:
1. Create file crates/unblock-mcp/tests/e2e_workflow.rs
2. Gate the test with an env var check (has_github_token() + UNBLOCK_REPO check), return early if not set — same pattern as existing integration tests.
3. Implement a CloseIssueGuard that manages multiple issue numbers (Vec) for batch cleanup — adapt from the single-issue guard in unblock-github integration tests.
4. The test CANNOT call tool handlers directly via UnblockServer methods because they take rmcp Parameters<T> wrappers. 5. The E2E test flow must call setup before create to ensure field_ids are cached on the client (client.set_field_ids()). Without setup, project field assignment silently fails.
6. After each write operation, call rebuild_cache(&state) to keep the cache fresh for ready checks — or call the full execute_write_tool pattern.
7. For ready verification steps, use the pattern: get_ready_set from cache + filter_ready_set.
8. Use #[tokio::test(flavor = 'multi_thread')] for the test since CloseIssueGuard's Drop uses block_in_place which requires multi-thread runtime.

title: 1.4.11 update tool
description:
Implement the 'update' MCP tool in crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/update.rs — updates issue metadata and Projects V2 fields.

#[tool] macro on struct UpdateTool
Input: UpdateParams {
  id: u64,
  priority: Option<Priority>,
  status: Option<Status>,
  labels_add: Option<Vec<String>>,
  labels_remove: Option<Vec<String>>,
  body_section: Option<BodySectionUpdate> { section: SectionName, content: String },
  milestone: Option<String>,
  story_points: Option<f64>,
  defer_until: Option<DateTime<Utc>>
}
Output: Issue (updated issue, re-fetched)

Tool logic:
1. fetch_issue(id) → IssueNotFound if absent
2. If priority/status/story_points/defer_until changed: update Projects V2 fields via update_field()
3. If labels_add/labels_remove: update via REST PATCH (add labels, then remove)
4. If milestone: resolve milestone number by name, update via REST PATCH
5. If body_section: parse current body into BodySections, update target section, write back via REST PATCH
6. Rebuild cache (execute_write_tool)
7. Return re-fetched Issue
design: Reference: PRD §6.1. The body_section update is the most delicate operation: parse the existing body into BodySections, replace only the named section, call to_markdown(), then PATCH the issue body. SectionName enum: Description, Acceptance, Design, Notes. Milestone resolution: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/milestones, find by title.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Integration test: update priority → re-fetch confirms new priority
- [ ] Integration test: update body_section 'acceptance' → re-fetch shows section changed, other sections intact
- [ ] Integration test: labels_add → re-fetch shows label added
- [ ] Integration test: labels_remove → re-fetch shows label removed
- [ ] Integration test: update non-existent issue → IssueNotFound
- [ ] Updating only priority does not clear other fields
- [ ] body_section update preserves other sections (roundtrip via BodySections)
- [ ] Tool registered in server tool list
close_reason: QA passed. All checks green, all prior MAJOR findings resolved. Integration tests tracked in unblock-45a.12.

- crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs — Needs NEW methods: update_issue_body(), add_labels(), remove_labels(), list_milestones(), update_issue_milestone() (none of these exist today; only close_issue uses REST PATCH)
- crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs:347-485 — BodySections with from_markdown()/to_markdown() roundtrip already works perfectly; 3 sections: description, design_notes, acceptance_criteria
- crates/unblock-github/src/projects.rs:559-601 — update_field() exists and works for Projects V2 fields (Priority, Status, StoryPoints, DeferUntil)
- crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs:660-710 — get_project_item_id() resolves issue node_id to project item_id (needed for update_field calls)
- crates/unblock-github/src/projects.rs:380-431 — resolve_project_info() gets project ID
- crates/unblock-github/src/client.rs:156-158 — field_ids() returns cached ProjectFieldIds

Approach:
1. Create crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/update.rs with UpdateParams (matching bead spec), UpdateResult (or reuse Issue), and a SectionName enum mapping to BodySections fields. IMPORTANT: Bead says 4 sections (Description, Acceptance, Design, Notes) but BodySections only has 3 fields (description, design_notes, acceptance_criteria). Map SectionName::Description->description, SectionName::Acceptance->acceptance_criteria, SectionName::Design->design_notes. There is NO 'Notes' section — either omit it or discuss with user.
2. Add new REST methods in crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs: (a) update_issue_body(number, body) via PATCH /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/{n} with {body}, (b) add_labels_to_issue(number, labels) via POST /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/{n}/labels, (c) remove_label_from_issue(number, label) via DELETE /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/{n}/labels/{label}, (d) list_milestones() via GET /repos/{o}/{r}/milestones, (e) update_issue_milestone(number, milestone_number) via PATCH /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/{n} with {milestone}
3. Register 'pub mod update;' in tools/mod.rs
4. Add the update handler in server.rs #[tool_router] impl block following the create/close pattern: validate inputs, call execute_write_tool with closure that: (a) fetch_issue to validate existence, (b) update Projects V2 fields if priority/status/story_points/defer_until provided, (c) add/remove labels via new REST methods, (d) resolve and set milestone, (e) parse body into BodySections, update named section, write back via update_issue_body, (f) re-fetch issue to return updated state
5. Add imports in server.rs for update types

Risks:
- BodySections SectionName mismatch: bead says 4 sections but BodySections has 3. SectionName enum should have 3 variants, not 4. Supervisor must reconcile.
- story_points type mismatch: Issue.story_points is Option<i32> but bead spec says Option<f64> and FieldValue::Number takes f64. UpdateParams should accept f64 to match the Projects V2 API, even though Issue stores i32.
- Milestone resolution is a new REST call not yet implemented anywhere (create tool also skips it with a warning). This is the first tool to actually resolve milestone title -> number.
- Labels add/remove are separate API calls — partial failure possible (some labels added, some fail). Use best-effort pattern like other tools.
- Body section update is a read-modify-write cycle — race condition if another actor modifies the body concurrently. Acceptable for single-agent MCP server.
- The execute_write_tool pattern wraps the entire operation in one closure. All mutations (Projects V2 fields, labels, milestone, body) should happen inside the closure before cache rebuild.

Related tests:
- crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs has comprehensive BodySections roundtrip tests (unit + proptest)
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs has execute_write_tool / execute_read_tool unit tests
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/claim.rs has validate_claimable unit tests (pattern to follow for update validation)

Approach:
1. Create crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/comment.rs with CommentParams { id: u64, body: String } and CommentResult { issue_number: u64, comment_url: String } — derive Debug, Deserialize/Serialize, JsonSchema per existing patterns
2. Add 'pub mod comment;' to crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs (alphabetical order, after 'pub mod claim;')
3. Add #[tool] fn comment handler in server.rs #[tool_router] impl:
   a. Validate body is non-empty — return ErrorData INVALID_PARAMS if empty (before any API call)
   b. Validate issue exists: execute_read_tool(state, || client.fetch_issue(id)) — IssueNotFound propagates automatically
   c. Call execute_read_tool(state, || client.add_comment(id, body)) — returns html_url
   d. Return Json(CommentResult { issue_number: id, comment_url })
4. Import CommentParams and CommentResult in server.rs use block
5. Add /// doc comments on all pub types

NOTE on execute_read_tool: The bead says 'use execute_read_tool() pattern' because comments do NOT affect the dependency graph. This is correct — add_comment returns a URL, no cache invalidation needed. Despite being a write to GitHub, it is a 'read tool' from the graph perspective.

NOTE on body validation: Validate body.trim().is_empty() BEFORE the fetch_issue call. This avoids a wasted API call for obviously invalid input — matches the design note about body validation happening before the API call.

title: 1.4.9 depends tool
description:
Implement the 'depends' MCP tool in crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/depends.rs — adds a blocking dependency between two issues, with cross-repo support.

#[tool] macro on struct DependsTool
Input: DependsParams {
  source: u64,        // the issue that will be blocked (must be in the configured repo)
  target: IssueRef,   // the issue that blocks source — accepts local u64 OR owner/repo#number for cross-repo
}
Output: DependsResult { source: u64, target: String, message: String }

Tool logic:
1. Validate source issue exists (fetch_issue → IssueNotFound if absent)
2. Resolve target via resolve_issue_ref(): local number → same repo, owner/repo#number → cross-repo
3. Get current graph from cache
4. Check would_create_cycle(source, target) → return CircularDependency if true
5. Check if relationship already exists → return DuplicateDependency if already present
6. Call add_blocked_by(source, target)
7. Update source issue Projects V2 fields: ReadyState → NotReady, Status → Blocked
8. Rebuild cache (execute_write_tool)
9. Return DependsResult with confirmation message

IssueRef formats:
- Local: plain integer (e.g., 42) — resolves within the configured repo
- Cross-repo: string in owner/repo#number format (e.g., websublime/other-repo#7)
design: Reference: PRD §6.2, ARCH §10.5. The target param was changed from u64 to IssueRef to support cross-repo dependency tracking (plan v1.2.0-draft). IssueRef is Local(u64) or CrossRepo { owner, repo, number } from unblock-core::types. resolve_issue_ref() was implemented in task 1.3.5. The cycle check uses the cached graph (via cache.get_graph()) — cheap pre-validation before making the API call. For cross-repo targets, the graph uses QualifiedId (owner/repo#number) as the node key so duplicate-number issues across repos remain distinct nodes. If graph is stale, rebuild before checking to avoid stale cycle detection.

title: 1.4.8 show tool
description:
Implement the 'show' MCP tool in crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/show.rs — fetches full detail for a single issue.

#[tool] macro on struct ShowTool
Input: ShowParams { id: u64, include_comments: Option<bool> (default true), include_deps: Option<bool> (default true) }
Output: ShowResult {
  issue: Issue (full fields),
  body_sections: BodySections (parsed from issue.body),
  blocking: Vec<IssueSummary> (issues this one blocks),
  blocked_by: Vec<IssueSummary> (issues blocking this one),
  dependency_tree: Option<Vec<(u64, usize)>> (if include_deps=true, up to depth 3),
  comments: Option<Vec<IssueComment>> (if include_comments=true)
}

Tool logic:
1. fetch_issue(id) — returns IssueNotFound if absent
2. Parse body via BodySections::from_markdown(issue.body)
3. If include_deps: get graph from cache, call dependency_tree(id, Both, 3)
4. Return ShowResult

This is a read tool — use execute_read_tool() pattern.
design: Reference: PRD §6.3, ARCH §10.6. The dependency_tree uses the cached DependencyGraph (via cache.get_graph()) — no graph rebuild needed for a read. If cache is empty, skip the tree (return None). The ShowResult provides agents everything they need to understand an issue's full context in one call.

title: 1.4.7 create tool
description:
Implement the 'create' MCP tool in crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/create.rs — creates a new GitHub Issue with all metadata.

#[tool] macro on struct CreateTool
Input: CreateParams {
  title: String,
  issue_type: Option<IssueType> (default Task),
  priority: Option<Priority> (default P2),
  body: Option<String>,
  labels: Option<Vec<String>>,
  milestone: Option<String>,
  blocked_by: Option<Vec<IssueRef>>,  // accepts local number or owner/repo#number for cross-repo
  parent: Option<u64>,
  story_points: Option<f64>,
  defer_until: Option<DateTime<Utc>>
}
Output: Issue (the created issue with all fields)

Tool logic:
1. Build issue body from params (BodySections format if body is None)
2. Create issue via create_issue()
3. Add to project → set fields: Priority, IssueType, StoryPoints, DeferUntil, Status → Backlog, ReadyState → Ready
4. If blocked_by is given: for each IssueRef, call resolve_issue_ref() to get the node ID (handles cross-repo references in owner/repo#number format), then call add_blocked_by() → update ReadyState → NotReady
5. If parent is given: call add_sub_issue(parent, new_number)
6. Rebuild cache (execute_write_tool)
7. Return the created Issue

IssueRef resolution:
- Local: plain u64 number → resolves within the configured repo
- Cross-repo: owner/repo#number → resolves via the target repo's GraphQL endpoint
- resolve_issue_ref() centralises this logic (implemented in 1.3.5)
design: Reference: PRD §6.1, ARCH §10.4. The blocked_by param was changed from Vec<u64> to Vec<IssueRef> to support cross-repo dependency tracking (plan v1.2.0-draft). IssueRef is a type from unblock-core::types — Local(u64) or CrossRepo { owner, repo, number }. resolve_issue_ref() resolves from any repo and was implemented in task 1.3.5. Label creation: if a label in CreateParams.labels does not exist on the repo, create it via REST POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/labels with a generated color. The body field, if provided, is used as-is. If nil, generate a BodySections template with empty sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Integration test: create issue with all params → re-fetch confirms all fields set
- [ ] Integration test: create with blocked_by=[X] (local) → new issue has X in blockedBy, ReadyState = NotReady
- [ ] Integration test: create with blocked_by=[owner/repo#N] (cross-repo) → cross-repo blocking relationship created
- [ ] Integration test: create with parent=Y → new issue appears as sub-issue of Y
- [ ] Integration test: create with no optional params → defaults applied (P2, Task, Backlog)
- [ ] Labels created on repo if they do not exist
- [ ] After create, cache is rebuilt and new issue appears in ready set (if unblocked)
- [ ] IssueRef accepts both local number and owner/repo#number format
- [ ] Tool registered in server tool list
close_reason: QA passed. All acceptance criteria met. 2 deviations tracked as findings (unblock-b6b.76, unblock-b6b.77).

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: Feature implementation — create MCP tool does not exist yet. File crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/create.rs needs to be created from scratch.

Files:
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/create.rs (NEW) — the main tool module to create
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs:34 — must add 'pub mod create;' to register module
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:141 — must add create tool handler in #[tool_router] impl block, import CreateParams/CreateResult
- crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs:104 — create_issue() exists, takes CreateIssueParams, returns Issue
- crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs:306 — add_issue_to_project() is PRIVATE and returns Ok(()), discards the ProjectV2Item ID needed for update_field()
- crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs:421 — add_blocked_by() takes (issue_number, blocked_by_number), both u64 (local repo only)
- crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs:538 — add_sub_issue() takes (parent_number, child_number), both u64
- crates/unblock-github/src/projects.rs:559 — update_field() needs project_id, item_id (ProjectV2Item), field_id, FieldValue
- crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs:267 — BodySections with to_markdown() for generating default body
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs:100 — execute_write_tool() handles cache rebuild

Approach:
1. Define CreateParams struct with JsonSchema (title, issue_type, priority, body, labels, milestone, blocked_by, parent, story_points, defer_until). NOTE: IssueRef type and resolve_issue_ref() do NOT exist in the codebase — the bead says they were in task 1.3.5 but they are absent. blocked_by must use Vec<u64> for local numbers only OR the supervisor must first implement IssueRef in unblock-core::types and resolve_issue_ref() in unblock-github::mutations before the create tool can support cross-repo refs.
2. Define CreateResult struct (mirrors ShowIssue or returns the Issue as JSON).
3. Implement tool logic in create.rs:
   a. If body is None, generate BodySections template via BodySections::default().to_markdown() — this yields empty string. Better: create a BodySections with empty placeholder sections.
   b. Build CreateIssueParams from CreateParams (title, body, labels, milestone as u64 lookup needed, assignees empty).
   c. Call client.create_issue(params) — this handles REST POST + best-effort add_issue_to_project + re-fetch.
   d. For setting project fields (Priority, IssueType, StoryPoints, DeferUntil, Status=Backlog, ReadyState=Ready): PROBLEM — create_issue() already adds issue to project via add_issue_to_project() but discards the ProjectV2Item ID. update_field() requires this item_id. Options: (A) modify add_issue_to_project() to return the item_id, then plumb it through create_issue(), or (B) query for the item_id after creation, or (C) set fields in a separate method that resolves the item_id internally.
   e. If blocked_by is given: for each number, call client.add_blocked_by(new_number, blocker_number). Then update ReadyState -> NotReady.
   f. If parent is given: call client.add_sub_issue(parent, new_number).
   g. Use execute_write_tool() pattern for cache rebuild — but note the tool does multiple mutations (create + set fields + add dependencies). The supervisor should wrap all mutations in the op closure, or call execute_write_tool for the final step only.
4. Register in mod.rs and server.rs.
5. Write integration tests in crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs.

Risks:
- IssueRef and resolve_issue_ref() are MISSING — cross-repo blocked_by acceptance criteria cannot be met without implementing these first. Supervisor must decide: implement IssueRef now (scope creep) or defer cross-repo to a follow-up task and use Vec<u64> for now.
- ProjectV2Item ID gap: add_issue_to_project() is private and discards the item ID. Setting project fields after creation requires either: (A) changing add_issue_to_project() to return String (item_id) and modifying create_issue() to return it alongside Issue, or (B) a separate query to resolve the item_id from the issue's node_id. Option B is simpler but adds an extra API call.
- Milestone: CreateIssueParams.milestone is Option<u64> (numeric ID), but CreateParams.milestone is Option<String> (title). The tool must resolve milestone title to number, which requires a GitHub REST call (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/milestones). No such method exists on GitHubClient yet.
- Label creation: the bead requires creating labels that don't exist. No create_label/ensure_label method exists. Must be added to unblock-github (REST POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/labels).
- story_points type mismatch: Issue.story_points is Option<i32> but CreateParams.story_points is Option<f64> per the bead spec. The FieldValue::Number takes f64, but there's a narrowing concern.

Related tests:
- crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs — existing integration test pattern; create tests go here
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs (mod tests) — unit tests for execute_write_tool pattern
- crates/unblock-github/tests/integration.rs — if mutations are added/changed, test here too

title: 1.4.6 close tool
description:
Implement the 'close' MCP tool in crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/close.rs — closes an issue and triggers the cascade unblock.

#[tool] macro on struct CloseTool
Input: CloseParams { id: u64, reason: Option<String> }
Output: CloseResult { issue_number: u64, unblocked: Vec<u64> }

Tool logic:
1. Validate issue exists and is Open (fetch_issue → IssueNotFound if absent, IssueClosed if already closed)
2. If reason provided: add comment with reason text first
3. Close issue via close_issue(id, reason)
4. Update Projects V2 fields: Status → Done, ReadyState → NotReady
5. Rebuild cache (invalidate → fetch → build → compute)
6. Compute cascade: graph.compute_unblock_cascade(id, &all_issues)
7. For each newly unblocked issue in cascade:
   - Update Projects V2 fields: ReadyState → Ready, Status → Backlog (if not already InProgress)
   - Add comment: '✅ Unblocked by closing #{closed_number}'
8. Return CloseResult { issue_number, unblocked: Vec<u64> of cascade numbers }
design: Reference: PRD §6.1, ARCH §10.3. The cascade step is the most complex part. After rebuilding the cache post-close, we have a fresh graph. Use compute_unblock_cascade() with the fresh issues list to find the cascade. Update each cascaded issue's fields and post comments. These field updates are individual GitHub API calls — do not batch them.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Integration test: close issue A that blocks B → B appears in unblocked list
- [ ] Integration test: close issue A that co-blocks E with D → E NOT in unblocked list
- [ ] Integration test: close already-closed issue → IssueClosed error
- [ ] Integration test: cascade comment appears on each unblocked issue
- [ ] Integration test: cascade issues have ReadyState = Ready after close
- [ ] After close, closed issue no longer in any ready set
- [ ] CloseResult.unblocked contains only issues that were FULLY unblocked
- [ ] Tool registered in server tool list

comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: New feature — implement close MCP tool. No close.rs file exists yet. All dependencies are resolved: compute_unblock_cascade (unblock-core/graph.rs), close_issue + add_comment (unblock-github/mutations.rs), execute_write_tool + rebuild_cache (tools/mod.rs), and Projects V2 field update (unblock-github/projects.rs).

Files:
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/close.rs (NEW) — CloseParams, CloseResult structs
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs:34 — add 'pub mod close;' to module declarations
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:19-33 — add use statements for close types
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:~845 — add #[tool] handler fn close() (follow claim pattern at line 712-834)
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:222 — compute_unblock_cascade(closed_number, all_issues) -> Vec<u64>
- crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs:188 — close_issue(number, reason) -> Result<(), Error>
- crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs:255 — add_comment(number, body) -> Result<String, Error>
- crates/unblock-github/src/projects.rs:559 — update_field(project_id, item_id, field_id, value) -> Result<(), Error>
- crates/unblock-github/src/graphql.rs:201 — fetch_issue(number) -> Result<Issue, Error>
- crates/unblock-core/src/errors.rs:59-63 — IssueClosed domain error variant (status 409)
- crates/unblock-core/src/errors.rs:26-29 — IssueNotFound domain error variant (status 404)

Approach:
1. Create crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/close.rs with CloseParams {id: u64, reason: Option<String>} and CloseResult {issue_number: u64, unblocked: Vec<u64>} (follow create.rs pattern: derive Debug, Deserialize/Serialize, JsonSchema, doc comments)
2. Add 'pub mod close;' to tools/mod.rs at line 34
3. Add tool handler in server.rs following claim tool pattern (lines 712-834):
   a. Fetch issue via client.fetch_issue(id)
   b. Validate: if issue.state == IssueState::Closed, return IssueClosedSnafu error
   c. If reason provided, add_comment handles it (close_issue already does this internally — see mutations.rs:190-192, so just pass reason through)
   d. Call client.close_issue(id, reason) — this handles reason comment + REST PATCH
   e. Update Projects V2 fields on closed issue: Status -> Done, ReadyState -> Not Ready (follow claim pattern for field resolution: field_ids, resolve_project_info, get_project_item_id)
   f. Cache rebuild happens via execute_write_tool wrapper
   g. After rebuild, get fresh graph from cache: state.cache.get_graph().await
   h. Also need fresh issues for cascade — fetch_graph_data again OR use the graph from cache. Note: execute_write_tool already rebuilds cache with fresh graph. Access via state.cache.get_graph()
   i. Call graph.compute_unblock_cascade(id, &fresh_issues) — PROBLEM: cache stores graph but not raw issues. Need to call client.fetch_graph_data() again for the issues list, or refactor. Simpler: call fetch_graph_data after rebuild to get issues, or compute cascade inside the execute_write_tool closure AFTER manual rebuild. Better approach: do NOT use execute_write_tool — instead do manual close + manual rebuild + cascade + field updates + then return. The cascade logic needs post-rebuild data.
   j. REVISED: Use a custom flow instead of execute_write_tool. Close the issue, then manually call rebuild_cache(state), then get graph from cache, call compute_unblock_cascade. For the all_issues param, call client.fetch_graph_data() to get fresh issues (or restructure). Actually, looking at compute_unblock_cascade signature — the _all_issues param is unused (prefixed with underscore, line 222). So pass an empty slice for now.
   k. For each unblocked issue: update ReadyState -> Ready, Status -> Backlog (if not InProgress), add comment with unblock message
   l. Return CloseResult

4. IMPORTANT DETAIL: execute_write_tool does close + rebuild but the cascade logic needs to happen AFTER rebuild. Two options:
   Option A: Put everything inside execute_write_tool closure — close, manual rebuild_cache inside closure, cascade, field updates — but this means double rebuild (closure + execute_write_tool wrapper). Bad.
   Option B: Do NOT use execute_write_tool. Instead: close issue, call rebuild_cache manually, compute cascade, update cascade fields, return. This is cleaner.
   Option C: Split into two phases — use execute_write_tool for the close, then after it returns (cache is rebuilt), compute cascade and do field updates. This avoids double rebuild.
   RECOMMENDED: Option C — call execute_write_tool for close+validate, then after it returns, get graph from cache, compute cascade, update each cascaded issue's fields and post comments.

5. Register tool in server tool list (the #[tool] macro + tool_router! handles this automatically)

Risks:
- compute_unblock_cascade needs all_issues param but it is currently unused (_all_issues). Pass empty slice. If future versions use it, this will need updating.
- Cascade field updates are individual API calls — if one fails, others should still proceed (best-effort, log warnings like claim does)
- Race condition: between close and cascade field updates, another agent could modify the cascaded issues. Acceptable for single-agent MCP use case.
- The execute_write_tool rebuilds cache BEFORE cascade computation, which is correct (we need the fresh graph reflecting the closed state). But the graph was built BEFORE the close was reflected (issue_state snapshot). Actually: fetch_graph_data after close will show the issue as Closed, so the graph will have correct state. The cascade function treats closed_number as closed regardless (line 247), so this is safe either way.
- Double rebuild concern if cascade field updates trigger another rebuild — they should NOT since cascade updates use direct client calls, not execute_write_tool.

Related tests:
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs tests (lines 694-813) — compute_unblock_cascade unit tests (already passing, no changes needed)
- crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs — integration tests for MCP tools (acceptance criteria require new integration tests here for close scenarios)
- crates/unblock-core/src/errors.rs tests — IssueClosed error tests (already passing)

title: 1.4.5 claim tool
description:
Implement the 'claim' MCP tool in crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/claim.rs — atomically claims an issue for an agent.

#[tool] macro on struct ClaimTool
Input: ClaimParams { id: u64, agent: Option<String> }
Output: ClaimResult { issue_number: u64, agent: String, claimed_at: DateTime<Utc> }

Tool logic:
1. Fetch issue via fetch_issue(id) — returns IssueNotFound if not found
2. Validate: issue must be Open → else return IssueClosed
3. Validate: issue must have no active blockers in the current graph → else return IssueBlocked { blocked_by }
4. Validate: issue must not be deferred → else return IssueDeferred
5. Update Projects V2 fields: Status → InProgress, Agent → agent name, ClaimedAt → now, ReadyState → NotReady
6. Add comment: '🤖 Claimed by {agent} at {timestamp}'
7. Rebuild cache (execute_write_tool pattern)
8. Return ClaimResult

Agent name resolution: use ClaimParams.agent if provided, else Config.agent, else 'unknown'.
design: Reference: PRD §6.1, ARCH §10.2. The validation sequence matters — check closed first (cheapest), then blocked (requires graph lookup), then deferred (requires date comparison). The 'atomic' claim is best-effort: GitHub has no transactions. If two agents claim simultaneously, both may succeed — the second write wins. This is acceptable for Phase 1.
acceptance_criteria:

title: 1.4.4 ready tool
description:
Implement the 'ready' MCP tool in crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/ready.rs — the primary tool agents call to find work.

#[tool] macro on struct ReadyTool
Input: ReadyParams {
  limit: Option<usize> (default 10),
  issue_type: Option<IssueType>,
  priority: Option<Priority>,
  milestone: Option<String>,
  agent: Option<String>,
  label: Option<String>,
  include_claimed: Option<bool> (default false)
}
Output: Vec<IssueSummary>

Tool logic:
1. Check cache.is_fresh() — if stale, rebuild (fetch_graph_data → build → compute_ready_set → update cache)
2. Get ready set from cache
3. Filter by params: issue_type, priority, milestone, agent, label
4. Exclude deferred (defer_until > now) unless include_claimed = true
5. If include_claimed = false: exclude issues with Status::InProgress
6. Sort: priority ASC (P0 first), then created_at ASC
7. Return top N (limit)

This is a read tool — use execute_read_tool() pattern.
design: Reference: PRD §6.1, ARCH §10.1. This is the most called tool — performance matters. The cache hit path must not call GitHub API. Cache rebuild is triggered here lazily (not on a timer) to avoid unnecessary API calls. The filter parameters allow orchestrators to query by agent assignment (what is agent X currently working on?).

title: 1.4.3 setup tool
description:
Implement the 'setup' MCP tool in crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/setup.rs.

#[tool] macro on struct SetupTool
Input: SetupParams { project: Option<u32>, dry_run: Option<bool> }
Output: SetupResult { fields_created: Vec<String>, fields_skipped: Vec<String>, project_id: String }

Tool logic:
1. Resolve project (use param if given, else from config/auto-detect)
2. If dry_run == true: query existing fields, report what would be created/skipped, return without mutating
3. Else: call client.setup_fields() which creates the 7 required fields idempotently
4. Return SetupResult with created and skipped field names

This is a write tool — use execute_write_tool() pattern even though setup is idempotent (invalidates cache so fresh data is loaded with new fields).
design: Reference: PRD §6.4, ARCH §10.7. The setup tool is typically the first tool an agent calls on a fresh repo. It is safe to call repeatedly. The dry_run mode is useful for checking whether setup has been run without modifying state. Field names in the result use their canonical names (Status, Priority, IssueType, Agent, StoryPoints, DeferUntil, ReadyState).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Integration test: setup on clean project creates all 7 fields
- [ ] Integration test: setup run twice — second call skips all 7 (fields_created empty)
- [ ] Integration test: dry_run=true reports fields but creates nothing (re-fetch confirms)
- [ ] SetupResult JSON is returned to the MCP client
- [ ] Tool is registered in server tool list
- [ ] All pub types have /// doc comments
close_reason: Closed

INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: New file needed — crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/setup.rs does not exist yet. This is a feature implementation, not a bug fix.

Files:
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs — tools module root; must add 'pub mod setup;' and already has execute_write_tool() helper at line 95

- crates/unblock-github/src/projects.rs:254 — setup_fields(project_id) returns ProjectFieldIds but does NOT distinguish created vs skipped fields
- crates/unblock-github/src/projects.rs:360 — fetch_existing_fields() is private; needed for dry_run mode

- crates/unblock-github/src/client.rs:164 — set_field_ids() caches resolved field IDs after setup

Approach:
1. In unblock-github/src/projects.rs: expose a public constant REQUIRED_FIELD_NAMES: &[&str] = &['Status', 'Priority', 'IssueType', 'Agent', 'StoryPoints', 'DeferUntil', 'ReadyState'] (7 names). Also add a new pub method 'query_setup_status(project_id) -> Result<SetupStatus>' that returns which fields exist and which are missing, reusing fetch_existing_fields internally. This enables dry_run without duplicating logic. Alternatively, modify setup_fields() to return a richer result (SetupReport { field_ids, created, skipped }) instead of plain ProjectFieldIds — this is cleaner because it avoids two round-trips.
2. Create crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/setup.rs with: SetupParams { project: Option<u32>, dry_run: Option<bool> } deriving Deserialize + JsonSchema. SetupResult { fields_created: Vec<String>, fields_skipped: Vec<String>, project_id: String } deriving Serialize + JsonSchema.
3. The tool handler: resolve project via client.resolve_project_info() (uses project param or config). If dry_run: call the query method to check existing fields, compare against 7 required names, return created=[] and skipped=existing names. If not dry_run: call client.setup_fields(project_id), then client.set_field_ids(ids), wrap in execute_write_tool for cache invalidation.
4. Register tool in server.rs: add #[tool(name = 'setup', description = 'Create required Projects V2 fields (idempotent)')] async fn setup(&self, Parameters(params): Parameters<SetupParams>) -> Result<Json<SetupResult>, ErrorData> inside the #[tool_router] impl block.
5. Add 'pub mod setup;' to tools/mod.rs.
6. Doc comments on all pub types.

Risks:
- setup_fields() currently returns ProjectFieldIds without distinguishing created vs skipped. The tool needs this distinction per acceptance criteria. Either (a) change setup_fields return type to include created/skipped lists (breaking API change to unblock-github), or (b) call fetch_existing_fields before and after to diff (extra API call), or (c) add a new wrapper method. Option (a) is cleanest — change return type to SetupReport { field_ids: ProjectFieldIds, created: Vec<String>, skipped: Vec<String> }.
- fetch_existing_fields and REQUIRED_FIELDS are private. For dry_run, either make them pub(crate)/pub or add a dedicated pub method.
- project param in SetupParams is Option<u32> per bead spec but client.project_number() returns Option<u64>. Need u32->u64 conversion (safe, u32 fits in u64).
- The rmcp #[tool] macro requires method to be inside the #[tool_router] impl block on UnblockServer, not on a separate struct. The bead description says '#[tool] macro on struct SetupTool' but rmcp 1.2.0 uses #[tool(...)] attribute on methods inside #[tool_router] impl blocks. Follow rmcp pattern, not the bead's suggested struct-based approach.

Related tests:
- crates/unblock-github/tests/integration.rs — has setup_fields tests at lines 1093, 1199; may need updates if return type changes
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs — has unit tests for execute_write_tool pattern (line 141+)
