title: 1.4.2 Tool execution pattern — shared helper
description:
Implement the shared tool execution helper in crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs (or tools/mod.rs). All 9 MCP tool handlers must use this pattern — no tool should implement its own rebuild/invalidate logic.

The helper function signature:
async fn execute_write_tool<F, Fut, R>(state: &ServerState, op: F) -> Result<R, McpError>
where F: FnOnce() -> Fut, Fut: Future<Output = Result<R, Error>>

Write tool flow (for tools that mutate state):
1. Call op() — the actual GitHub mutation
2. On success: call cache.invalidate()
3. Fetch fresh graph data: client.fetch_graph_data()
4. Build new DependencyGraph: DependencyGraph::build(issues, edges)
5. Compute new ready set: graph.compute_ready_set(&issues)
6. Update cache: cache.update(ready_set, graph)
7. Return the op() result

Read tool flow (for tools that only read):
async fn execute_read_tool<F, Fut, R>(state: &ServerState, op: F) -> Result<R, McpError>
- Just calls op(), maps Error to McpError

Error mapping: From<unblock_github::Error> for McpError must be implemented here.
design: Reference: ARCH §9.3. The key invariant: the cache is always consistent after a write tool completes (either it was updated or it was left as-is due to failure). Do not hold the cache write lock across the GitHub API call — invalidate after success, then rebuild.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] execute_write_tool compiles and is used by at least one tool (can stub the rest)
- [ ] Unit test: mock op() succeeds → cache is invalidated and rebuilt
- [ ] Unit test: mock op() fails → cache is NOT invalidated
- [ ] execute_read_tool compiles and maps errors correctly
- [ ] From<unblock_github::Error> for McpError maps all 8 error variants
- [ ] All pub functions have /// doc comments
close_reason: Closed

Approach:
1. In errors.rs, add impl From<unblock_github::errors::Error> for rmcp::ErrorData. Map status_code() to appropriate ErrorCode constants: 400/404/409/412/422 -> INVALID_PARAMS, 429/503 -> INTERNAL_ERROR, 500 -> INTERNAL_ERROR. Use error Display as message. NOTE: The bead says 'McpError' but rmcp 1.2.0 uses ErrorData — the supervisor should use ErrorData.
2. In tools/mod.rs, implement execute_read_tool<F, Fut, R>(state: &ServerState, op: F) -> Result<R, ErrorData> where F: FnOnce() -> Fut, Fut: Future<Output = Result<R, unblock_github::Error>>. Simply calls op().await and maps error via From.
3. In tools/mod.rs, implement execute_write_tool<F, Fut, R>(state: &ServerState, op: F) -> Result<R, ErrorData>. Recommend using a trait-based approach or making the rebuild step a separate testable function.

Options: (a) extract a trait in unblock-github (scope creep), (b) accept integration-test-only coverage for the rebuild path, (c) make execute_write_tool accept a rebuild closure for testability. title: 1.3.7 Infrastructure errors — GitHub error enum
description:
Implement the infrastructure-level Error enum in crates/unblock-github/src/errors.rs for all GitHub API failure modes.

Error enum variants (snafu derive):
- Domain { source: DomainError } — wraps domain errors (IssueNotFound, etc.)
- GitHubApi { status: u16, message: String } — non-2xx REST response
- GitHubGraphQL { errors: Vec<String> } — GraphQL errors array in response
- GitHubUnavailable { source: reqwest::Error } — network/connection failure
- RateLimited { reset_at: chrono::DateTime<Utc> } — 429 with X-RateLimit-Reset header
- CircuitBreakerOpen { since: std::time::Instant } — circuit breaker tripped (for Phase 2)
- ProjectNotConfigured — no project ID available and auto-detect failed
- GitRemote { message: String } — failed to read/parse git remote URL

From<Error> for McpError — conversion that maps each variant to an MCP error code and message.
fn status_code(&self) -> u16 on Error — HTTP status for each variant.
design: Reference: ARCH §13.2. The From<Error> for McpError conversion will live in unblock-mcp (not here) to avoid circular dependency. In this task, implement the status_code() and Display traits. CircuitBreakerOpen is a stub variant — full circuit breaker implementation is Phase 2. The Domain wrapper variant allows bubbling DomainError through the GitHub layer cleanly.

- [ ] All pub types have /// doc comments

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: The Error enum exists with all 8 variants but is incomplete per the bead spec. Four gaps remain:
(1) GitHubApi is missing the 'status: u16' field — bead spec says 'status: u16, message: String' but code only has 'message: String'
(2) RateLimited is a unit variant — bead spec says it needs 'reset_at: chrono::DateTime<Utc>' and Display must include reset_at
(3) CircuitBreakerOpen is a unit variant — bead spec says it needs 'since: std::time::Instant'
(4) No status_code() method on Error — bead requires 'fn status_code(&self) -> u16' (parallel to DomainError::status_code())

Files:
- crates/unblock-github/src/errors.rs:23-71 — the Error enum, needs field additions and status_code() impl
- crates/unblock-core/src/errors.rs:114-138 — DomainError::status_code() pattern to follow for consistency
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/errors.rs:1-5 — stub file where From<Error> for McpError will eventually live (NOT in this bead per design notes)
- docs/unblock-architecture-github.md:1360-1399 — arch spec section 13.2, the contract for this enum

Approach:
1. Add 'status: u16' field to GitHubApi variant. Update Display to include status code: 'GitHub API error ({status}): {message}'
2. Add 'reset_at: chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>' field to RateLimited. Update Display to include reset_at per AC
3. Add 'since: std::time::Instant' field to CircuitBreakerOpen. Note: Instant is not Display-friendly, consider using elapsed() or debug format
4. Add 'impl Error { pub fn status_code(&self) -> u16 }' following DomainError pattern. Mapping: Domain delegates to source.status_code(), GitHubApi returns its status field, GitHubGraphQL->422, GitHubUnavailable->503, RateLimited->429, CircuitBreakerOpen->503, ProjectNotConfigured->412, GitRemote->500
5. Update all tests: GitHubApi tests need status field, RateLimited test needs reset_at, CircuitBreakerOpen test needs since, add status_code() tests for every variant
6. Do NOT implement From<Error> for McpError in this crate — that goes in unblock-mcp per design notes (avoids circular dep)

Risks:
- Adding 'since: std::time::Instant' means CircuitBreakerOpen cannot derive Clone, PartialEq, or Serialize (Instant has no serialization). This is fine since Error already cannot derive these (reqwest::Error lacks them too). But if someone later needs to serialize errors, Instant will be a problem — consider making it Duration or u64 millis instead. Check with user.
- The status_code() mapping is not explicitly in the arch doc for infrastructure errors (only for domain errors). The values above are inferred from HTTP semantics. Confirm mapping is correct.
- chrono is already a workspace dep in unblock-github/Cargo.toml so no new deps needed.

Related tests:
- crates/unblock-github/src/errors.rs:74-186 — existing tests, all need updates for new fields + new status_code() tests needed

title: 1.3.6 Projects V2 fields — setup and update
description:
Implement Projects V2 field management in crates/unblock-github/src/projects.rs.

async fn resolve_project(&self) -> Result<ProjectInfo, Error>
- Queries the linked GitHub Projects V2 for the repo
- Returns ProjectInfo { id: String (global node ID), number: u32 }

async fn setup_fields(&self, project_id: &str) -> Result<ProjectFieldIds, Error>
- Creates the 7 required custom fields if they do not exist (idempotent):
  1. Status — single select: Backlog, In Progress, Done, Blocked, Deferred
  2. Priority — single select: P0, P1, P2, P3, P4
  3. IssueType — single select: Task, Bug, Feature, Epic, Chore
  4. Agent — text field
  5. StoryPoints — number field
  6. DeferUntil — date field
  7. ReadyState — single select: Ready, Not Ready
- Checks existing fields first, only creates missing ones
- Returns ProjectFieldIds (map of field name → field ID)

async fn update_field(&self, item_id: &str, field_id: &str, value: FieldValue) -> Result<(), Error>
- GraphQL mutation: updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue
- FieldValue enum: Text(String), Number(f64), Date(chrono::NaiveDate), SingleSelectOption(String)
design: Reference: ARCH §8.4. GraphQL mutations for Projects V2: createProjectV2Field, updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue. Field existence check via projectV2 { fields { nodes { name } } } query. Cache the ProjectFieldIds in GitHubClient state after first resolution to avoid repeated lookups on every update_field call.

Approach:
1. Define new types in projects.rs: ProjectInfo { id: String, number: u32 }, ProjectFieldIds (with FieldMeta for single-select fields per ARCH 8.1), FieldMeta { field_id: String, options: HashMap<String,String> }, FieldValue enum { Text(String), Number(f64), Date(chrono::NaiveDate), SingleSelectOption(String) }.
2. Add to GitHubClient struct: project_id: Option<String>, field_ids: Option<ProjectFieldIds>. Since caching field_ids requires interior mutability (&self methods), use tokio::sync::OnceCell<ProjectFieldIds> or tokio::sync::RwLock<Option<ProjectFieldIds>>. OnceCell is cleaner since setup_fields is called once. But update bead says setup_fields returns Result<ProjectFieldIds> and caches — so tokio::sync::OnceCell wont work since setup_fields creates fields first. Use tokio::sync::Mutex<Option<ProjectFieldIds>> or simply return ProjectFieldIds and let caller set it. Simplest: make field_ids a tokio::sync::OnceCell and have setup_fields call get_or_init.
3. Implement resolve_project(&self) -> Result<ProjectInfo, Error>: GraphQL query projectV2(number: N) { id } on repository. Requires project_number to be set (return ProjectNotConfigured if None). Note: mutations.rs:306-328 already has this exact query inline — factor out or duplicate in projects.rs.
4. Implement setup_fields(&self, project_id: &str) -> Result<ProjectFieldIds, Error>: First query existing fields via projectV2 { fields(first:50) { nodes { ... on ProjectV2SingleSelectField { id name options { id name } } ... on ProjectV2Field { id name dataType } } } }. Then for each of the 7 required fields, if missing, create via createProjectV2Field mutation. For single-select fields also create options. Return ProjectFieldIds with all resolved IDs. Cache in self.field_ids.
5. Implement update_field(&self, item_id: &str, field_id: &str, value: FieldValue) -> Result<(), Error>: GraphQL mutation updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue with appropriate value input based on FieldValue variant.
6. Add integration tests in tests/integration.rs following existing patterns.
7. Update GitHubClient struct, new(), new_for_test(), and make_test_client() to include new fields.

IMPORTANT — Field names and options discrepancy:
- Bead description says Status options: Backlog, In Progress, Done, Blocked, Deferred
- ARCH section 7.1 says Status options: open, in_progress, blocked, deferred, closed
- Bead also says ReadyState options: Ready, Not Ready (only 2)
- ARCH 7.1 says Ready State: ready, blocked, not_ready, closed (4 options)
- The bead description is the contract for THIS task. Follow the bead: Status={Backlog, In Progress, Done, Blocked, Deferred}, Priority={P0-P4}, IssueType={Task,Bug,Feature,Epic,Chore}, ReadyState={Ready, Not Ready}

Risks:
- Interior mutability: GitHubClient is currently a plain struct with no async sync primitives. Adding tokio::sync::OnceCell or Mutex for field_ids cache changes the struct — may affect Debug derive (OnceCell does impl Debug). Check tokio version supports OnceCell.

- createProjectV2Field mutation for single-select fields requires creating options separately via updateProjectV2Field or the options argument — verify the exact GraphQL schema.
- Integration tests will require UNBLOCK_PROJECT env var to be set (real project number).
- The 7 fields per the bead do NOT include 'Claimed At' but ARCH 7.1 does. Bead lists: Status, Priority, IssueType, Agent, StoryPoints, DeferUntil, ReadyState. Follow the bead (7 fields, no ClaimedAt).

title: 1.3.5 Mutations — blocking relationships and sub-issues
description:
Implement blocking relationship mutations in crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs using GitHub GraphQL API.

async fn add_blocked_by(&self, issue_number: u64, blocked_by_number: u64) -> Result<(), Error>
- GraphQL mutation: addBlockedBy(issueId, blockedById)
- First resolves both issue numbers to global node IDs via GraphQL
- Returns CircularDependency if adding would create a cycle (check first via would_create_cycle)
- Returns DuplicateDependency if relationship already exists

async fn remove_blocked_by(&self, issue_number: u64, blocked_by_number: u64) -> Result<(), Error>
- GraphQL mutation: removeBlockedBy(issueId, blockedById)
- Returns IssueNotFound if either issue does not exist

async fn add_sub_issue(&self, parent_number: u64, child_number: u64) -> Result<(), Error>
- GraphQL mutation using the sub_issues preview feature
- Requires header: GraphQL-Features: sub_issues
- Resolves both numbers to node IDs, then calls addSubIssue mutation
design: Reference: ARCH §8.3. GitHub blocking relationships use GraphQL mutations addBlockedBy/removeBlockedBy with global node IDs (not numbers). Node ID resolution: repository { issue(number: N) { id } }. The sub_issues feature is in preview as of March 2026 — the header must be included. Cycle checking is done in the graph layer (1.2.6) before calling this mutation.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Integration test: add_blocked_by(A, B) — re-fetch A shows B in blockedBy
- [ ] Integration test: remove_blocked_by(A, B) — re-fetch A shows B no longer in blockedBy
- [ ] Integration test: add_sub_issue(parent, child) — re-fetch parent shows child in subIssues
- [ ] add_blocked_by with pre-existing relationship returns DuplicateDependency
- [ ] All mutations return IssueNotFound for non-existent issue numbers
- [ ] GraphQL-Features: sub_issues header included in add_sub_issue request
- [ ] All pub methods have /// doc comments
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: Feature implementation — three new pub async methods needed in mutations.rs on GitHubClient: add_blocked_by, remove_blocked_by, add_sub_issue. Each accepts issue numbers (u64), resolves them to GraphQL node IDs, then calls the corresponding GraphQL mutation.

Files:
- crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs — primary implementation file. Currently has create_issue, close_issue, add_comment (REST), and add_issue_to_project (GraphQL). New methods go here as impl GitHubClient methods.
- crates/unblock-github/src/graphql.rs:325 — the pub(crate) graphql() method that sends GraphQL requests. Takes query string + serde_json::Value variables. Handles rate-limit, non-2xx, and GraphQL-level errors. New mutations will call this.
- crates/unblock-github/src/errors.rs — Error enum with Domain variant wrapping DomainError via context(false). CircularDependency, DuplicateDependency, IssueNotFound are in unblock_core::errors::DomainError and auto-convert via .into().
- crates/unblock-core/src/errors.rs — DomainError has IssueNotFound{number}, CircularDependency{source,target}, DuplicateDependency{source,target} with snafu selectors.
- crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs:39 — Issue struct has node_id: String field (GraphQL node ID).
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:274 — would_create_cycle(source, target) -> bool exists in DependencyGraph for pre-mutation cycle checking. NOTE: cycle check is done at the MCP tool layer (bead 1.2.6/1.4.9), NOT in this github layer. The bead description mentions it but ARCH 10.5 shows it happens at the tool handler level before calling addBlockedBy.
- crates/unblock-github/tests/integration.rs — existing integration tests follow pattern: skip if no GITHUB_TOKEN, create test issue, use CloseIssueGuard for cleanup, call mutation, re-fetch and assert. New tests go here.
- docs/unblock-architecture-github.md:655-695 — ARCH 8.3 shows the three methods. Note: arch doc signatures take &str node IDs, but bead description says methods take u64 issue numbers and resolve internally. Follow the bead (u64 numbers).

Approach:
1. Add a private helper resolve_node_id(&self, number: u64) -> Result<String, Error> that runs: query { repository(owner, name, issue(number: N) { id } } } and returns the node ID string. Returns IssueNotFound if the issue does not exist (null response).
2. Implement add_blocked_by(&self, issue_number: u64, blocked_by_number: u64) -> Result<(), Error>:
   - Call resolve_node_id for both numbers
   - Run GraphQL mutation: mutation { addBlockedBy(issueId: , blockedById: ) { blockedByItem { id } } }
   - NOTE: The actual GitHub GraphQL mutation name is NOT confirmed in the GitHub docs as of March 2026. The architecture doc uses addBlockedBy. If the mutation name differs, the GraphQL error will be clear.
   - For DuplicateDependency detection: check if GitHub returns an error when the relationship already exists, or pre-check by fetching the issue and checking trackedInIssues/trackedByIssues.
3. Implement remove_blocked_by(&self, issue_number: u64, blocked_by_number: u64) -> Result<(), Error>:
   - Call resolve_node_id for both numbers
   - Run GraphQL mutation: mutation { removeBlockedBy(issueId: , blockedById: ) { ... } }
   - Return IssueNotFound if either issue does not exist
4. Implement add_sub_issue(&self, parent_number: u64, child_number: u64) -> Result<(), Error>:

title: 1.3.4 Mutations — create, close, comment
description:
Implement write mutations in crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs using GitHub REST API.

async fn create_issue(&self, params: CreateIssueParams) -> Result<Issue, Error>
- REST POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues
- Params: title (required), body, labels, milestone, assignees
- Returns the created issue (re-fetched via fetch_issue for full field set)
- After creation, add to project via Projects V2 mutation (if project is configured)

async fn close_issue(&self, number: u64, reason: Option<String>) -> Result<(), Error>
- REST PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number} with state: 'closed'
- If reason is provided: add a comment first via add_comment()
- Returns IssueNotFound if number does not exist

async fn add_comment(&self, number: u64, body: String) -> Result<String, Error>
- REST POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}/comments
- Returns the URL of the created comment
- Returns IssueNotFound if issue does not exist
design: Reference: ARCH §8.3. Use REST not GraphQL for these mutations — GitHub REST is simpler for CRUD. POST /issues uses JSON body with title, body, labels (array), milestone (number), assignees (array). PATCH /issues/{n} with { state: 'closed', state_reason: 'completed' }. Integration tests must clean up after themselves (close/delete created issues).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Integration test: create_issue() creates issue, returns with correct fields
- [ ] Integration test: close_issue() closes issue, re-fetch confirms state is closed
- [ ] Integration test: add_comment() posts comment, re-fetch confirms it appears
- [ ] Integration test: close_issue() with reason adds comment before closing
- [ ] create_issue() adds issue to project if UNBLOCK_PROJECT is configured
- [ ] All mutations return IssueNotFound for non-existent issue numbers
- [ ] All pub methods have /// doc comments
close_reason: Closed

INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: mutations.rs is a stub file (10 lines, module-level docs only, no impl). Three REST mutation methods need to be implemented on GitHubClient: create_issue, close_issue, add_comment. The bead description specifies CreateIssueParams as input struct (does not exist yet — must be defined). Architecture doc §8.3 defines signatures slightly differently (title/body/labels/milestone/issue_type as separate params rather than a params struct) — bead description takes precedence as it is the task spec.

Files:
- crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs:1-10 — STUB, target file for all implementation
- crates/unblock-github/src/client.rs:23-36 — GitHubClient struct (http, api_base_url, owner, repo, project_number fields)
- crates/unblock-github/src/client.rs:146-152 — rest_url() helper builds REST URLs from path suffix
- crates/unblock-github/src/client.rs:115-119 — http() accessor returns reqwest::Client reference
- crates/unblock-github/src/graphql.rs:325-387 — graphql() method shows pattern: send request, handle 429 rate limit, handle non-2xx, parse JSON. REST mutations need analogous error handling but for REST endpoints
- crates/unblock-github/src/graphql.rs:186-219 — fetch_issue() shows pattern for IssueNotFound: returns DomainError via IssueNotFoundSnafu
- crates/unblock-github/src/graphql.rs:390-401 — parse_rate_limit_reset() is private to graphql.rs, needs to be made pub(crate) or duplicated for REST use
- crates/unblock-github/src/errors.rs:34-41 — GitHubApi variant for non-2xx REST responses
- crates/unblock-github/src/errors.rs:56-68 — RateLimited variant with reset_at field
- crates/unblock-core/src/errors.rs:25-29 — IssueNotFound domain error (number: u64), status_code 404
- crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs:34-84 — Issue struct with all fields (number, node_id, title, body, state, labels, milestone, assignees, comments, url, etc.)
- crates/unblock-github/src/lib.rs:20 — mutations module already declared as pub mod
- crates/unblock-github/tests/integration.rs — existing integration tests for fetch_issue/fetch_graph_data, new mutation tests go here
- docs/unblock-architecture-github.md:655-695 — §8.3 architecture reference for mutation signatures

Approach:
1. Define CreateIssueParams struct in mutations.rs: title (String, required), body (Option<String>), labels (Vec<String>), milestone (Option<u64>), assignees (Vec<String>). Derive Debug, Clone, and add doc comments.
2. Make parse_rate_limit_reset in graphql.rs pub(crate) so mutations.rs can reuse it for REST 429 handling, OR extract a shared rest_error_handling helper. Recommended: create a pub(crate) helper method on GitHubClient (e.g., handle_rest_response) that handles 429/non-2xx/parse-json the same way graphql() does.
3. Implement create_issue(&self, params: CreateIssueParams) -> Result<Issue, Error>:
   - POST to rest_url(format!('/repos/{}/{}/issues', self.owner(), self.repo()))
   - JSON body: { title, body, labels, milestone, assignees }
   - Handle 429, non-2xx errors
   - After creation, re-fetch via self.fetch_issue(number) to get full field set (per bead spec)
   - If self.project_number().is_some(), add to project via GraphQL addProjectV2ItemById mutation
4. Implement close_issue(&self, number: u64, reason: Option<String>) -> Result<(), Error>:
   - If reason is Some, call self.add_comment(number, reason) first
   - PATCH to rest_url(format!('/repos/{}/{}/issues/{}', self.owner(), self.repo(), number))
   - JSON body: { state: 'closed', state_reason: 'completed' }
   - Handle 404 -> IssueNotFound, 429, other non-2xx
5. Implement add_comment(&self, number: u64, body: String) -> Result<String, Error>:
   - POST to rest_url(format!('/repos/{}/{}/issues/{}/comments', self.owner(), self.repo(), number))
   - JSON body: { body }
   - Parse response for html_url field, return it
   - Handle 404 -> IssueNotFound, 429, other non-2xx
6. Add integration tests in tests/integration.rs: create_issue creates and returns correct fields, close_issue closes (re-fetch confirms), add_comment returns URL, close_issue with reason adds comment first, IssueNotFound for nonexistent numbers. Tests must clean up (close created issues).
7. Add doc comments on all pub items.

Risks:
- parse_rate_limit_reset is private to graphql.rs — must be made pub(crate) or refactored into a shared location before mutations can handle 429 properly
- REST 404 for close_issue/add_comment does NOT return the same shape as GraphQL null — need to check status code 404 and map to IssueNotFoundSnafu manually
- create_issue + addProjectV2Item is a two-step operation with no rollback — if addProjectV2Item fails, the issue exists but is not in the project. The bead says 'if project is configured' so this should be best-effort with a warning log, not a hard failure.
- Integration tests create real GitHub issues — must close them in cleanup even if assertions fail (use a cleanup guard or ensure close runs in a finally-like pattern)
- Architecture doc §8.3 mentions reopen_issue and update_issue — these are NOT in this bead's scope (bead only covers create, close, comment). Do not implement them.
- The bead description says create_issue takes CreateIssueParams but arch doc §8.3 uses separate params — follow the bead description (params struct)

Related tests:
- crates/unblock-github/tests/integration.rs — add new mutation tests here following existing pattern (has_github_token guard, test_config helper)
- No unit tests needed for mutations themselves (they hit real API), but the CreateIssueParams struct could have unit tests for Default/validation

title: 1.3.2 fetch_graph_data — paginated GraphQL
description:
Implement fetch_graph_data() on GitHubClient in crates/unblock-github/src/graphql.rs — the primary data fetch that builds the full dependency graph.

async fn fetch_graph_data(&self) -> Result<(Vec<Issue>, Vec<BlockingEdge>), Error>

GraphQL query must fetch for all open issues (paginated, 100 per page):
- Issue fields: number, title, body, state, labels, milestone, assignees, createdAt, updatedAt, closedAt
- Blocking relationships: blockedBy { nodes { number } }, blocking { nodes { number } }
- Projects V2 fieldValues: Status, Priority, IssueType, Agent, StoryPoints, DeferUntil, ReadyState, ClaimedAt

Pagination: use GraphQL cursor pagination (after: , pageInfo.endCursor, hasNextPage). Loop until hasNextPage is false.

Mapping:
- Each issue → Issue struct (domain type)
- Each blockedBy edge → BlockingEdge { source: issue.number, target: blocker.number }
- Projects V2 field values mapped to enum variants
design: Reference: ARCH §8.2. GraphQL query is defined as a const &str in graphql.rs. Use serde_json for response deserialization into intermediate structs, then map to domain types. The Projects V2 fieldValues node uses a union type — handle all variants: text, number, singleSelect, date.
acceptance_criteria:

- [ ] Pagination: test with repo that has > 100 issues — all pages fetched
- [ ] All Projects V2 fields mapped: Status, Priority, IssueType, Agent, StoryPoints, DeferUntil, ReadyState
- [ ] BlockingEdge direction is correct: source blocked by target

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: fetch_graph_data() is not yet implemented in graphql.rs. The method signature is defined in ARCH §8.2 as: pub async fn fetch_graph_data(&self) -> Result<(Vec<Issue>, Vec<BlockingEdge>), Error>. The file already has fetch_issue(), the graphql() helper, and all parse_* helpers ready — this is a feature addition, not a bug fix.

Files:
- crates/unblock-github/src/graphql.rs:1-969 — PRIMARY. Add FETCH_GRAPH_DATA_QUERY const and fetch_graph_data() method on GitHubClient. All parse helpers (parse_issue, extract_field_values, parse_status_field, etc.) already exist and are reusable. The graphql() low-level method (line 158) handles auth, rate limiting, and error checking.
- crates/unblock-github/src/client.rs:23-36 — GitHubClient struct. Has owner(), repo(), project_number() accessors needed for GraphQL variables. project_number is Option<u64> — the query must handle the case where no project is configured (skip Projects V2 fields).
- crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs:29-84 — Issue struct (target type). Note: comments, blocked_by, blocking, parent, sub_issues are documented as 'populated by fetch_issue() only' — fetch_graph_data should leave these as empty Vec/None.
- crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs:202-212 — BlockingEdge struct. source=blocked issue, target=blocker issue. Direction: source blocked BY target.
- crates/unblock-github/src/errors.rs:1-100 — Error enum. All needed variants exist (GitHubGraphQL, GitHubApi, RateLimited, GitHubUnavailable).
- crates/unblock-github/tests/integration.rs — Add integration tests here.

Approach:
1. Define FETCH_GRAPH_DATA_QUERY const in graphql.rs. Use repository.issues(first:100, states:OPEN, after:) with cursor pagination. Include: number, id, title, body, state, url, createdAt, updatedAt, labels, milestone, assignees, trackedByIssues (blockedBy), trackedInIssues (blocking), projectItems with fieldValues (same union fragments as FETCH_ISSUE_QUERY). Do NOT include comments, parent, or subIssues — per types.rs docs these are fetch_issue()-only.
2. Implement fetch_graph_data() on GitHubClient in the existing impl block. Loop: call graphql() with cursor=null initially, parse each page of issues using existing parse_issue() helper, extract BlockingEdge from trackedByIssues nodes (source=issue.number, target=blocker.number), advance cursor via pageInfo.endCursor until hasNextPage is false.
3. The parse_issue() helper already handles all field extraction including Projects V2 fields. It returns Issue with blocked_by/blocking/comments/parent/sub_issues populated if present in JSON, or empty if absent — so the query simply omits those fields it does not need, and parse_issue will default them.
4. Actually, IMPORTANT: parse_issue() reads 'trackedBy' and 'trackedInIssues' for blocked_by/blocking (lines 260-261). For fetch_graph_data we DO need trackedByIssues to build BlockingEdge, but the Issue.blocked_by/blocking fields should stay empty per the types.rs contract. Two options: (a) use a separate parse function for graph data that skips those fields, or (b) parse_issue works fine since it populates them from JSON — just don't include trackedInIssues in the query (we only need trackedByIssues for edges), and clear blocked_by/blocking on the resulting Issue. Recommend option (a): create a lightweight parse_graph_issue() that reuses helpers but skips comments/parent/subIssues/blockedBy/blocking on the Issue, and separately extracts BlockingEdge from the trackedByIssues nodes.
5. Add unit tests: test pagination loop with mocked multi-page JSON, test BlockingEdge extraction direction, test empty repo returns empty vecs.
6. Add integration test in tests/integration.rs: fetch_graph_data() returns non-empty issues from real repo (gated on GITHUB_TOKEN).

Risks:
- GitHub API field names: trackedByIssues vs trackedInIssues naming is counterintuitive. trackedByIssues = 'issues that track this one' = blockers. Verify with FETCH_ISSUE_QUERY which already uses these aliases correctly (line 55-68: trackedInIssues maps to blocking, trackedBy: trackedByIssues maps to blocked_by).
- Pagination cursor type: GraphQL expects String for after param — pass null on first request, then endCursor string on subsequent.
- Large repos: 100 issues per page is the GraphQL max. Pagination loop must not have off-by-one (check hasNextPage BEFORE advancing).
- Projects V2 fields: if project_number is None, projectItems may return empty — this is fine, extract_field_values handles it gracefully (line 428-434).
- The query should include the pageInfo { endCursor hasNextPage } on the issues connection.

Related tests:
- crates/unblock-github/src/graphql.rs (mod tests, line 529-969) — existing unit tests for parse helpers, all reusable
- crates/unblock-github/tests/integration.rs — add fetch_graph_data integration test
- crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs (mod tests) — BlockingEdge struct tests if needed

Using parse_issue() would populate those fields from trackedBy JSON data, violating the contract. A separate function makes the distinction explicit and avoids accidental data leakage.

title: 1.3.1 GitHub client bootstrap
description:
Implement GitHubClient in crates/unblock-github/src/client.rs — the central struct for all GitHub API communication.

GitHubClient::new(config: &Config) -> Result<Self, Error>:
- Builds a reqwest::Client with Authorization: Bearer {token} header
- Sets User-Agent: unblock-mcp/{version}
- Sets Accept: application/vnd.github+json and X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28 headers
- Calls resolve_repo() to determine owner/repo
- Calls resolve_project() to determine project number

fn resolve_repo(config: &Config) -> Result<(String, String), Error>:
- If UNBLOCK_REPO is set: parse 'owner/repo' format
- Otherwise: read git remote URL from .git/config in cwd, parse GitHub URL
- Supported formats: https://github.com/owner/repo.git, git@github.com:owner/repo.git

fn resolve_project(client, owner, repo, config: &Config) -> Result<Option<u32>, Error>:
- If UNBLOCK_PROJECT is set: use it directly
- Otherwise: query GitHub Projects V2 API to find first linked project

fn parse_github_url(url: &str) -> Result<(String, String), Error> — unit-testable URL parser
design: Reference: ARCH §8.1. The reqwest::Client should be built with connection pooling defaults. For git remote parsing, read .git/config directly (no git CLI invocation). Integration tests are gated by #[cfg(feature = 'integration')] or require GITHUB_TOKEN env var to be set.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] parse_github_url() handles https://github.com/owner/repo.git
- [ ] parse_github_url() handles git@github.com:owner/repo.git
- [ ] parse_github_url() handles URLs without .git suffix
- [ ] parse_github_url() returns Error for non-GitHub URLs
- [ ] Unit test for each parse_github_url() case (no network needed)
- [ ] UNBLOCK_REPO override bypasses git remote detection
- [ ] Integration test: GitHubClient::new() connects to real repo (requires GITHUB_TOKEN in env)
- [ ] All pub methods have /// doc comments
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: Feature implementation — client.rs is scaffolded with only a module-level doc comment (6 lines). The GitHubClient struct, its constructor, resolve_repo(), resolve_project(), parse_github_url(), rest_url(), and graphql_url() all need to be implemented from scratch.

Files:
- crates/unblock-github/src/client.rs:1-6 — Target file. Only has module doc comment. All code goes here.
- crates/unblock-core/src/config.rs:41-80 — Config struct with fields: token (String), api_base_url (String), repo (Option<String> in owner/repo format), project_number (Option<u64>), agent, cache_ttl, log_level, otel_endpoint.
- crates/unblock-github/src/errors.rs:1-7 — Only has module doc comment. Error enum needs to be implemented per ARCH §13 (variants: Domain, GitHubApi, GitHubGraphQL, GitHubUnavailable, RateLimited, CircuitBreakerOpen, ProjectNotConfigured, GitRemote).
- crates/unblock-github/src/lib.rs:1-27 — Module declarations already exist for client, graphql, mutations, projects, errors.
- crates/unblock-github/Cargo.toml:1-21 — Dependencies already declared: unblock-core, serde, serde_json, tokio, reqwest (0.12 with json feature), tracing, chrono, snafu.
- docs/unblock-architecture-github.md:544-611 — ARCH §8.1 defines GitHubClient struct shape, fields, and method signatures.
- docs/unblock-architecture-github.md:1345-1376 — ARCH §13 defines Error enum for unblock-github with 8 variants.

Approach:
1. Implement Error enum in errors.rs per ARCH §13 (Domain, GitHubApi, GitHubGraphQL, GitHubUnavailable, RateLimited, CircuitBreakerOpen, ProjectNotConfigured, GitRemote). Include From<Error> for McpError stub or skip MCP conversion for now (unblock-mcp dep).
2. Implement GitHubClient struct in client.rs with fields: http (reqwest::Client), token (String), api_base_url (String), owner (String), repo (String), project_number (Option<u64>), project_id (Option<String>), field_ids (Option<ProjectFieldIds>).
3. Implement parse_github_url(url: &str) -> Result<(String, String), Error> — pure function, handles https://github.com/owner/repo.git, git@github.com:owner/repo.git, and URLs without .git suffix. Returns error for non-GitHub URLs.
4. Implement resolve_repo(config: &Config) -> Result<(String, String), Error> — if config.repo is Some, split on '/' and return. Otherwise read .git/config from cwd, find remote origin URL, call parse_github_url(). Use std::fs::read_to_string, NOT git CLI.
5. Implement resolve_project() as async — if config.project_number is Some, use it directly. Otherwise placeholder for GraphQL query (full impl is bead unblock-467.6). For this bead, the method can return Ok(config.project_number) since the GraphQL query is a later task.
6. Implement GitHubClient::new(config: &Config) -> Result<Self, Error> as async — build reqwest::Client with default headers (Authorization: Bearer {token}, User-Agent: unblock-mcp/{version}, Accept: application/vnd.github+json, X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28), call resolve_repo(), call resolve_project().
7. Implement rest_url(&self, path: &str) -> String and graphql_url(&self) -> String helper methods per ARCH §8.1.
8. Write unit tests for parse_github_url() covering all 4 acceptance criteria (https with .git, ssh, no .git suffix, non-GitHub URL error).
9. Write unit test for resolve_repo() with config.repo set (bypasses git remote).
10. Write integration test gated on GITHUB_TOKEN env var for GitHubClient::new().

Risks:
- Bead description says resolve_project returns Option<u32> but Config.project_number is Option<u64> and ARCH uses u64. Use u64 consistently.
- errors.rs needs to be implemented as part of this bead (it is currently empty). The From<Error> for McpError conversion references rmcp which is NOT a dependency of unblock-github — that conversion belongs in unblock-mcp. Skip it here.
- The .git/config parsing for resolve_repo is fragile — need to handle both url = https://... and url = git@... formats in the [remote "origin"] section. Consider using a simple line-by-line parser.
- reqwest 0.12 default_headers() API: use reqwest::header::HeaderMap and HeaderValue for building default headers.

Related tests:
- No existing test files for unblock-github (crates/unblock-github/tests/ does not exist).
- Unit tests should be in client.rs #[cfg(test)] module.
- Integration tests should go in crates/unblock-github/tests/integration.rs gated by GITHUB_TOKEN env check.

title: 1.2.7 Cache layer
description:
Implement GraphCache in crates/unblock-core/src/cache.rs — an in-memory cache for the computed ready set with configurable TTL.

CacheEntry struct:
- ready_set: Vec<IssueSummary>
- computed_at: std::time::Instant
- graph: DependencyGraph (so callers can run ad-hoc graph queries without rebuilding)

GraphCache struct:

- async fn invalidate(&self) — sets inner to None
- async fn is_fresh(&self) -> bool — true if entry exists and computed_at + ttl > now
- async fn get_graph(&self) -> Option<DependencyGraph> — for ad-hoc graph queries

This is a write-through cache: invalidate on every write operation.

title: 1.2.6 Graph — cycles and tree traversal
description:
Implement cycle detection and tree traversal methods on DependencyGraph in crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs.

Methods to implement:

1. fn would_create_cycle(&self, source: u64, target: u64) -> bool
   - Returns true if adding edge source→target would create a cycle
   - Use petgraph::algo::has_path_connecting(target, source) — if path exists target→source, adding source→target creates a cycle

2. fn detect_all_cycles(&self) -> Vec<Vec<u64>>
   - Use petgraph::algo::tarjan_scc
   - Returns all SCCs with more than 1 node (those are cycles)
   - Each inner Vec contains the issue numbers in the SCC

3. fn dependency_tree(&self, root: u64, direction: TraversalDirection, max_depth: usize) -> Vec<(u64, usize)>
   - BFS from root node
   - direction: Upstream (who blocks root?) or Downstream (what does root block?)
   - max_depth: stop expanding at this depth
   - Returns Vec of (issue_number, depth) pairs

Add TraversalDirection enum: Upstream, Downstream.
design: Reference: ARCH §6.4. Use petgraph::algo for both has_path_connecting and tarjan_scc. The would_create_cycle check is called before add_blocked_by mutations to give early rejection. dependency_tree is used by the 'show' tool to display blocking chains.

title: 1.2.5 Graph — cascade
description:
Implement compute_unblock_cascade() on DependencyGraph in crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs.

fn compute_unblock_cascade(&self, closed_number: u64, all_issues: &[Issue]) -> Vec<u64>

Logic:
- Find all issues that have closed_number as a blocker (incoming edge from closed_number)
- For each such issue, check whether ALL of its remaining blockers are now closed (treating closed_number as if it just closed)
- Return the issue numbers of those that are NOW fully unblocked (all blockers closed)
- Issues that still have other open blockers are NOT returned

Example:
- A blocks B, C. Close A → B and C are fully unblocked → cascade returns [B, C]
- A and D both block E. Close A → E still has D as open blocker → cascade returns []
- A blocks nothing → cascade returns []
design: Reference: ARCH §6.3. This method is called by the MCP 'close' tool after closing an issue to determine which downstream issues need their fields updated (Status → Ready, comment added). The method is purely computational — it does not mutate the graph or call any I/O.

DependencyGraph struct wrapping petgraph::DiGraph<u64, ()>:

  - Creates a node per issue number

INVESTIGATION ADDENDUM — CRITICAL: unsafe_code and edition 2024 testing strategy

The workspace has 'unsafe_code = deny' in workspace lints (Cargo.toml line 36). In Rust edition 2024, std::env::set_var() and std::env::remove_var() are unsafe functions. This means Config::load() tests CANNOT call set_var/remove_var without either:

Option A: Make Config::load() accept a generic env-reader (e.g., a closure or HashMap) so tests can inject env vars without touching the real environment. Production path passes std::env::var. This is the cleanest approach.

Option B: Add temp-env crate as dev-dependency and use #[allow(unsafe_code)] on the test module. Less clean but simpler.

Option C: Use #[cfg_attr(test, allow(unsafe_code))] on the test module and wrap set_var in unsafe blocks. Works but pollutes test code with unsafe.

RECOMMENDATION: Option A — Config::load_from() that takes an impl Fn(&str) -> Result<String, VarError> parameter, with Config::load() as a thin wrapper calling Config::load_from(std::env::var). Tests call load_from() with a HashMap-backed closure. Zero unsafe code needed.

title: Extend GitHubApi with cross-repo-aware primitives for Phase-3 cascade loop
description:
## Finding

Risk identified during QA validation of unblock-iov (response-shape only task for close handler).

## Location

crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:1068-1127 — Phase-3 cascade side-effects block.

## Problem

The close handler cascade loop calls:
- client.add_comment(u64)
- client.fetch_issue(u64)
- update_field(u64)

All three resolve against the single configured (owner, repo). When compute_unblock_cascade returns cross-repo dependents (e.g., other/repo#99), these calls silently resolve against <configured_owner>/<configured_repo>#99. Mismatched updates are swallowed by tracing::warn! fallbacks, so no error surfaces to the caller.

SPEC §8.2 flow step 6 and §11.4 row 4 assert aspirationally that cross-repo dependents ARE still cascade-updated. The current GitHubApi surface cannot honor this contract.

The unblock-iov task preserved this pre-existing behavior deliberately (its scope was response-shape only). This finding captures the required follow-up.

## Required Work

1. Extend the GitHubApi trait/impl with cross-repo-aware primitives:
   - add_comment_ref(QualifiedId, ...) — posts comment to any (owner, repo, number)
   - fetch_issue_ref(QualifiedId) — fetches issue from any (owner, repo, number)
   - update_field_ref(QualifiedId, ...) — updates field on any (owner, repo, number)
2. Migrate the Phase-3 cascade loop (server.rs:1068-1127) to use the *_ref variants when the dependent's repo differs from the configured repo.
3. Patch docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md and docs/plans/01-plan-mcp-foundation.md if the SPEC §8.2/§11.4 cross-repo cascade contract needs relaxation or refinement.

## References

- unblock-iov INVESTIGATION Risk #2
- QA BOUNDARIES RISK #1
- SPEC §8.2 flow step 6
- SPEC §11.4 row 4
design: The GitHubApi surface in crates/unblock-github/src/client.rs needs new methods that accept QualifiedId (owner + repo + number) instead of bare u64. The cascade loop in server.rs must detect when a dependent belongs to a foreign repo and dispatch to the *_ref variant. The tracing::warn! fallback paths can be removed or tightened once the *_ref variants are in place. API additions to unblock-github are non-breaking (additive); existing single-repo callers are unchanged. Commit message must carry an API: line per project coding standards.
close_reason: QA passed (verdict PASS); code review APPROVE; findings tracked as unblock-eos.16 (finding:deviation) and unblock-eos.17 (finding:risk) under parent epic unblock-eos.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:

Root cause / scope: The close handler Phase-3 cascade loop (server.rs:1068-1127) applies three side effects per cascade member — add_comment, fetch_issue, update_field — using primitives that only accept a bare `u64` AND resolve it against the single configured (owner, repo). When compute_unblock_cascade returns a cross-repo QualifiedId (e.g. other/repo#99), all three calls silently retarget <config.owner>/<config.repo>#99. The tracing::warn! fallbacks (server.rs:1072-1077, 1105-1110, 1118-1124) absorb the resulting errors, so the mismatch never surfaces to the MCP caller. Loop 1068-1127 iterates &cascade and derives cascaded_number = cascaded_qid.number (line 1069) — DROPS the (owner, repo). Lines 1072, 1087, 1097 are the three offending call sites.

comments.text: DECISION: Kept best-effort tracing::warn! fallbacks (did NOT promote to hard failure) in the Phase-3 cascade loop for add_comment_ref / fetch_issue_ref / update_field on cross-repo dependents. Reason: the configured token may lack write scope on a foreign repo; a hard failure on cascade would abort the close itself (which already succeeded on GitHub's side), leaving the graph inconsistent with the truth on GitHub. Added qualified_id=%cascaded_qid to the warn! fields so operators can observe which owner/repo#number was dropped.

comments.text: DECISION: Did NOT add update_field_ref. Reason: Projects V2 single-select field mutations operate on globally-scoped node IDs (project_id + item_id), not on (owner, repo, number). The project/item is resolved once per (owner, repo, number) via fetch_issue_ref (which now routes cross-repo), and the resulting node IDs are used directly with the existing update_field. Only fetch_issue and add_comment needed *_ref variants for the cascade ladder.

title: prime §7.3 full alignment — rewrite PrimeResult to { context: String } with §11.4 markdown trailer (BREAKING)
description:
**SPEC CONTRACT (MANDATORY):** Before implementing, read `docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md` §7.3 (prime tool — `PrimeResult` shape + flow), §11.4 (Cross-Repo Response Contract — markdown adaptation), §14 Invariant 14 (response-shape guarantee), and `docs/plans/01-plan-mcp-foundation.md` Task 04.13 + GAP-14 + DoD §11(b). This bead description is a pointer only — NOT a spec substitute. Acceptance criteria must be verified against spec + plan files, not assumed from this description.

---

## Scope

Path A (full spec alignment) decision for unblock-fah root cause. SPEC §7.3 defines `PrimeResult { context: String }` as a markdown blob; current impl returns a typed struct with categorised lists (`in_progress`, `ready`, `blocked`, `completed`, `hotspots`, `stale`, `session`, `drift_warnings`, `counts`). This bead closes the spec/impl drift by implementing §7.3 verbatim and delivering the §11.4 markdown trailer as a natural side-effect.

Changes:
- Rewrite `crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/prime.rs::PrimeResult` to `{ pub context: String }` per SPEC §7.3 (drop all other public fields).
- Port existing categorisation into a markdown renderer that produces (per SPEC §7.3 flow step 2):
  1. Header: repo/project identifiers.
  2. Counts block: ready / blocked / in-progress counts from the categorised lists.
  3. Cycle summary: `graph.detect_all_cycles()` rendered per §7.3 ("Issues with cycles (if any)"). Local cycle members render as bare `#N`.
  4. §11.4 trailer: when any detected cycle touches a cross-repo `QualifiedId`, append `## Cross-repo references` section listing each ref as `owner/repo#N` (`QualifiedId::Display`), sorted lexicographically, followed by italic `_{summary}_` line. Section omitted entirely when no cross-repo node participated.
- Update `#[tool]` shim at `crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:1994-2015` to return `Json<PrimeResult>` with the new `{ context: String }` shape.
- Mirror cycle-projection pattern from `crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/dep_cycles.rs::project_cycle` + `build_cross_repo_refs` (this is the third user of the summary pattern — implementer evaluates extract-vs-duplicate per unblock-eos.2 observation).
- Use `BTreeSet<String>` keyed by `QualifiedId::Display` for determinism (never `HashSet`), per §14 Invariant 14.
- Rewrite prime unit-test suite (~700 lines at prime.rs:740-1962) to assert on markdown content; preserve `categorise_*` / `filter_*` helper tests (they feed the renderer).
- Update `crates/unblock-mcp/tests/dyn_dispatch.rs:889-916` (`prime_dispatches_through_dyn_vtable`) to assert on `context` field instead of `result.counts.ready`.
- Add two integration tests to `crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs` using the hermetic MockGitHubClient harness (mirror `ready_*` / `dep_cycles_*` cross-repo style at integration.rs:757-1119 and 3643-3905):
  1. Cross-repo cycle fixture → `## Cross-repo references` section present in `context` with expected `owner/repo#N` bullets + italic summary.
  2. Local-only fixture → `## Cross-repo references` section absent.

## BREAKING CHANGE discipline

- Per CLAUDE.md "Pub API Change Tracking" — the commit landing the `PrimeResult` rewrite MUST carry a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer. `API:` line is INSUFFICIENT.
- Wire-contract impact: every MCP client consuming prime's typed fields (`counts.ready`, `in_progress`, `drift_warnings`, etc.) breaks. Document this explicitly in the commit body.
- No spec patch required — SPEC §7.3 already specifies the target shape; this bead closes impl drift.

## Coordination with sibling beads

- **unblock-fah** — superseded by this bead. Path A fulfils fah's §11.4 retro-fit intent as a natural consequence of the §7.3 alignment. Recommend closing/superseding fah once this bead's implementation lands.
- **unblock-eos.2** (shared cross_repo_refs summary helper, open) — this bead is the third user of the pattern (after `ready`, `dep_cycles`). Implementer decides extract-now-or-defer here.
- **unblock-eos.5** (compute_ready_set source scoping, closed) — prime's cached `ready_set` is already local-only by construction. Cycle-summary projection is therefore the ONLY §11.4 surface on prime that needs the cross-repo partition.
- **unblock-iov** (CloseResult §11.4 retro-fit, still open) — unrelated shape; no coordination needed.

## Out of scope

- Any SPEC §7.3 shape change (none required — impl catches up to existing spec).
- Any prime functionality beyond SPEC §7.3 flow steps 1-4.
- Migration guide for existing MCP agents consuming the typed shape (tracked separately if needed).
acceptance_criteria:
1. `PrimeResult` at `crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/prime.rs` is exactly `{ pub context: String }` per SPEC §7.3 — no other public fields.
2. `handle_prime` produces a markdown `context` containing repo/project identifiers, ready/blocked/in-progress counts, and a cycle summary built from `graph.detect_all_cycles()` per SPEC §7.3 flow step 2.
3. When any detected cycle touches a cross-repo `QualifiedId`, `context` ends with a `## Cross-repo references` section per SPEC §11.4 markdown-adaptation template (bulleted `owner/repo#N` lex-sorted, italic `_{summary}_` line). Omitted entirely otherwise.

6. `crates/unblock-mcp/tests/dyn_dispatch.rs:889-916` updated — asserts on `context` field, not on removed typed fields.
7. Prime unit suite (~700 lines at prime.rs:740-1962) rewritten to assert on markdown content; helper tests (`categorise_*`, `filter_*`) preserved as renderer building-blocks.
8. Two new integration tests in `crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs` — hermetic MockGitHubClient harness; one cross-repo cycle fixture (section present + expected bullets), one local-only (section absent).
9. Commit landing the `PrimeResult` rewrite carries `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer per CLAUDE.md Pub API Change Tracking.
10. Quality gate: `cargo fmt --check --all` + `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `cargo test --workspace` + `cargo doc --no-deps --workspace` all green.
11. SPEC §14 Invariant 14 holds (determinism via `BTreeSet<String>` keyed by `QualifiedId::Display`; never `HashSet` in projection).
12. No spec patch committed (Path A is impl catching up to existing §7.3 — spec unchanged).

The §11.4 trailer `_{summary}_` italic line MUST be grammatically parallel to the typed-response summaries, or the contract drifts.

- /Users/ramosmig/Public/WS-Labs/unblock/docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md:1750-1830 — SPEC §11.4 markdown-adaptation template (the exact markdown shape to emit).
- /Users/ramosmig/Public/WS-Labs/unblock/docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md:1960-1976 — §14 Invariant 14(b) determinism clause.
- /Users/ramosmig/Public/WS-Labs/unblock/docs/plans/01-plan-mcp-foundation.md:504-508 — Task 04.13 acceptance (markdown trailer presence/absence).

Approach (step-by-step for the implementing supervisor):

1. Branch per task (rust-supervisor house style); no worktree. Commit family should be atomic: (a) prime.rs rewrite + renderer + helper demotion; (b) server.rs shim description update; (c) dyn_dispatch.rs test update; (d) integration.rs two new tests. Optional fifth commit if supervisor chooses to also add `#[deprecated]` migration notes (likely not applicable — this is a hard break).

2. In prime.rs: demote `PrimeCounts`, `PrimeIssueSummary`, `HotspotSummary`, `StaleIssueSummary`, `CompletedIssueSummary` from `pub` to module-private (or `pub(super)`) — they are renderer inputs only. `SessionMeta` can follow the same demotion OR be inlined into the markdown header directly; supervisor choice — SPEC §7.3 does not require session metadata to appear in the markdown, but existing behaviour is agent-client detection. STRICT §7.3 read = drop session entirely from the markdown. User should confirm; flag as a decision point.

3. Replace `PrimeResult` with:
   ```rust
   #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
   pub struct PrimeResult {
       pub context: String,
   }
   ```
   Only one pub field. No `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = …)]` — `String` serialises as empty string when empty (SPEC §7.3 does not say the field is ever omitted; the markdown may be minimal but is always present).

4. Port the categorisation pipeline into a private `render_context` function:
   - Inputs: `&[Issue]`, `&DependencyGraph`, `&[IssueSummary] ready_summaries`, filtered/truncated `CategorisedIssues`, `configured_owner: &str`, `configured_repo: &str`, optional drift-warnings output (user-confirmed, see step 2).
   - Outputs: `String` — the §7.3 markdown blob.
   - Body structure (mirrors SPEC §7.3 flow step 2 verbatim, extended with the §11.4 trailer):
     1. Header line: `# Session context` or similar; `**Repo:** acme/widgets`; `**Project:** #N` (project number sourced from `state.github.project_number()` if available — verify via Grep; if not, elide and flag).
     2. Counts block: `- **Ready:** {n}`, `- **Blocked:** {n}`, `- **In progress:** {n}` (sourced from the POST-FILTER categorisation lengths, same as today's `PrimeCounts`).
     3. Cycle summary: call `graph.detect_all_cycles()` → `Vec<Vec<QualifiedId>>`. For each cycle, project members via the `project_cycle` pattern (local members → bare `#N` bullets; cross-repo members → `BTreeSet<String>` accumulator for the §11.4 trailer). Render as `## Issues with cycles` section with `- Cycle 1: #6 → #7 → #6` (or similar agent-readable form). `max_per_category` param applies to truncation here (cap number of cycle bullets).
     4. §11.4 trailer: if the accumulator is non-empty, append:
        ```
        ## Cross-repo references
        - \`owner/repo#N\`
        - \`owner/repo#M\`

        _{N cross-repo cycle member(s) omitted from \`cycles\`}_
        ```
        Use the exact summary phrasing from `dep_cycles::build_cross_repo_refs` (grammar parallel: '1 cross-repo cycle member omitted…' vs 'N cross-repo cycle members omitted…'). Italic line ends with blank line OR EOF.
   - Assert (debug_assert or test-covered): markdown is UTF-8, trailing newline, no partial sections.

5. Update `handle_prime` steps 7-8 (prime.rs:394-435): build `context` via `render_context(…)`, return `PrimeResult { context }`. Drop `filtered_ip / filtered_ready / filtered_blocked / filtered_stale` truncation into `PrimeIssueSummary` collections — replace with direct markdown bullet emission inside `render_context` (respect `max_per_category` for cycle list and any in-progress bullets if kept).

6. Update server.rs:2000-2015: change `description = "…"` to advertise a markdown blob ("Returns a markdown context blob for agent session injection. Includes repo/project identifiers, ready/blocked/in-progress counts, cycle summary, and cross-repo references per SPEC §11.4.").

7. Rewrite dyn_dispatch.rs:889-916 shape assertion: `let _ = result.context;` → `assert!(!result.context.is_empty());`. Fetch count assertions stay.

8. Rewrite prime.rs unit tests that introspect typed fields (prime.rs:1305-1539 range): replace with string-content assertions against the rendered markdown (`context.contains("**Ready:** 1")`, `context.contains("## Cross-repo references")`, etc.). Preserve ALL `categorise_*`, `hotspots_*`, `completed_*`, `filter_*`, `has_open_blockers_*`, `agent_filter_*`, `compute_*` helper tests — they feed the renderer unchanged.

9. Add two integration tests to integration.rs (mirror section at dep_cycles 3643-3905):
   - `prime_markdown_emits_cross_repo_section_when_cycle_touches_foreign_repo`: fixture = three issues in `acme/widgets` (#6, #7) + one in `other/repo` (#99), with a cycle #6 → #7 → `other/repo#99` → #6 via mocked edges. Call `handle_prime`. Assert `result.context.contains("## Cross-repo references")`, `result.context.contains("\`other/repo#99\`")`, `result.context.contains("cross-repo cycle member omitted from \`cycles\`")`. Assert lex ordering if multiple cross-repo bullets.
   - `prime_markdown_omits_cross_repo_section_when_all_cycles_are_local`: fixture = local 2-cycle #6 ↔ #7. Assert `result.context.contains("## Issues with cycles")` AND `!result.context.contains("## Cross-repo references")`.

10. Quality gate: `cargo fmt --check --all && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace && cargo doc --no-deps --workspace`.

11. Commit message: `refactor(mcp): rewrite prime result as markdown blob per SPEC §7.3` with body containing a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer enumerating the removed pub fields (`in_progress`, `ready`, `blocked`, `completed`, `hotspots`, `stale`, `session`, `drift_warnings`, `counts`) and the new shape. API: line is INSUFFICIENT per CLAUDE.md Pub API Change Tracking.

Impact:

- Wire-contract break: every MCP client / agent that parsed typed prime fields needs to re-parse markdown. No backwards compat layer (Path A was chosen over Path B exactly because adding a hybrid was rejected).
- Library-crate impact: prime.rs lives in the BINARY crate (`unblock-mcp`) — per CLAUDE.md Pub API Change Tracking, binary-crate API changes are EXCLUDED from the library-changelog requirement. HOWEVER, the bead explicitly requires a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer because the wire contract consumed by MCP clients IS a public contract. Supervisor MUST include the footer anyway per the bead's acceptance criterion #9 — do NOT rely on the crate-type exclusion.
- Deletion / demotion of `PrimeIssueSummary`, `HotspotSummary`, `StaleIssueSummary`, `CompletedIssueSummary`, `PrimeCounts`, possibly `SessionMeta`: also BREAKING for any external consumer that imports these from `unblock_mcp::tools::prime` (no grep hits outside the crate — safe in practice, but strictly speaking they were `pub`).
- unblock-fah becomes a closeable no-op as soon as this lands; supervisor should (a) note this in the commit body, or (b) leave the cross-bead closure to the user per the sibling-beads coordination notes.
- unblock-eos.2 extraction decision is live: prime becomes the third user. Recommend defer (duplicate now, extract in eos.2 later) to keep this bead scoped, but surface the choice to the user before coding.

Risks:

- `max_per_category` semantics under markdown: the param controls 'items per category' today (truncates lists). Under §7.3 the rendered markdown has no typed categories — supervisor must decide whether the param now truncates the cycle summary, or truncates an implicit bullet list of ready/blocked/in-progress issue numbers rendered alongside counts. SPEC §7.3 is silent. Strict read: counts-only (no per-category bullets) + untruncated cycle summary → `max_per_category` becomes effectively unused and should be deprecated (but left in PrimeParams for backwards compat to avoid a second breaking change to the params shape). Flag this to the user before coding.
- `stale_threshold_hours` similarly: currently governs stale claim detection and the completed-issues window. Under §7.3 neither section is mandated by spec. Strict read: drop stale + completed from the markdown → `stale_threshold_hours` becomes unused. Same deprecation/retention note as above.
- Drift warnings: handled via a background tokio::spawn (prime.rs:331-340, 433-454). Dropping them from the response loses the only current surface for reconcile output. The background spawn overhead remains; without a sink, removing it is a reasonable clean-up — but it's OUT OF SCOPE for this bead (crosses into Epic 1.6 drift-warnings scope). Recommend keeping the spawn in place but ignoring its output for now and surfacing a follow-up bead to either render drift warnings into the markdown or drop the spawn.
- Determinism (§14 Invariant 14): cross-repo bullets MUST use `BTreeSet<String>` keyed by `QualifiedId::Display`, never `HashSet`. The cycle summary itself must be deterministic too — Tarjan's SCC returns a stable ordering per petgraph, but within each cycle the order depends on the traversal root. Supervisor should test an idempotent hash over the full rendered markdown (`format!` output equals across runs) at least once in the integration suite.
- Session metadata: if supervisor drops SessionMeta from the response shape, the PRD §6.3 / Epic 1.5 delivery is partially undone. Per-bead scope says §7.3 alignment — SessionMeta is Epic 1.5 work that grew on top of the old shape. STRICT read = it goes; but this is another user-decision checkpoint.
- Test-rewrite scope: prime.rs has ~1220 lines of tests; ~280 lines of typed-shape assertions get rewritten; ~940 lines of helper tests survive. That's a lot of churn in a single commit — supervisor may want to split (a) renderer + helpers into commit 1, (b) PrimeResult + handler rewrite + test rewrite into commit 2. Each commit must still compile and pass tests (atomic-commit discipline).
- JSON-layer elision: SPEC §11.4 typed-response responses use `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = …)]` on `cross_repo_refs`. title: [OBSERVATION] compute_ready_set() leaks cross-repo source issues into bare-u64 ready projection
description:
## Finding

Source: unblock-cjv QA validation (OBSERVATION logged in COMPLETED comment; not previously tracked as a separate bead).

## Context

During integration test development for SPEC §11.4 cross_repo_refs in ReadyResult, it was observed that compute_ready_set() emits cross-repo source issues (e.g. other/repo#99) into the IssueSummary list with their bare number=99. This is exactly the ambiguity SPEC §11.4 warns about for the response-side projection — bare u64 numbers are ambiguous when the graph contains cross-repo nodes.

## Impact

- The integration test 'ready_cross_repo_open_blocker_populates_cross_repo_refs' in unblock-cjv had to assert on MEMBERSHIP (local issue #1 filtered OUT, #2 present) rather than count==1, because cross-repo source issue #99 leaks into the ready-set projection with its bare number.
- SPEC §11.4 affected-tools table covers cross-repo BLOCKER surfacing for the 'ready' tool, but the response shape still emits cross-repo SOURCE issues as bare u64 — a gap the spec/plan have not yet pinned down.

## Scope

Out-of-scope for unblock-cjv. That retro-fit was strictly about surfacing cross-repo BLOCKERS of LOCAL issues, not scrubbing cross-repo SOURCE issues from the ready set projection.

## Suggested Directions (to be evaluated by architect)

1. **Scrub cross-repo source issues from compute_ready_set() projection** — strict §11.4 interpretation: the ready tool returns LOCAL issues only.
2. **Extend §11.4 to a second response-shape pattern on IssueSummary** — e.g. add a qualified_id: Option<QualifiedId> field, following the same pattern as cross_repo_refs on the aggregate side.
3. **Accept current behavior as spec-gap** — document the bare-u64-in-mixed-repo ambiguity explicitly, deferring resolution.

## Reference Files

- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs (compute_ready_set)
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/ready.rs (handle_ready + compute_cross_repo_refs)
- docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md §7.1, §11.4
- crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs (ready_cross_repo_open_blocker_populates_cross_repo_refs test assertions)
close_reason: Direction 1 decided by user. Spec+plan patches landed on branch feat/eos.4-direction-1-spec-plan (commit 1ad7dbf). Implementation follow-up tracked as unblock-eos.5 (rust-supervisor, depends on unblock-eos.1). Closing this observation bead now; spec/plan PR and unblock-eos.5 implementation will go through their own review gates.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION (Sherlock):

Root cause: confirmed. compute_ready_set() in crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:144-217 iterates over the ENTIRE issues slice it is given (no (owner, repo) scoping) and emits IssueSummary { qualified_id, number: issue.number, ... } for every open + non-preserved-status + unblocked issue — including cross-repo SOURCE issues. The engine-level test cross_repo_ready_set_with_mixed_repos (graph.rs:1399-1414) locks this behavior in: it explicitly asserts acme/gadgets#1 is returned when only acme/widgets#1 is the local repo. Downstream, ReadyIssueSummary::from_core (tools/ready.rs:151-167) copies ONLY summary.number (u64) into the wire-level ReadyIssueSummary — qualified_id is dropped — so a cross-repo source like other/repo#99 appears in the JSON as a bare {\"number\": 99, ...} indistinguishable from a local issue #99. That is the exact §11.4-warned ambiguity. The handler never re-scopes by configured_owner/configured_repo between compute_ready_set (tools/mod.rs:167 via rebuild_cache, or cache.get_ready_set at ready.rs:400) and filter_ready_set (ready.rs:174-219); user-facing filters (priority, label, milestone, agent, issue_type, defer_until, claimed) do not touch (owner, repo). compute_cross_repo_refs (ready.rs:256-335) correctly guards at its input (skips cross-repo source issues at line 279-283), so the §11.4 envelope itself is fine — the gap is strictly on the primary issues vector.

Scope / policy question (MUST be resolved before code changes):
This is NOT a straightforward bugfix. The bead itself enumerates three candidate directions (scrub, extend §11.4 to IssueSummary, accept as spec-gap). Per user rule "never unilaterally simplify", a supervisor CANNOT pick one and run. The observation bead is labeled finding:observation on purpose — it needs an architect decision on which of (1)/(2)/(3) to pursue, then spec/plan patches, and only THEN an implementation bead. Choosing option 1 silently changes compute_ready_set semantics (breaks cross_repo_ready_set_with_mixed_repos, changes a pub fn in unblock-core — requires API:/BREAKING CHANGE: note per CLAUDE.md). Choosing option 2 adds a new field to response-side IssueSummary / ReadyIssueSummary (additive but touches a core shared type — API: note). Choosing option 3 is a spec patch only. None of the three is safe to land without explicit direction.

Files (evidence):
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:144-217 — compute_ready_set iterates full issues slice with no owner/repo scoping; emits IssueSummary per-issue.
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:1399-1414 — cross_repo_ready_set_with_mixed_repos test asserts current (leaking) behavior is correct at engine level.
- crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs:392-427 — IssueSummary struct: holds qualified_id, but also a bare u64 number — the bare-u64 is what the wire projection uses.
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/ready.rs:121-167 — ReadyIssueSummary + from_core: drops qualified_id, keeps number: u64 → the response-side bare-u64 projection §11.4 discusses.
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/ready.rs:256-335 — compute_cross_repo_refs: correctly guards cross-repo sources (line 279-283) for the REFS envelope, so its own implementation is consistent with the §11.4 contract as written.
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/ready.rs:379-438 — handle_ready: no re-scope of ready_set by (owner, repo) between cache read and filter_ready_set.
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs:161-170 — rebuild_cache passes the full issues slice straight into graph.compute_ready_set; cache then stores the leaked ready_set.
- crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs:896-977 — ready_cross_repo_open_blocker_populates_cross_repo_refs: uses membership assertion (!local_numbers.contains(&1), local_numbers.contains(&2)) instead of count==N specifically to sidestep this leak.
- docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md §2.9 (220-234), §3.3 (367-422), §7.1 (950-990), §11.4 (1718-1791), §14 Invariant 14 (1937) — the contract the bead claims has a gap.
- docs/plans/01-plan-mcp-foundation.md GAP-14 (765-790), D6 (803), DoD §11 (821).

Approach (recommended sequence):
1. Architect decision — not a rust-supervisor task. Present options 1/2/3 to the user with trade-offs (below) and get a pick. Do NOT pre-solve.
   - Option 1 (scrub): rust-supervisor work across 2 crates. compute_ready_set signature stays but semantics shift; add a configured (owner, repo) parameter OR a separate tool-layer scrub pass. Implementation contract: ready-set projection contains local issues only; update engine test cross_repo_ready_set_with_mixed_repos to match; make the integration test flip back to count==1. API:/BREAKING CHANGE: depending on whether signature changes.
   - Option 2 (extend §11.4 to IssueSummary): architect work first — design a response-side qualified_id: Option<QualifiedId> (or "qualified_number": Option<String>) field on IssueSummary/ReadyIssueSummary, document under §11.4 as the second response-shape pattern, update Invariant 14, add property-test goal, thread through all §11.4 affected tools if the pattern is universal. Then rust-supervisor retro-fits.
   - Option 3 (accept gap): architect patch to spec/plan only. Document the bare-u64-in-mixed-repo ambiguity explicitly in §11.4 (e.g., a "Known limitations" sub-section), note compute_ready_set emits cross-repo sources by design, and defer a structured fix to a named follow-up phase.
2. Once direction picked, create the implementation bead(s). If option 1 or 2, they are siblings to the current §11.4 retro-fit beads (unblock-fah, unblock-iov) and MUST be evaluated against GAP-14 retro-migration sequencing (plan lines 779-790). If option 3, only a spec/plan patch bead under unblock-eos — no crate edits.
3. Cross-check with sibling bead unblock-eos.1 (compute_cross_repo_refs missing-state fallback) — options 1/2 here may touch the same helper; sequencing matters.

Risks / edge cases:

- The bead description itself notes the retro-fit test in unblock-cjv had to use MEMBERSHIP assertions (not count==1). If option 1 is chosen, revisit that test (integration.rs:896) to tighten the assertion.
- Invariant 14 (§14, spec line 1937) currently speaks of "cross-repo node NOT emitted in the bare-u64 projection" — option 1 strengthens this (nothing cross-repo in projection at all); option 2 weakens it (projection can carry cross-repo via qualified_id extension). Either direction requires Invariant 14 re-wording.
- unblock-core::types::IssueSummary is pub — a new field triggers API: note per CLAUDE.md commit policy.
- unblock-core::graph::DependencyGraph::compute_ready_set signature change (option 1) requires API:/BREAKING CHANGE: note; it is also referenced by prime.rs (tools/prime.rs:1496) and tests across the workspace — audit call sites before any signature change.
- The list tool (§7.5) was listed as NOT affected by §11.4 because it's scoped to configured repo. If option 1 is chosen for ready, verify that list's scoping is ALSO explicit (not incidental), to avoid the same gap re-appearing.
- compute_ready_set is property-tested (graph.rs:1449-1598). Any semantic change invalidates existing proptest expectations; new properties need to be added.

Related tests (that need review depending on chosen option):
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:1399-1414 — cross_repo_ready_set_with_mixed_repos (engine-level — explicit leak assertion).
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:1658-1726 — cross_repo_same_numbers_distinct_in_graph proptest (only asserts IssueState::Open; silent w.r.t. scoping).
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/ready.rs:1100-1118 — cross_repo_refs_cross_repo_source_issue_does_not_contribute (helper-level guard — intact).
