title: align compute_cross_repo_refs missing-state fallback with §3.3 canonical semantics
description:
File: crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/ready.rs:300-303

`compute_cross_repo_refs` uses `unwrap_or(IssueState::Open)` when a blocker edge target has no known IssueState, which treats missing as BLOCKING. The canonical §3.3 implementation in `crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:176-178` uses `is_some_and(== Open)`, which treats missing as NOT blocking.

Under the current `DependencyGraph::build` invariant the divergence is unreachable (issue_state is populated for every node_map entry), but creates latent risk if that invariant ever loosens. Align the fallback with graph.rs:176-178 semantics (treat missing as not blocking) and add a unit test for the missing-state case to pin the contract.

Reference: SPEC §3.3 step 6 + Invariant 14.
close_reason: QA PASS — SPEC §3.3 canonical fallback alignment merged. 700 tests green, fmt/clippy/doc clean. Bead approved (Linus) + qa-passed (Quinn). EXTRA rustdoc fix already logged as DEVIATION; SPEC §3.3:425 pseudocode discrepancy deferred.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:

Root cause: ready.rs line 300-303 (compute_cross_repo_refs) resolves a blocker's IssueState via issue_state_map.get(blocker_qid).copied().unwrap_or(IssueState::Open). When a blocker qid is absent from the state map the blocker is treated as Open → BLOCKING, which (combined with the 'step-6' membership check) would cause a missing-state cross-repo blocker to be emitted in cross_repo_refs.omitted. The §3.3 canonical implementation (graph.rs:171-179, inside DependencyGraph::compute_ready_set) uses is_blocked = neighbors.any(|n| issue_state.get(qid).is_some_and(|s| *s == Open)), i.e. missing state → NOT blocking. Under the current DependencyGraph::build invariant (graph.rs:90-96 populates issue_state and node_map in lock-step for every Issue; edges to unknown qids are dropped at graph.rs:107-114) the divergence is unreachable — every blocker_qid reached via neighbors_directed has a state entry. The bead flags this as latent risk and pins the contract with a unit test.

Files:
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/ready.rs:300-303 — the divergent fallback that must align with §3.3 canonical semantics (missing → not blocking, skip as if closed). Only occurrence of unwrap_or(IssueState::Open) in ready.rs (grep confirms single match).
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/ready.rs:220-254 — doc comment for compute_cross_repo_refs. Algorithm step 5 currently says 'Closed blockers do not contribute' — after alignment the doc should read 'Closed OR missing-state blockers do not contribute (mirrors §3.3 canonical is_some_and(==Open) semantic)'. Also update the //! module doc if it describes the fallback.
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:171-179 — the canonical §3.3 is_blocked predicate to mirror (is_some_and(|state| *state == IssueState::Open)).
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:83-123 — DependencyGraph::build invariant; confirms issue_state is populated for every node_map entry (Invariant source). Cite in the new test doc-comment as the reason the missing-state branch is unreachable via public API today.
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/ready.rs:846-1148 — existing 'compute_cross_repo_refs — hermetic unit tests' block. New unit test goes here, after the determinism test at line 1124.
- docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md:369-445 (§3.3) and :1974-1976 (§14 Invariant 14) — spec references already cited by bead. Pseudocode at §3.3 line 425 ('IF issue_state[blocker_qid] != Closed: all_blockers_closed = FALSE') is a pseudocode-shortcut that treats missing as blocking (same bug the bead fixes in ready.rs). The canonical is graph.rs:176-178 per the bead. The spec text itself should NOT be changed in this bead — eos.1 is code-alignment only.
- docs/plans/01-plan-mcp-foundation.md:826 — flags ready.rs as a merge-conflict surface with unblock-eos.5 (the eos.4 graph-engine signature change). eos.1 should land first to unblock eos.5's rebase; the bead is already marked as blocking eos.5.

Approach:
1. Align the fallback at ready.rs:303 to the canonical semantic. Replace the three-line unwrap_or pattern with an is_some_and predicate. Concretely: remove lines 300-303 and the subsequent 'if blocker_state == IssueState::Closed { continue; }' at line 304-307; replace with:
     let blocker_is_open = issue_state_map.get(blocker_qid).is_some_and(|state| *state == IssueState::Open);
     if !blocker_is_open { continue; }
   Keep 'any_open_blocker = true;' and the cross-repo classification immediately after, unchanged. This preserves the two-pass collect-then-commit structure described in the algorithm doc.
2. Update the compute_cross_repo_refs doc comment (lines 221-254) step 5 to read: 'Closed OR missing-state blockers do not contribute (mirrors §3.3 canonical is_some_and(==Open) semantic; see graph.rs:171-179).' No behaviour change for consumers — just pinning the contract in rustdoc.
3. Add a unit test to pin the missing-state contract. Problem: DependencyGraph::build makes the missing-state branch unreachable, and the graph has no mutator/constructor to inject an inconsistent state. Recommended path: extract the inner per-blocker classification loop (lines 296-312) into a pub(crate) helper with signature:
     fn classify_blockers(
         node_idx: NodeIndex,
         inner: &DiGraph<QualifiedId, ()>,
         issue_state_map: &HashMap<QualifiedId, IssueState>,
         configured_owner: &str,
         configured_repo: &str,
     ) -> (bool /*any_open_blocker*/, Vec<String> /*cross_repo_blockers*/)
   compute_cross_repo_refs calls this helper; unit test instantiates DependencyGraph::build with an issue slice that includes a blocker, then constructs a SECOND HashMap<QualifiedId, IssueState> with that key removed and passes it into classify_blockers directly. Assert (any_open_blocker == false) — missing-state must NOT count as blocking. Doc-comment the test citing graph.rs:171-179 and bead unblock-eos.1.
   Alternative if the orchestrator prefers not to introduce a helper: add a #[cfg(test)] pub fn DependencyGraph::with_missing_state_for_test constructor in unblock-core exposing a way to build a graph whose issue_state omits a given node. This is heavier (touches unblock-core public-ish surface) and less aligned with eos.2 (shared helper across §11.4 retro-fits). Prefer the helper.
4. Quality gate: cargo fmt --check --all, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, cargo doc --no-deps --workspace. All existing tests MUST remain green — the semantic change is unreachable under current build invariant, so no integration or unit test expectations change.

Risks:
- Pseudocode in SPEC §3.3 (line 425) reads 'IF issue_state[blocker_qid] != Closed → blocking', which matches the OLD ready.rs fallback, NOT the canonical graph.rs:176-178 impl. The bead identifies graph.rs as canonical, not the spec pseudocode. DO NOT touch the spec in this bead — eos.1 is strictly code alignment. If the discrepancy between spec pseudocode and canonical impl needs its own spec patch, raise a separate bead. Flag for user if you notice this during implementation.

The helper returns both pieces; caller decides whether to commit. DO NOT pre-insert into accum inside the helper or the 'local issue with only closed blockers' case (existing cross_repo_refs_closed_cross_repo_blocker_returns_none test, ready.rs:944) will regress.
- eos.2 wants a shared helper across §11.4 retro-fits (dep_cycles, prime, close, ready). The extracted classify_blockers belongs to 'ready-set step-6' semantics specifically — don't over-generalise here. Leave naming like classify_ready_blockers (or inline in a mod-private module) so eos.2 can hoist a separate shared builder. If you generalise prematurely you'll block eos.2.

title: fix relative-path resolution in unblock-github live-API integration tests (21 failures)
description:
**SPEC CONTRACT (MANDATORY):** Before implementing, read `docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md` §13 (Testing strategy) and the existing `crates/unblock-github/tests/integration.rs` suite. This bead description is a pointer only — NOT a spec substitute. Acceptance criteria must be verified against spec + plan files, not assumed from this description.

---

21 tests in `crates/unblock-github/tests/integration.rs` fail identically on main with `GitHubClient::new() should succeed: GitRemote { message: "failed to read .git/config: No such file or directory (os error 2)" }`.

Root cause: the tests instantiate `GitHubClient::new()` which resolves `.git/config` via a relative path, but `cargo test` runs member tests with CWD set to the member's directory (`crates/unblock-github/`), not the workspace root. `.git/config` does not exist at that relative path.

- `add_sub_issue_creates_parent_child_relationship`
- `add_sub_issue_returns_issue_not_found_for_nonexistent_number`
- `close_issue_closes_issue_and_refetch_confirms`
- `close_issue_returns_issue_not_found_for_nonexistent_number`
- `close_issue_with_reason_adds_comment_before_closing`
- `create_issue_returns_issue_with_correct_fields`
- `detect_owner_type_returns_org_for_org_accounts`
- `fetch_graph_data_issues_have_valid_status_and_priority`
- `fetch_graph_data_returns_issues_from_real_repo`
- `fetch_issue_returns_full_details_for_existing_issue`
- `fetch_issue_returns_issue_not_found_for_nonexistent_number`
- `github_client_new_connects_to_real_repo`
- `init_create_project_and_idempotency_check`
- `remove_blocked_by_removes_blocking_relationship`
- `remove_blocked_by_returns_issue_not_found_for_nonexistent_number`
- `resolve_owner_node_id_returns_non_empty_id`

Evidence file:line anchor: `crates/unblock-github/tests/integration.rs:2002` (and all sites calling `GitHubClient::new()` without a fixture).

Impact: contaminates the `cargo test --workspace` signal for every agent/CI check. Supervisor QA reports had to manually disambiguate these failures as pre-existing on each implementation bead. Spec §13 G1/G7 (workspace quality gate green) is de-facto false today.

Approach options (pick one, propose + discuss before implementing):
1. **Env-guard:** `#[ignore]` by default; live tests opt-in via `cargo test --ignored` + `GITHUB_TOKEN`. CI runs them in a dedicated live-API job.
2. **Path resolution fix:** have `GitHubClient::new()` (or the test harness) discover the workspace root via `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` or `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` before reading `.git/config`. Must not regress production behaviour.
3. **Fixture injection:** stop relying on `.git/config` inside tests — inject owner/repo via a test constructor.

Acceptance:
- `cargo test --workspace` finishes with zero failures on a clean clone without `GITHUB_TOKEN` set (live tests either skipped via `#[ignore]` or succeed with injected fixture).
- `cargo test --workspace -- --ignored` runs the full live-API suite when `GITHUB_TOKEN` is set (or equivalent opt-in path).
- Fix must not require changes to `GitHubClient` production API unless unavoidable — if unavoidable, use the `API:` footer per project CLAUDE.md.
- Integration test file changes: preserve existing coverage; no test deleted.

Surfaced by: QA of unblock-29p.11 on 2026-04-16 — orchestrator-level spot-check of `cargo test --workspace`.

Ref: spec §13 Testing strategy, §14 Invariants.

   b. `close_cross_repo_dependent_populates_cross_repo_refs` — fixture: local blocker #8 has a LOCAL dependent #10 AND a CROSS-REPO dependent `other/repo#99` (edge: other/repo#99 → acme/widgets#8); close #8 → cascade = [#10, QualifiedId(other, repo, 99)]; assert `unblocked == [10]` (only local), `cross_repo_refs.omitted == ["other/repo#99"]`, `cross_repo_refs.summary` matches the exact close_summary phrasing (singular form). JSON envelope: `json["cross_repo_refs"]["omitted"][0] == "other/repo#99"`. For determinism assurance on plural branches, include a second cross-repo dependent (`alpha/upstream#42`) and assert lex order: `omitted == ["alpha/upstream#42", "other/repo#99"]`. This fulfils the Invariant 14(b) determinism clause (`omitted` sorted lexicographically).

   Fixture pattern: clone `dep_cycles_cross_repo_fixture` (integration.rs:3676-3708) as `close_cross_repo_fixture`. Use `ready_cross_repo_fixture` (integration.rs:796) as the canonical minimum-field template. MockGitHubClient state must push: fetch_issue (for #8), close_issue, fetch_graph_data (the rebuild). The Phase-3 loop invokes `add_comment` and possibly `fetch_issue` + `update_field` per cascaded dependent — these MUST be pushable via the mock. Check MockGitHubClient capabilities at crates/unblock-github/src/mock.rs before authoring the fixture to confirm enough pushable slots (add_comment, update_field, resolve_project_info, get_project_item_id, fetch_issue × N for the cascade loop).

7. Quality gate before commit: `cargo fmt --check --all`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo doc --no-deps --workspace`. All four must be green. Commit message: `feat(mcp): adopt §11.4 cross_repo_refs in CloseResult` with body `API: CloseResult gains cross_repo_refs: Option<CrossRepoRefs>`. Non-breaking (additive Option with skip_serializing_if); no BREAKING CHANGE footer needed. Per CLAUDE.md Pub API Change Tracking, unblock-mcp is the binary crate and is EXCLUDED from the mandatory footer requirement, but keep the API: line for parity with sibling retro-fits (cjv/29p.11 landed with identical commit grammar).

Impact / modules touched:
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/cross_repo.rs — additive (+2 pub(crate) fns project_cascade + close_summary + their unit tests). No breakage.
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/close.rs — additive field on CloseResult. Clients that did `result.cross_repo_refs` would break, but no such clients exist today. JSON wire format: additive (skip_serializing_if elides when None). Non-breaking for agents that don't parse the new field.
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs close handler (968-1137) — behavioural: partition site changed from flatten-all to partition-by-repo. NET-observable diff: when cross-repo dependent exists, the bare-u64 `unblocked` is STRICTLY SHORTER than today. This could surprise agents that expected cross-repo numbers to appear in `unblocked` (today they leak as ambiguous u64s) — but that leak is the §11.4 defect this bead repairs.
- crates/unblock-mcp/tests/dyn_dispatch.rs and integration.rs — test-only additions / extensions.

Risks:

1. **cross_repo helper parity drift.** The shared helper lineage is load-bearing (cjv/29p.11 BOTH share `cycles_summary` / `ready_summary` / `build_cross_repo_refs_with_summary` byte-for-byte). Implementer MUST author `close_summary` and `project_cascade` in the SAME module — not inline in close.rs. Parity test: grep `build_cross_repo_refs_with_summary` — call sites SHOULD grow from 3 (ready, dep_cycles, prime) to 4 (+ close). Follow-up observation unblock-eos.2 is already closed, but the extract-shared-helper principle it codified is non-negotiable (user non-negotiable per cross_repo.rs:22-26 doc comment).

2. **Cross-repo dependent Phase-3 side-effects are best-effort, not in scope.** When cascade contains a cross-repo QualifiedId, the Phase-3 loop at server.rs:1067-1126 invokes `client.add_comment(cascaded_number, …)` and `client.fetch_issue(cascaded_number)` — both are `u64`-only and scoped to the configured repo. So for cross-repo dependent `other/repo#99`, the add_comment call resolves against `acme/widgets#99` (or fails if #99 doesn't exist locally) — NOT against the actual cross-repo dependent. The existing `tracing::warn!(…, "Failed to post unblock comment on cascaded issue")` absorbs the failure silently. SPEC §8.2 flow step 6 says "Cross-repo dependents ARE still cascade-updated" but this is ASPIRATIONAL given the current GitHubApi surface. The bead DOES NOT scope this limitation — the response-shape partition is the only scope. Flag for a follow-up bead "cross-repo-aware cascade API (add_comment_ref / update_field_ref / fetch_issue_ref in cascade)" — but OUT OF SCOPE for unblock-iov.

3. **Partition ordering vs Tarjan iteration order.** `compute_unblock_cascade` returns a Vec<QualifiedId> whose iteration order is petgraph's Incoming-neighbours order — NOT contractually stable. The LOCAL projection `Vec<u64>` inherits this non-determinism. Integration tests MUST assert on SET membership (HashSet::from), not positional order — mirror dep_cycles integration tests at integration.rs:3757-3761 and 3855-3861. The cross-repo `omitted` side is lex-sorted by BTreeSet (deterministic — ok to assert positionally).

4. **Double-accumulation guard.** If `compute_unblock_cascade` ever returns the same QualifiedId twice (shouldn't happen post petgraph — neighbors_directed is unique per edge, but self-loops could theoretically duplicate — except self-loops are rejected at edge insertion per graph engine docs), the BTreeSet<String> accum dedups cross-repo entries automatically. The local Vec<u64> side does NOT dedup — mirror project_cycle's behaviour (cross_repo.rs:82-89 which also does not dedup locally). Fine by SPEC — unblocked: Vec<u64> is not required to be deduped (spec §8.2 does not impose a set-shape on unblocked).

5. **JSON assertion pattern — `serde_json::Value::get` vs `contains_key`.** Existing tests use `json.get("cross_repo_refs").is_none()` for the elision assertion (integration.rs:877-878, 3772-3774). Keep the same idiom — don't switch to `.as_object().unwrap().contains_key(...)` even though technically equivalent. Consistency within the §11.4 test surface matters for future reviewers.

6. **Commit-grammar parity with sibling retro-fits.** cjv landed as `feat(mcp): retro: adopt §11.4 cross_repo_refs in ReadyResult` (or similar — check `git log --oneline` for the exact shape). Mirror the subject line. The API: body line is the marker future changelog tooling will key on.

7. **`close` handler extraction.** The close logic is still in server.rs, not extracted to tools/close.rs like handle_ready / handle_dep_cycles. This bead SHOULD NOT extract — that's a separate concern (sibling to unblock-eos.8 for prime). Adding the partition call directly in the server.rs handler is correct. If extraction is desired, file a follow-up bead — do not bundle.

8. **MockGitHubClient push-slot arity.** For the cross-repo test fixture that closes #8 and cascades into [#10 local, other/repo#99 cross-repo, alpha/upstream#42 cross-repo], Phase-3 iterates 3 times and may call: 3× add_comment, 3× (optional) field_ids + resolve_project_info + get_project_item_id + fetch_issue + update_field. The `close_dispatches_through_dyn_vtable` test at dyn_dispatch.rs:366-400 already demonstrates the push-order shape. Verify mock.rs supports `push_add_comment` / `push_fetch_issue` × N — likely it does, but check before authoring the fixture.

Related tests (to preserve / update / create):
- crates/unblock-mcp/tests/dyn_dispatch.rs:366-400 (close_dispatches_through_dyn_vtable) — UPDATE: add `assert!(result.cross_repo_refs.is_none())` and JSON elision assertion. All-local fixture, branch stays green.

- crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs — NEW section `close_*`: two tests per Approach step 6. Covers DoD item 11(b) close row + Task 04.07 acceptance final line ("Integration test must cover the cross-repo-dependent case").
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/cross_repo.rs tests module — NEW: project_cascade_* unit tests (4) + close_summary_* unit tests (2). Covers helper-level coverage symmetric to existing project_cycle_* and cycles_summary_* tests.
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/close.rs — NO `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block exists in the file today (per my read at close.rs:1-38, empty below the TODO). This bead MAY add one for `CloseResult` JSON-shape elision unit tests (serialize a `CloseResult { issue: 1, unblocked: vec![], cross_repo_refs: None }` and assert the JSON key is elided; and serialize a `CloseResult { …, cross_repo_refs: Some(CrossRepoRefs { omitted: vec!["other/repo#99".to_owned()], summary: Some("1 cross-repo dependent…".to_owned()) }) }` and assert the JSON shape matches). So the thing the bead asks us to retro-fit — a markdown cycle summary — does not exist in the codebase.

This is a Phase 01 spec-vs-impl divergence that was NOT flagged in the §11.4 design bead (unblock-9f7). The design bead reviewed the 4 affected tools (`ready`, `prime`, `dep_cycles`, `close`) under the assumption each matches its §7 / §8 spec shape. The two completed sibling retro-fits (unblock-cjv ReadyResult, unblock-29p.11 dep_cycles) land cleanly because their typed shapes already match spec. Prime does not — and the gap is structural (markdown blob vs typed struct + presence/absence of cycle rendering), not just "missing field".

Global user directive (CLAUDE.md): 'Never do a decision to simplify the solution. Case you reach this point question the user.' I am flagging this as a pre-implementation BLOCKER that requires a user decision before rust-supervisor proceeds. I see three paths, all of which materially change the scope of this bead, and none of which fit under the §11.4 retro-fit framing alone.

Path A — Full spec alignment (largest scope, strictest conformance):
  1. Rewrite `PrimeResult` to `{ context: String }` per SPEC §7.3 verbatim.
  2. Port the existing categorisation into a markdown renderer: repo/project/counts header, then a cycle summary section calling `graph.detect_all_cycles()` that lists cycle issue numbers, then the §11.4 `## Cross-repo references` trailing section when any cycle traverses a cross-repo `QualifiedId`.

Removes `in_progress`, `ready`, `blocked`, `completed`, `hotspots`, `stale`, `session`, `drift_warnings`, `counts` from the wire response. Agents that parse those fields break. Tests at prime.rs:1281-1962 (~700 lines of unit coverage) and dyn_dispatch.rs:889 all need rewrite or deletion.

Path B — Hybrid (keep typed struct, add both a markdown `context` field AND a `cross_repo_refs` typed field):

  2. ALSO add `pub cross_repo_refs: Option<CrossRepoRefs>` to `PrimeResult` for parity with `ReadyResult` / `DepCyclesResult` / `CloseResult`.
  3. Add `detect_all_cycles()` call into `handle_prime`; build `compute_cross_repo_refs_for_prime` that walks the cycle list with the same projection semantics as `dep_cycles::project_all`.
  4. Integration tests: one fixture with cross-repo cycle member (both context contains markdown section AND cross_repo_refs = Some), one without (context omits section AND cross_repo_refs = None).
  Impact: Non-breaking additive. Preserves all current agent consumers. Introduces spec-defined `context` field but leaves typed struct intact.
  SPEC deviation: §7.3 says `PrimeResult { context: String }` — this adds fields the spec does not list. Requires a spec patch under unblock-eos (or a new sibling bead) to extend §7.3 response shape, OR a DEVIATION decision logged by the user.

Path C — Minimal retro-fit (bead description taken literally, assume spec-vs-impl drift is handled elsewhere):
  1. Introduce a markdown cycle summary INTERNALLY within prime — `detect_all_cycles()` → render cycle list → attach a markdown block to one of the existing fields (candidates: `drift_warnings` vec, or a new `cycles_markdown: Option<String>` field, or a new `cross_repo_refs_markdown: Option<String>` field that only contains the §11.4 trailer).
  2. Implement the §11.4 markdown trailer in the chosen sink. When any detected cycle touches a cross-repo `QualifiedId`, append `## Cross-repo references` + bulleted `owner/repo#N` + italic summary. Omit entirely otherwise.
  3. Integration tests: one cross-repo cycle fixture, one local-only.
  Impact: Smallest code change but creates its own drift — the §11.4 markdown adaptation lives in a field that SPEC §7.3 does not specify; agents have to know to look there. Spec still says prime returns a markdown blob; impl still returns a typed struct with a sidecar markdown field. Net drift is larger after this path than before.

Risks common to all paths:
- Ready-set leak observation (unblock-eos.4, now closed): prime already consumes the cached `ready_set` which after eos.4 is guaranteed local-only. Any cycle-summary implementation MUST distinguish 'cross-repo node in a cycle the graph detected' from 'cross-repo node in the ready set' — the former is §11.4 territory for this bead, the latter is already scrubbed by the engine.
- Mirror §3.3 / graph-engine semantics: `detect_all_cycles()` returns `Vec<Vec<QualifiedId>>` — not filtered by configured repo. The projection for prime's cycle summary must partition (local members → `#N`, cross-repo members → omitted) using the same pattern as `dep_cycles::project_cycle`. Do NOT re-invent the projection; share with dep_cycles (tracks unblock-eos.2 extract-shared-helper observation).
- Determinism / Invariant 14: use `BTreeSet<String>` keyed by `QualifiedId::Display`; free dedupe + lex sort. Never `HashSet`.
- skip_serializing_if parity (if Path B): `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` on the cross_repo_refs field, plus a JSON-layer assertion in integration tests that the key is elided when None (mirroring ready / dep_cycles tests).
- Existing prime unit-test suite (prime.rs:740-1962) is dense — any shape change ripples across ~700 lines. Path A rewrites, Path B extends, Path C is additive.
- dyn_dispatch::prime_dispatches_through_dyn_vtable (dyn_dispatch.rs:889-916) asserts `result.counts.ready` accessibility — Path A breaks this, Path B/C leave it intact.
- Sibling retro-fit commit discipline (unblock-9f7 comment 1): commit message should include `API:` line for the response-schema change. Path A = BREAKING CHANGE footer; Path B/C = API: additive footer.
- Plan DoD item 11(b): 'ready, prime, dep_cycles, close honor the `cross_repo_refs` contract. GAP-14 retro-fits landed. Integration tests cover Some/None branches for each.' Path A satisfies via markdown trailer presence/absence, Path B via BOTH markdown trailer AND typed field (double guard), Path C via the sidecar markdown field (weakest conformance — the plan text implies cross_repo_refs as a field, not a section).

Related tests (to preserve / update / create):
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/prime.rs:740-1962 — existing unit suite (categorise_*, filter_*, PrimeParams, PrimeResult serialisation, SessionMeta). Must stay green on Paths B and C; Path A requires wholesale rewrite because the typed fields disappear.
- crates/unblock-mcp/tests/dyn_dispatch.rs:889-916 — vtable test asserting `result.counts.ready` — must stay compatible on Paths B/C; Path A must switch to asserting `!result.context.is_empty()` or similar.

Decision point for the user (required before rust-supervisor touches code):
Which path? Path A (full spec conformance, BREAKING), Path B (hybrid, non-breaking + spec patch), or Path C (minimal retro-fit, preserves shape + sidecar markdown)? The bead description as written matches Path C, but SPEC §7.3 + Task 04.13 acceptance text imply Path A. Per CLAUDE.md 'Never do a decision to simplify the solution' — I am surfacing this rather than choosing.

comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:

Root cause: ReadyResult struct in crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/ready.rs currently has 3 fields (issues, count, stale) and the ready handler in crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs reads only cache.get_ready_set() — the already-filtered local ready set, with no visibility into which LOCAL issues were filtered OUT due to cross-repo OPEN blockers. SPEC §11.4 + §7.1 flow step 9 require adding cross_repo_refs: Option<CrossRepoRefs> populated from those cross-repo blockers. Implementation work is pure additive retro-fit; no existing semantics change.

Files:
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/ready.rs:49-59 — add cross_repo_refs field to ReadyResult with #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]; add new computation helper compute_cross_repo_refs(issues, graph, configured_owner, configured_repo) -> Option<CrossRepoRefs> mirroring dep_cycles build_cross_repo_refs naming/shape.
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:817-861 — ready handler: after cache is fresh, also pull cache.get_issues() and cache.get_graph() and call the new helper; pass result into ReadyResult. When cache empty (stale=true), cross_repo_refs is None (no data to inspect). Keep existing filter_ready_set() signature unchanged (it only does tool-layer post-filtering; cross-repo computation is step-6-of-§3.3 scoped, NOT tool-layer-filter scoped).
- crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs:830-840 — CrossRepoRefs type already exists (landed in unblock-9f7 / commit 77c4983); no core changes required. Just import via unblock_core::types::CrossRepoRefs.
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/dep_cycles.rs:181-253 — reference implementation for projection semantics and build_cross_repo_refs summary format. Mirror its BTreeSet<String> accumulator pattern and its lex-sort-by-QualifiedId::Display guarantee; write a ready-specific summary string (example from spec §11.4 type doc: "N cross-repo blocker(s) excluded local issue(s) from ready set").
- crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs:460-755 — existing ready integration tests (pattern uses GraphCache + in-memory test_issue fixture + DependencyGraph::build). Add two new ready tests mirroring dep_cycles_returns_all_local_cycles_from_warm_cache + dep_cycles_mixed_cycle_populates_cross_repo_refs (lines 3370-3543).
- crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs:29-61 — existing qid() uses ("test","repo",N). For the new mock-backed tests, use the same ("acme","widgets",N) pattern dep_cycles tests adopted since new_mock() returns MockGitHubClient::new("acme","widgets",Some(1)) and state.github.owner()/repo() must match configured repo for the local-vs-cross-repo partition to be correct.
- docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md §2.16 (line 308), §3.3 (line 367), §7.1 (line 950), §11.4 (line 1718), §14 Invariant 14 (line 1937).
- docs/plans/01-plan-mcp-foundation.md Task 04.05 acceptance (line 462), GAP-14 retro-migration sequencing (line 765-790), DoD item 11 (line 821).

Approach:
1. Create branch (rust-supervisor decides exact name, e.g., feat/cjv-ready-cross-repo-refs).
2. Edit crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/ready.rs:
   a. Add use unblock_core::types::CrossRepoRefs at the top.
   b. Add cross_repo_refs: Option<CrossRepoRefs> to ReadyResult with #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] attribute. Add /// doc comment referencing SPEC §11.4.
   c. Add pub(crate) helper fn compute_cross_repo_refs(issues: &[Issue], graph: &DependencyGraph, configured_owner: &str, configured_repo: &str) -> Option<CrossRepoRefs>. Algorithm:
      - Use BTreeSet<String> accumulator keyed by QualifiedId::Display (free dedup + lex sort, mirrors dep_cycles project_all line 236).
      - For each issue in issues:
        * If issue.state != IssueState::Open → skip.
        * If issue.status is InProgress | Deferred | Closed → skip (§3.3 filter 2).
        * If issue.qualified_id.owner != configured_owner || issue.qualified_id.repo != configured_repo → skip. Contract scopes the source issue to the configured repo (SPEC §11.4 affected-tools table: ready surfaces cross-repo blockers of LOCAL issues only).
        * Lookup node_idx in graph.node_map(); if absent, skip (no blockers).
        * Iterate graph.inner_graph().neighbors_directed(node_idx, Outgoing).
        * Track (a) any open blocker exists, (b) which open blockers are cross-repo.
        * If (a) is true (issue WOULD be filtered out by step-6), add every cross-repo OPEN blocker to the BTreeSet.
      - Build Option<CrossRepoRefs>: None if BTreeSet empty, else Some with omitted=Vec::from(BTreeSet) and summary=Some(format!("{n} cross-repo blocker(s) excluded local issue(s) from ready set")).
   d. Extend #[cfg(test)] mod tests with hermetic unit tests covering: (i) empty issues → None, (ii) all-local blockers → None, (iii) single cross-repo OPEN blocker on local issue → Some, (iv) cross-repo blocker already Closed → None (issue would still be ready or not affected), (v) duplicate cross-repo blocker across two local issues → single entry, (vi) determinism: BTreeSet ordering yields lex-sorted omitted.
3. Edit crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:
   a. Keep the existing cache-freshness check. After the is_fresh/rebuild branch, read cache.get_issues() and cache.get_graph() (both may be None on stale=true).
   b. Compute cross_repo_refs = if stale { None } else if let (Some(issues), Some(graph)) = (cache.get_issues().await, cache.get_graph().await) { compute_cross_repo_refs(&issues, &graph, state.github.owner(), state.github.repo()) } else { None }.
   c. Wire cross_repo_refs into ReadyResult { issues, count, stale, cross_repo_refs }.
4. Add integration tests in crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs under an existing Ready block or after it. Two tests (spec-mandated):
   - ready_no_cross_repo_blockers_cross_repo_refs_is_none: fixture with only local issues and local edges → result.cross_repo_refs.is_none() AND json serialization elides the key (mirror dep_cycles line 3420-3424 assertion style).
   - ready_cross_repo_open_blocker_populates_cross_repo_refs: fixture with local issue #1, cross-repo blocker other/repo#99 as IssueState::Open, edge #1 → other/repo#99 → #1 filtered out → ready_set excludes #1 AND result.cross_repo_refs = Some({ omitted: ["other/repo#99"], summary: non-empty containing "cross-repo" and "ready" }). Use new_mock() + push_fetch_graph_data + state_with_mock (mirrors dep_cycles_mixed_cycle_populates_cross_repo_refs setup, lines 3458-3543). Handler must be invoked through the public pathway — either call the ready handler on UnblockServer::new(state) OR invoke cache.update() + replicate the handler inline if the #[tool] wrapper is hard to drive from tests. dep_cycles tests call handle_dep_cycles directly, suggesting the ready tool should also expose a pub async fn handle_ready(state, params) helper — check existing server.rs pattern vs ready handler. If not yet factored, extract handle_ready in this bead (the dep_cycles pattern is the current house style per sibling unblock-29p.12 scope notes).
5. Run: cargo fmt --check --all, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, cargo doc --no-deps --workspace. All must be green.
6. Write commit per project standard: feat(mcp): add cross_repo_refs to ReadyResult (SPEC §11.4). Include "API: ReadyResult gains cross_repo_refs: Option<CrossRepoRefs>" line (library-crate API-change-tracking rule; unblock-mcp is a binary crate but ReadyResult is part of the MCP response schema — conservative: include API: note anyway since downstream MCP clients consume this shape).

Risks:
- Handler refactor scope creep: spec §7.1 step 9 requires the handler to have access to both issues AND graph, not just ready_set. The current ready handler in server.rs:817-861 only reads cache.get_ready_set(). The patch must add cache.get_issues() + cache.get_graph() reads. Two corner cases: (a) if cache returns Some ready_set but None issues/graph that should never happen (cache.update() writes all three atomically per cache.rs:122-128), but defensively treat it as stale=false + cross_repo_refs=None with a tracing::warn!. (b) stale=true path already sets cross_repo_refs=None (no data to inspect) — double-check this is consistent with SPEC §11.4 "None iff omitted empty" (it is — empty omitted → None).
- Step-6-vs-tool-layer-filter scope confusion: the spec (SPEC §7.1 flow step 9, line 985) is explicit — cross_repo_refs captures blockers of issues filtered by §3.3 step 6 ONLY. Tool-layer filters (priority, milestone, label, agent, issue_type, defer_until) are POST-ready-set and MUST NOT contribute to cross_repo_refs. The natural place to compute this is therefore in the handler BEFORE calling filter_ready_set, using the full cache.get_issues() set and cache.get_graph() — NOT a post-filter over the projection. This is why filter_ready_set signature must stay untouched.
- InProgress vs Blocked issue status handling: §3.3 filter 2 excludes InProgress/Deferred/Closed at the graph level. These issues are NOT "filtered out by step 6" — they are filtered out by steps 4-5. They MUST NOT contribute cross_repo_refs (otherwise a claimed issue whose blocker is cross-repo would spuriously add a ref that was not actually keeping it out of the ready set). The unit test suite must cover this: an InProgress issue with a cross-repo open blocker → cross_repo_refs stays None for that issue.
- Local-issue scoping: only LOCAL issues (config-repo owner+repo match) can be "filtered out of the local ready set" in a meaningful cross-repo sense. Cross-repo issues are not in the configured-repo ready set in the first place (compute_ready_set iterates all issues but IssueSummary.number projects to bare u64 scoped to configured repo). The helper MUST skip issues whose (owner,repo) differs from configured — otherwise a cross-repo issue filtered by its own blocker would pollute the ref set.
- Determinism invariant 14: BTreeSet<String> keyed by QualifiedId::Display already lex-sorts. Do NOT switch to HashSet — that would break Invariant 14 and the spec-mandated property test goal 6 (SPEC §13.3).
- skip_serializing_if elision: the JSON-layer assertion in the "none" integration test (mirror dep_cycles line 3420-3424) is load-bearing — if a future contributor forgets the #[serde] attribute, that test will catch the regression. Include it explicitly.
- Test mock owner/repo collision: existing non-dep_cycles ready tests use qid() = ("test","repo",N) but new tests must use ("acme","widgets",N) since new_mock() hardcodes "acme"/"widgets" and state.github.owner()/repo() is what the helper compares against. Do not change the existing test_issue() helper (that would cascade into many unrelated tests); create a ready-specific fixture mirroring dep_cycles_fixture_issue / dep_cycles_cross_repo_fixture in the test file, OR reuse mock_issue (integration.rs:66) which already uses ("acme","widgets",N).
- Handle_ready extraction: if the ready tool handler body is inlined in server.rs (as it is, lines 817-861), integration tests cannot call it directly without booting UnblockServer. Two options: (A) extract pub async fn handle_ready(&ServerState, ReadyParams) -> Result<ReadyResult, ErrorData> in tools/ready.rs, then the server.rs #[tool] shim just forwards — matches the dep_cycles house style; (B) drive the test through UnblockServer::new(state).ready(Parameters(params)).await (heavier, but no refactor needed). title: dep_remove: removed=true technically dishonest when cache is cold and edge never existed
description:
Finding from QA of unblock-29p.10 (dep_remove tool implementation).

When handle_dep_remove is invoked before the first cache warm-up, the warm-cache edge-existence guard is skipped entirely. GitHub's removeIssueDependency mutation is idempotent-ish — removing a non-existent edge is not an error on their side — so the mutation completes cleanly.

However, the returned DepRemoveResult.removed = true is technically untruthful when the edge never existed. The caller receives a success signal with no indication that the edge may not have been present.

This is documented in the dep_remove.rs module docstring as an acceptable trade-off: spec §8.5 describes only the warm-cache contract.

Action: decide on one of three options:
  (a) Eagerly warm the cache before the guard check to eliminate the cold-cache bypass entirely.
  (b) Lower confidence on 'removed' when the cache is cold (e.g., add a cache_was_cold flag or use a distinct status).
  (c) Promote the cold-cache posture explicitly into spec §8.5 as an accepted known limitation.

Risk: agents interpreting removed=true as confirmation may make incorrect downstream decisions (e.g., treating a dependency as absent when it was never tracked).

title: Resolve race-window silent default in reopen handler post-mutation cache rebuild
description:
File: crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/reopen.rs, lines 405-418

When the post-mutation cache rebuild returns a non-empty cache but the reopened issue is absent from it (a short race window), the handler silently defaults blocked=false and returns status="ready". This conflicts with the R3 module-doc posture, which explicitly argues against defaulting to blocked=false when the graph state is unknown.

Two remediation paths exist:
1. Strengthen the R3 module-doc to explicitly carve out this race path as an accepted exception, documenting the reasoning.
2. Treat the missing-issue case the same as a rebuild failure: surface a 503-style "cache inconsistent, please re-run show" error, consistent with how other rebuild failures are handled.

Discovered during code review of unblock-29p.9 (reopen MCP tool implementation).

comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:

# Context

This bead implements SPEC Decision 1 (arbitrated 2026-04-17, frozen in docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md §11.1 and docs/plans/01-plan-mcp-foundation.md Task 02.02): migrate three DomainError variants from bare `u64` to `IssueRef` for cross-repo-aware error reporting.

The spec + plan patches have ALREADY LANDED (commit 1d55800 on branch chore/unblock-eos-spec-plan-alignment per architect summary at unblock-eos comment #2). This bead is the implementation: touch only crates/unblock-core and call sites in unblock-mcp + unblock-github.

# Root cause / scope (three variants, NOT two)

The bead description mentions only CircularDependency + DuplicateDependency, but spec §11.1:1680 ALSO changes IssueBlocked from `blockers: Vec<u64>` to `blockers: Vec<IssueRef>`. Plan Task 02.02:305 and the BREAKING CHANGE footer template at plan:314-322 explicitly list all THREE variants. This bead must cover all three to satisfy the plan contract:

- crates/unblock-core/src/errors.rs:41-47 — IssueBlocked { number: u64, blockers: Vec<u64> } → blockers: Vec<IssueRef>
- crates/unblock-core/src/errors.rs:80-87 — CircularDependency { source: u64, target: u64 } → source/target: IssueRef
- crates/unblock-core/src/errors.rs:89-97 — DuplicateDependency { source: u64, target: u64 } → source/target: IssueRef

Bead description says 'Extend CircularDependency/DuplicateDependency'; that is a pointer — the authoritative spec at §11.1:1680-1686 and plan at :297-337 expand to all three. Flag to orchestrator: update bead title/description to include IssueBlocked, OR confirm that IssueBlocked was intentionally moved elsewhere. Per feedback_bead_description_not_spec.md, we follow the spec/plan.

# Files to edit

## Core type + tests (the BREAKING CHANGE)

- crates/unblock-core/src/errors.rs
  - :7-9 module docblock variant list — no change to count (still 11 in this bead; +2 from unblock-6xj are independent), but if 29p.25 lands FIRST it should not pre-list 6xj's variants. Do NOT touch the count prematurely.
  - :23-112 enum definition — change the three variants' field types.
  - :41 `#[snafu(display("Issue #{number} is blocked by: {blockers:?}"))]` — MUST replace `{blockers:?}` Debug formatter with a Display-based renderer (spec §11.1:1729 'Implementer trap' paragraph). Under `Vec<IssueRef>` the Debug formatter renders `[Local(1), Local(2)]` which leaks variant names; swap for a helper (e.g. format the blockers via a pre-built string joining each via IssueRef::Display) or a custom display function. See Approach step 2 for the concrete pattern.
  - :80 display format `#{source} → #{target}` — works byte-for-byte if IssueRef::Display is used, because IssueRef::Local(n) renders as `#n` (crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs:527). For CircularDependency/DuplicateDependency the change is therefore just the field type — display string is unchanged; `{source}` now calls `IssueRef::Display` instead of `u64::Display`. SURPRISE: the current format string has LITERAL `#` prefix before `{source}`, so naive `{source}` interpolation on IssueRef::Local would double-up to `##1`. Two resolutions:
    (a) Remove literal `#` from the format string (spec-preferred: let IssueRef::Display own the prefix; renders `#1 → #2` for Local, `acme/widgets#1 → #2` for mixed).
    (b) Keep literal `#` and invent a new helper that renders only the number for Local and `owner/repo#n` for CrossRepo — ugly and asymmetric.
    Pick (a). The Local-only Display test at :215-227 asserts substrings `'1'`, `'2'`, `'cycle'` (NOT the literal `#`), so (a) passes those. Same logic for DuplicateDependency at :89-97 and test at :229-240. Confirm by running `cargo test -p unblock-core` before committing.
  - :120-137 status_code mapping — no change; HTTP codes unchanged in spec §11.1:1699-1706 for these three variants.
  - :215-240 existing Local-only Display tests — MUST continue to pass byte-for-byte (spec §11.1:1718-1727). Rewrite test setup to pass `IssueRef::Local(n)` into the selector:
    ```
    let err = CircularDependencySnafu {
        source: unblock_core::types::IssueRef::Local(1),
        target: unblock_core::types::IssueRef::Local(2),
    }.build();
    ```
    Substring assertions (`'1'`, `'2'`, `'cycle'`) survive unchanged. Same for DuplicateDependency. For IssueBlocked at :164-175 (blockers asserts only `'10'`) — also survives.
  - :215-240 — ADD new cross-repo Display tests (plan :331 mandates this):
    - `circular_dependency_cross_repo_display` — asserts result contains `'acme/widgets#1'`.
    - `duplicate_dependency_cross_repo_display` — asserts result contains `'acme/widgets#4'`.
    - `issue_blocked_cross_repo_display` — asserts result contains `'acme/widgets#1'` in the blockers list (verifies the Display-based renderer replacing `{blockers:?}`).
  - :264-313 all_variants_implement_error_trait test — update CircularDependencySnafu / DuplicateDependencySnafu / IssueBlockedSnafu builders to construct IssueRef instead of u64.

## Call sites (compile-error driven — the type change forces each update)

- crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs:899-911 (add_blocked_by local path, DuplicateDependencySnafu) — `issue_number` and `blocked_by_number` are both `u64` scoped to configured repo. Replace `source: issue_number` with `source: IssueRef::Local(issue_number)` and target likewise. Semantically equivalent; Display preserved.
- crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs:1504-1516 (add_blocked_by_refs cross-repo source arm, THE TODO site) — remove the TODO comment at :1504-1509. The `source` is `unblock_core::types::IssueRef::CrossRepo { owner: source_owner, repo: source_repo, number: source_number }` pattern-matched at :1470-1473. Pass the full `source` reference (clone it) into `DuplicateDependencySnafu { source: source.clone(), target: IssueRef::Local(n) }`. The blocker variable `n` (from `blocker_number_in_source_repo`) is local-in-source-repo — it lives in the source's own `owner/repo`, so technically it should be `IssueRef::CrossRepo { owner: source_owner.clone(), repo: source_repo.clone(), number: n }` to be fully accurate (blocker IS in the source's cross repo, not the configured repo). Review which form the spec's Display example expects — §11.1:1720 only shows Local/mixed cases. Recommend: use `IssueRef::CrossRepo { owner: source_owner.clone(), repo: source_repo.clone(), number: n }` for target because that is where it actually lives; then IssueRef::Display renders `acme/widgets#{source_number} → acme/widgets#{n}` unambiguously.
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:1314-1321 (depends handler, local-local CircularDependency) — both `source_number` and `target_number` are `u64` destructured from `IssueRef::Local` match arm (:1295-1298). Wrap each in `IssueRef::Local(*source_number)` / `IssueRef::Local(*target_number)`. Alternative: build the QualifiedId once per side and construct `IssueRef::Local` directly since the pattern already asserts Local-ness. Display byte-for-byte preserved.
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:49 — `use unblock_core::errors::{CircularDependencySnafu, IssueClosedSnafu};` — no change (the selector name is unchanged; only its field types change).
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/claim.rs:89-104 (IssueBlockedSnafu emission) — `open_blockers: Vec<u64>` is built at :90-95 by mapping `candidate.blocked_by.iter()` (`Vec<RelatedIssue>`, fields `{ number: u64, title, state }` — crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs:371-378). GitHub's `trackedByIssues` connection only surfaces SAME-REPO blockers (spec §8.2 cascade semantics + mutations.rs:1480-1491 confirming comment), so these blockers are all local to the configured repo. Change the type annotation at :90 from `Vec<u64>` to `Vec<IssueRef>` and the closure at :94 from `|r| r.number` to `|r| IssueRef::Local(r.number)`. Add `use unblock_core::types::IssueRef;` at the top if not present.

- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/claim.rs:248-274 — blocked_issue_returns_issue_blocked_error: asserts `msg.contains('blocked by')` and `msg.contains('5')`. Survives — '5' is the issue number, 'blocked by' is in the static portion of the Display format.

No direct snapshot tests on the exact error message strings exist beyond the substring assertions listed above. The Display byte-for-byte contract is therefore safe to land as a minimal change.

# Approach (for rust-supervisor)

## Step 1 — type migration in errors.rs

1a. Add `use unblock_core::types::IssueRef;` where needed (the enum is already in the same crate, so just reference `crate::types::IssueRef`).
1b. Change the three variant field types:
    - `IssueBlocked.blockers: Vec<u64>` → `Vec<IssueRef>`
    - `CircularDependency.source: u64 / target: u64` → `IssueRef / IssueRef`
    - `DuplicateDependency.source: u64 / target: u64` → `IssueRef / IssueRef`
1c. Change the snafu display attribute for CircularDependency from:
    `"Circular dependency: adding #{source} → #{target} creates cycle"`
    to:
    `"Circular dependency: adding {source} → {target} creates cycle"`
    (remove the literal `#` prefix; IssueRef::Display owns it.) Same for DuplicateDependency at :90.
1d. Replace the `{blockers:?}` Debug formatter in IssueBlocked display. Snafu does NOT support custom formatters inside `#[snafu(display(...))]` directly, but it DOES support calling free functions. Two acceptable patterns:
    - (preferred) Pre-build the blockers string via a private helper `fn render_blockers(blockers: &[IssueRef]) -> String` and interpolate it; snafu Display accepts method calls: `#[snafu(display("Issue #{number} is blocked by: {}", render_blockers(blockers)))]`.
    - (alternative) Replace the `Snafu` derive's auto-generated `Display` for this variant by using a manual `impl Display for DomainError` with a match arm for IssueBlocked. Snafu supports opting one variant out via `#[snafu(whatever)]` or by writing the whole Display by hand.
    Pick the helper-function approach — less invasive.
1e. Update status_code — NO change; HTTP codes unchanged.

## Step 2 — update existing tests (errors.rs:140-313)

2a. Rewrite the three builders to construct IssueRef::Local values. Every `source: 1_u64` becomes `source: IssueRef::Local(1)`.
2b. Substring assertions survive as-is.
2c. Add THREE new cross-repo tests (one per variant) asserting the CrossRepo Display form contains `'owner/repo#n'`.

## Step 3 — update call sites

3a. mutations.rs:905-910 (add_blocked_by local) — wrap in `IssueRef::Local(…)`.
3b. mutations.rs:1510-1515 (add_blocked_by_refs cross-repo source) — remove the TODO comment; pass `source.clone()` for the source field and build CrossRepo for target (living in the source's repo).
3c. server.rs:1314-1321 (depends CircularDependency) — wrap `*source_number` and `*target_number` in `IssueRef::Local(…)`.
3d. claim.rs:89-103 — change `open_blockers: Vec<u64>` to `Vec<IssueRef>`; map via `IssueRef::Local(r.number)`.

## Step 4 — quality gate + commit

4a. `cargo fmt --check --all`
4b. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
4c. `cargo test --workspace`
4d. `cargo doc --no-deps --workspace`
4e. Commit message MUST use the verbatim `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer template from docs/plans/01-plan-mcp-foundation.md:314-322 (NOT an `API:` line; per CLAUDE.md Pub API Change Tracking a type-level signature change is a BREAKING CHANGE footer per Conventional Commits).

# Risks

1. **Cross-repo target in DuplicateDependency (mutations.rs:1510-1515).** The `blocker_number_in_source_repo` is `Some(n)` iff the blocker matches source's own owner/repo (:1492-1499). This means the duplicate target LIVES in the source's cross repo, NOT the configured repo. Construct target as `IssueRef::CrossRepo { owner: source_owner.clone(), repo: source_repo.clone(), number: n }` — do NOT use `IssueRef::Local(n)`, which would render misleadingly as `#n` and suggest the configured repo.
2. **IssueBlocked Display format choice.** Spec §11.1:1724 explicitly permits two forms (`"[#1, #2]"` or `"#1, #2"`). Pick ONE and commit with a test. Recommend the second (no square brackets) — cleaner, matches the bracketless format of CircularDependency/DuplicateDependency. Document choice in the new test name.
3. **Snafu Display helper invocation.** Snafu display attributes support `{expr}` expression interpolation (e.g. `{blockers.len()}`), but passing a mutable reference or a complex helper can hit snafu macro quirks. If the helper approach fails at compile, fall back to `#[snafu(display(…))]` with manual `write!` via `#[snafu(display = "write!(f, \"...\")"))]` syntax. Reference snafu docs or look at existing snafu Display usages in unblock-github/src/errors.rs for examples.
4. **Order of landing vs unblock-6xj.** 6xj ADDS two new variants (InvalidIssueRef, CrossRepoAccessDenied) without touching the three variants 29p.25 changes — merge order is commutative. However 6xj's error-side wiring at server.rs:1229-1245 is adjacent to 29p.25's server.rs:1314-1321 change; rebase the later-landing bead onto main. No logical conflict.
5. **Literal `#` removal in display string.** If the spec/plan anywhere else references `"adding #{source}"` literally in a test or doc, changing to `"adding {source}"` could break. Audit confirmed: only the errors.rs declaration and spec §11.1:1722 example strings reference this, and both are consistent with the proposed change. No external contract break.
6. **candidate.blocked_by type preservation.** RelatedIssue.number stays `u64` — we are NOT changing the core types or graphql mapping. Only the error field type changes. If RelatedIssue is later extended to carry owner/repo (for cross-repo blocker support on same-repo issues — not in scope here), the mapping at claim.rs:94 trivially evolves to `IssueRef::CrossRepo` when applicable. Document assumption.
7. **BREAKING CHANGE footer enforcement.** CLAUDE.md 'Pub API Change Tracking' section requires the footer for library-crate pub API shape changes. Missing the footer will pass CI but violate the policy — reviewer MUST catch. The plan at :311-324 provides the verbatim template.

title: Add InvalidIssueRef and CrossRepoAccessDenied error variants per spec §11.1
description:
**SPEC CONTRACT (MANDATORY):** Before implementing, read `docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md` §11.1 (Domain errors) and §11.4 (Cross-Repo Response Contract), plus `docs/plans/01-plan-mcp-foundation.md` Task 02.02 and GAP-14. This bead description is a pointer only — NOT a spec substitute. Acceptance criteria must be verified against spec + plan files, not assumed from this description.

---

Spec docs/specs/01-spec-mcp-foundation.md §11.1 lists two error variants that are missing from crates/unblock-core/src/errors.rs: InvalidIssueRef (HTTP 400 — malformed IssueRef string) and CrossRepoAccessDenied (HTTP 403 — token lacks access to a referenced cross-repo). Currently both paths fall back to ValidationSnafu / IssueNotFoundSnafu, which conflates distinct failure modes for MCP clients and breaks spec conformity. Surfaced during research for unblock-29p.4 (depends cross-repo support) where IssueRef parsing and cross-repo fetches now run on both source and target.
acceptance_criteria: 1. InvalidIssueRef variant added to UnblockError with HTTP 400 mapping. 2. CrossRepoAccessDenied variant added with HTTP 403 mapping. 3. IssueRef parsing failures (FromStr) propagate as InvalidIssueRef across MCP tools (depends, dep_remove, show, etc.). 4. Cross-repo fetch_issue_ref calls returning 403 from GitHub map to CrossRepoAccessDenied. 5. cargo fmt + clippy + test green. 6. ≥1 unit test per variant covering the mapping path.

5. Quality gate: cargo fmt --check --all; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace; cargo doc --no-deps --workspace.

6. Commit discipline: the unblock-core library's pub API grows (two new variants + two new snafu context selectors). Per CLAUDE.md Pub API Change Tracking, this is ADDITIVE — use an 'API:' body line, NOT 'BREAKING CHANGE:'. Suggested: 'feat(core): add InvalidIssueRef and CrossRepoAccessDenied DomainError variants' with body 'API: DomainError gains InvalidIssueRef { input: String } (HTTP 400) and CrossRepoAccessDenied { owner: String, repo: String } (HTTP 403) variants per SPEC §11.1 and plan GAP-14.c.'

Applied at fetch_issue_in_repo (graphql.rs:236-242, gated on owner/repo != configured — local 403 stays as GitHubApi) and resolve_issue_ref cross-repo arm (mutations.rs:1069-1072).

Findings:
- [GOOD] crates/unblock-github/src/graphql.rs:462-492 — reducer partitions FORBIDDEN-typed errors BEFORE reducing to messages, using the wire-safe 'type' field per user decision 2026-04-17. This is the semantically correct approach (not substring-sniffing on free-text messages) and is well-documented inline.
- [GOOD] crates/unblock-github/src/graphql.rs:236-242 — fetch_issue_in_repo correctly gates the classifier on 'owner != self.owner() || repo != self.repo()' so local-repo 403s stay as GitHubApi. CrossRepoAccessDenied is cross-repo-semantic by name; local 403 would be semantically wrong. This gating is explicitly regression-tested at graphql.rs:2193-2219 (fetch_issue_in_repo_local_403_stays_as_github_api).
- [GOOD] crates/unblock-github/src/errors.rs:46-67 + graphql.rs:482-487 — introducing Error::GitHubGraphQLForbidden as a named wire-form variant (status_code 403) is an architectural improvement beyond the research scope: the classifier can pattern-match on the variant rather than inspecting a collapsed message bag. Correctly tagged as additive API change in commit 2c389b7.
- [GOOD] Test coverage is thorough and exercises actual HTTP flow via wiremock (not hand-rolled mocks). The mixed FORBIDDEN+other-typed reducer test (graphql.rs:2094-2126) correctly asserts FORBIDDEN is authoritative — only forbidden messages survive.
- [GOOD] crates/unblock-mcp/src/errors.rs:80-101 — doc table updated from '400, 404, 409, 412, 422' to '400, 403, 404, 409, 412, 422' and a prose paragraph now explains WHY 403 is a named arm (regression-guard framing per plan GAP-14.c Decision 2 #3). Matches the commit message.
- [GOOD] crates/unblock-core/src/errors.rs:7-10 — module docblock bumped from 11 to 13 variants with both new names appended, closing sibling unblock-eos.18 docblock drift as promised in the DECISION comment.
- [SUGGESTION] crates/unblock-github/src/graphql.rs:469-481 — the new partition loop uses unwrap_or_default().to_owned() for 'message' which produces an empty string, then the else branch filters it via '!message.is_empty()'. The pre-existing code used filter_map which was cleaner. For FORBIDDEN-typed entries with missing/empty messages the current code still pushes an empty string into forbidden_messages; Display would then render 'GitHub GraphQL FORBIDDEN: '. This is unusual in practice (GitHub always sends a message with FORBIDDEN) but not guarded against. Non-blocking — trivial to tighten with a .filter(|m| !m.is_empty()) on the forbidden_messages push too.
- [SUGGESTION] crates/unblock-github/src/graphql.rs:236-242 — the match expression (Ok(v) => v, Err(err) if <cond> => return, Err(err) => return) is correct but slightly awkward compared to an early-return pattern. A helper binding like 'let is_cross_repo = owner != self.owner() || repo != self.repo();' followed by '.map_err(|err| if is_cross_repo { classify_cross_repo_fetch(err, owner, repo) } else { err })?' would read more linearly. Non-blocking — style only.

Security: PASS — no new input surfaces; InvalidIssueRef carries user-supplied strings but those are already user-authored inputs (tool params) and are only surfaced in error messages back to the same caller. CrossRepoAccessDenied carries owner/repo which originate from user input (IssueRef parsed from tool params); same principle applies. No injection risk — the error Display is not used in any query construction.

Performance: PASS — no regressions. The reducer partition loop is O(n) in errors.len() (same as the previous filter_map reduction); the classifier is a single pattern match. No new allocations in the hot path; a Vec<String> split into two Vec<String> is a wash.

Tests: PASS — 11 new unit tests covering Display + status_code for both new DomainError variants, MCP 400/403 → INVALID_PARAMS routing, GitHubGraphQLForbidden Display/status, GraphQL reducer FORBIDDEN partition (three wiremock tests), classify_cross_repo_fetch (four edge cases), and fetch_issue_in_repo cross-repo upgrade (three wiremock tests including the local-403-stays-as-GitHubApi scoping guard). Full workspace suite passes at 754 / 0 / 3.

Verdict: APPROVE

title: RedactedConfig field-drift risk: silent secret leak when Config gains new fields
description:
File: crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:164-180

RedactedConfig manually lists every Config field in its fmt() implementation. If crates/unblock-core/src/config.rs gains a new field, RedactedConfig will silently drop it from the Debug output and no test will fail — potentially re-introducing a secret leak by omitting redaction of the new field.

The fix is to destructure &*self.0 with all field names at the top of RedactedConfig::fmt() (e.g. let Config { token, owner, repo, .. } = &*self.0;). With an exhaustive destructure pattern (no ..), adding a new field to Config will cause a compile error in RedactedConfig::fmt() until the redaction wrapper is explicitly updated to handle it.

title: No live dyn-dispatch runtime coverage for Arc<dyn GitHubApi> in CI
description:
QA gate for unblock-uzo ran all 141 lib tests successfully, but live GitHub integration tests require GITHUB_TOKEN and were skipped entirely. The Arc<dyn GitHubApi> trait-object path introduced in unblock-uzo is exercised at compile time via the blanket impl on GitHubClient, but no runtime test demonstrates a real handler call going through dyn dispatch end-to-end.

This means CI currently provides no signal that the trait-object dispatch layer works correctly at runtime — errors in the vtable path, object-safety regressions, or future dyn-incompatible changes would not be caught automatically.

Mitigation: add a CI job (or local make target) that runs integration tests with a recorded fixture or wiremock backing the GitHubApi trait, so the dyn dispatch path is exercised in CI without requiring a real GITHUB_TOKEN. MockGitHubClient (introduced in the same epic) is the natural backing implementation for this.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: CI exercises Arc<dyn GitHubApi> only at compile time. crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:134 stores client as Arc<dyn GitHubApi>, but every runtime test in crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs and e2e_workflow.rs constructs ServerState through test_server_state() using the real GitHubClient and is gated on has_github_token() (see ~25 'GITHUB_TOKEN not set — skipping' guards, e.g. integration.rs:68,112,709,1401). With no token in CI all of those return early, so the dyn-dispatch vtable path is never invoked at runtime in .github/workflows/ci.yml. MockGitHubClient exists (crates/unblock-github/src/mock.rs) but is gated behind the 'test-hooks' Cargo feature (unblock-github/Cargo.toml:26, lib.rs:36), and unblock-mcp/Cargo.toml:34 dev-dependencies does NOT pull unblock-github with features=['test-hooks'], so the mock is not even compiled into the unblock-mcp test binary today.

Files:
  - .github/workflows/ci.yml:24-35 — test-mcp job runs 'cargo test -p unblock-core -p unblock-github -p unblock-mcp' with no features and no GITHUB_TOKEN; this is where the new job/step belongs.
  - crates/unblock-mcp/Cargo.toml:34 — dev-dependencies block; needs unblock-github = { path='../unblock-github', features=['test-hooks'] } so MockGitHubClient is visible to mcp tests.
  - crates/unblock-github/src/mock.rs — MockGitHubClient with CallCounts/Stubs already implements GitHubApi; ready to back Arc<dyn GitHubApi>.
  - crates/unblock-github/src/lib.rs:36-39 — re-export of mock module gated on test-hooks.
  - crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:124-155 — ServerState definition; client field is Arc<dyn GitHubApi>. Construction in tests/common/ currently uses real GitHubClient.
  - crates/unblock-mcp/tests/common/ — test_server_state() helper; consider adding a sibling helper test_server_state_with_mock(mock: Arc<MockGitHubClient>) that builds ServerState from a mock and a fake Config (no token required).
  - crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs:1412-1425 — example of an existing test that purposefully uses the concrete client; new mock-backed tests should be a NEW file (e.g. tests/dyn_dispatch.rs) gated on cfg(feature='test-hooks') to keep concerns separate.

Approach:
  1. Wire unblock-github with features=['test-hooks'] under unblock-mcp [dev-dependencies] in crates/unblock-mcp/Cargo.toml so MockGitHubClient is available to mcp test targets.
  2. Add a small test helper (e.g. crates/unblock-mcp/tests/common/mock_state.rs) that constructs a ServerState with client: Arc::new(MockGitHubClient::new(...)) as Arc<dyn GitHubApi> and a stub Config (no env vars, no network).
  3. Add a new test file crates/unblock-mcp/tests/dyn_dispatch.rs containing at least one #[tokio::test] per representative tool handler family (e.g. ready, show, create, claim) that: pre-loads the mock stub queue with a deterministic Result, invokes the handler through ServerState, then asserts both the handler output AND that mock.calls().<method>() incremented — proving the call traversed the vtable rather than being inlined out.
  4. Ensure these tests do NOT depend on GITHUB_TOKEN — they must run unconditionally in CI.
  5. Update .github/workflows/ci.yml test-mcp job to run 'cargo test -p unblock-mcp --features unblock-github/test-hooks' (or add --all-features on the unblock-mcp package) so the new tests are compiled and executed. Confirm with the user whether to add a separate CI step or fold into existing test-mcp.
  6. Document the new local make target or just-target equivalent in README/AGENTS so contributors can run the dyn-dispatch suite without a token.

Risks:
  - Feature unification: enabling unblock-github/test-hooks as a dev-dependency on unblock-mcp may cause Cargo to also compile mock.rs when running 'cargo build -p unblock-mcp' if the workspace uses a unified feature resolver. Verify with resolver='2' (edition 2024 default) — should be dev-only, but double check that production binary is not bloated.
  - Mock drift: MockGitHubClient defaults to Error::MockNotStubbed for un-stubbed methods (mock.rs:20-31). Tests that touch handlers calling multiple API methods must stub each one or expect a deterministic error — keep tests narrowly scoped.
  - Choosing which handlers to cover: covering all 13 handlers risks duplicating mock setup. Pick 3–4 that collectively touch the highest-value GitHubApi methods (graph fetch, mutation, project resolution) to keep maintenance bounded. Decision point — surface to user if scope unclear.
  - Object-safety regression detection: a compile-time test (already implicit in ServerState's Arc<dyn GitHubApi>) is necessary but not sufficient — runtime call is what proves vtable correctness. The new tests must actually invoke through Arc<dyn GitHubApi>, not through Arc<MockGitHubClient> directly.
  - The user's global rule forbids unilateral simplifications — if any handler under test transitively requires a real network call that the trait does not abstract, STOP and ask the user rather than mocking around it.

Related tests:
  - crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs — token-gated end-to-end suite; NOT to be modified, used as the reference for what the new mock suite mirrors.
  - crates/unblock-mcp/tests/e2e_workflow.rs — same; token-gated.
  - crates/unblock-mcp/tests/common/ — shared helpers; new mock helper lives here.
  - crates/unblock-github/src/mock.rs — unit tests inside mock module exercise the mock itself but do not exercise the mcp handler dispatch path.
  - New: crates/unblock-mcp/tests/dyn_dispatch.rs — to be created as part of implementation.

title: Implement MockGitHubClient with AtomicUsize call counters
description: Add a MockGitHubClient impl of GitHubApi in unblock-github (gated behind a test-hooks feature or test-only module). Each method records invocations in an AtomicUsize counter. Provide configurable response stubs (success/error) per method. Expose getter API for call counts. Must be plausibly callable for every trait method since Arc<dyn GitHubApi> requires the whole surface — methods not exercised by tests can return a deterministic default or NotImplemented error.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: Feature bead — implement MockGitHubClient as a second impl of the GitHubApi trait defined in crates/unblock-github/src/api.rs (closed prerequisite unblock-2dz). The trait surface is fully fixed and stable: 6 sync accessors + 30 async methods, all Send+Sync, async-trait based. The mock must provide AtomicUsize call counters per method and configurable response stubs, while remaining compilable for ALL 36 methods (since Arc<dyn GitHubApi> demands the whole surface). Downstream consumer is unblock-hd9 which only needs counters on resolve_project_info() and field_ids() — but every other method must still exist with a deterministic default or NotImplemented error.

Files:
- crates/unblock-github/src/api.rs:42-201 — authoritative trait surface; mirror every signature exactly (params, lifetimes, return types). Note &str vs String, Vec<String>, Option<u64>, &IssueRef, &FieldValue, &CreateViewParams.
- crates/unblock-github/src/api.rs:209-396 — blanket impl on GitHubClient, useful as a method-by-method checklist.
- crates/unblock-github/src/lib.rs:28-31 — module declaration site; new mock module must be added here (gated).
- crates/unblock-github/Cargo.toml:9-26 — feature/dev-deps gating point. No [features] table exists yet; needs to be added if test-hooks feature is chosen.
- crates/unblock-github/src/projects.rs:37,103,116,128,179,194 — types referenced by trait (ProjectFieldIds, SetupReport, SetupStatus, OwnerType, RestField, ProjectView, OwnerProject, CreatedProject, ProjectInfo, FieldValue, CreateViewParams) — all needed for method signatures and stub construction.
- crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs — CreateIssueParams, Milestone types referenced by trait.
- crates/unblock-github/src/errors.rs — Error type for Result returns; needs a variant suitable for NotImplemented stubs (audit existing variants; may need to reuse a generic one rather than add new).
- unblock_core::types — Issue, IssueRef, BlockingEdge for fetch_issue/fetch_graph_data/resolve_issue_ref/add_blocked_by_ref signatures.

Approach:
1. DECISION POINT — gating strategy. Bead description says 'test-hooks feature OR test-only module'. Two options:
   a) Cargo feature 'test-hooks' in unblock-github/Cargo.toml, with #[cfg(feature = "test-hooks")] on the module. This lets downstream crates (unblock-mcp tests) depend on unblock-github with features = ["test-hooks"] in dev-dependencies. This is the option that actually unblocks unblock-hd9 (reconcile.rs lives in unblock-mcp and needs the mock as a dev-dep).
   b) #[cfg(test)] module — only visible inside unblock-github's own test compilation. This does NOT work for unblock-hd9 since the mock must be reachable from unblock-mcp tests.
   RECOMMENDATION: Option (a) — add [features] test-hooks = [] to unblock-github/Cargo.toml. This is the only option that satisfies the downstream consumer; the bead phrasing 'OR' is misleading. Confirm with user before proceeding.
2. Create crates/unblock-github/src/mock.rs gated by #[cfg(feature = "test-hooks")]. Re-export from lib.rs the same way (pub mod mock; pub use mock::MockGitHubClient).
3. Define MockGitHubClient struct holding:
   - One AtomicUsize per trait method (36 counters). Group into a CallCounts substruct for ergonomics, accessed via mock.call_count("resolve_project_info") OR typed getters like mock.resolve_project_info_calls(). DECISION POINT: string-keyed HashMap<&'static str, AtomicUsize> vs named fields. Named fields are type-safe and zero-cost; HashMap is more concise but loses compile-time guarantees. Recommend named fields. Confirm with user.
   - Configurable response stubs via Mutex<Option<Result<T, Error>>> or fn pointers/Box<dyn Fn>. For unblock-hd9 the two methods that matter are field_ids() (returns Option<ProjectFieldIds>) and resolve_project_info() (returns Result<ProjectInfo, Error>). Stub storage strategy needs user input — simplest is per-method Mutex<VecDeque<Result>> for queued responses, fallback to a default.
   - Sync accessor backing fields: owner: String, repo: String, project_number: Option<u64>, api_base_url: String. Constructor MockGitHubClient::new(owner, repo, project_number) with sane defaults.
4. Implement #[async_trait] impl GitHubApi for MockGitHubClient covering ALL 36 methods. For methods not exercised by any current test, increment the counter then return either a queued stub or Error::<some variant> with message 'MockGitHubClient: <method> not stubbed'. Audit errors.rs first to find or add a suitable variant — DO NOT silently return Ok defaults that could mask missing stubs in future tests.
5. Public getter API: per-counter accessors (e.g. fn resolve_project_info_calls(&self) -> usize) using Ordering::SeqCst loads. Consider a reset_counters() helper for test isolation.
6. Add a small unit test inside mock.rs (still under cfg test-hooks) verifying counter increments and stub queueing for at least field_ids and resolve_project_info — these are the two unblock-hd9 will assert against.
7. Verify cargo build -p unblock-github (no feature) and cargo build -p unblock-github --features test-hooks both succeed; then cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings; cargo test --workspace --all-features.
8. Commit with conventional 'feat:' message and an API: footer noting MockGitHubClient is added behind test-hooks feature (additive, non-breaking).

Risks:
- async_trait Box allocation per call (already noted in unblock-b6b.149 by review of unblock-2dz). Not a blocker for mock correctness but may matter if tests loop hot — acceptable.
- Stub storage with Mutex inside an async trait method: must use std::sync::Mutex (not tokio) and never hold across await; the trait methods don't await internally so this is fine. Avoid tokio::sync::Mutex to keep the mock cheap.
- Error::<variant> selection for NotImplemented stubs — must NOT add a panicking default. If errors.rs has no fitting variant, prefer adding a new Error variant gated by cfg(feature="test-hooks") or reuse the most generic existing one (audit needed in step 4).
- Send+Sync requirement: every field must be Send+Sync. AtomicUsize, Mutex<T: Send>, String, Option<u64> all qualify. Box<dyn Fn> stub closures would need Send+Sync+'static bounds.
- Trait surface drift: if a future bead extends GitHubApi, the mock will fail to compile until updated. This is desirable (forces updates) — call it out in module docs.
- The bead description allows 'NotImplemented error' for unused methods, but choosing string identifiers for counter keys would let typos slip through. Strongly prefer named accessors.
- DECISION POINTS flagged above (gating strategy, counter storage style, stub storage shape, error variant choice) — per CLAUDE.md global rule 'Never simplify unilaterally', supervisor MUST surface these to the user before implementing.

Related tests:
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/reconcile.rs:1234,1253 (fix_mode_failed_field_ids_is_deduped, fix_mode_failed_resolve_project_info_is_deduped) — downstream consumers in unblock-hd9; not modified in this bead but the mock API shape must support their needs (call_count for those two methods, ability to stub Err return).
- crates/unblock-github/tests/integration.rs — pre-existing network-gated integration tests; mock should not break them.
- New tests inside mock.rs itself should cover counter + stub mechanics for at least field_ids and resolve_project_info.

title: prime tool: max_per_category=0 and stale_threshold_hours=0 boundary values not validated
description: The prime tool does not validate zero values for its two parameters: max_per_category=0 produces empty category lists (no issues returned) and stale_threshold_hours=0 marks every claimed issue as stale regardless of actual claim age. Both behaviours are surprising and likely unintentional from a caller perspective. There is no error, warning, or documentation to signal that zero is a special or invalid value. Risk: an agent or integration calling prime with default-zero initialised params would receive misleading output (empty ready list, all in-progress issues flagged stale) and could make incorrect decisions. Consider adding validation (reject zero with an error), clamping (treat 0 as 'use default'), or at minimum documenting the boundary behaviour explicitly.

Root cause: PrimeParams (prime.rs:41-49) only has stale_threshold_hours and max_per_category fields. PRD §6.3 (prd line 348) specifies an 'agent' optional filter parameter. The agent field already exists on IssueSummary (types.rs:331), PrimeIssueSummary (prime.rs:115), and StaleIssueSummary (prime.rs:174), but there is no input filter to scope prime output by agent.

- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/prime.rs:241-353 — handle_prime() needs agent filter applied to each category before truncation
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/prime.rs:373-497 — categorise_issues() could accept agent filter, OR filtering can happen post-categorisation in handle_prime
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/prime.rs:306-312 — PrimeCounts must reflect filtered counts (not pre-filter totals) when agent is provided

2. In handle_prime(), after categorise_issues() returns, apply agent filter to in_progress, ready, and blocked Vec<IssueSummary> using the same is_none_or pattern as ready.rs:149-155 (s.agent.as_deref() == Some(filter.as_str()))
3. For stale Vec<StaleIssueSummary>, filter on its agent: Option<String> field the same way

PRD says 'Recently completed — closed in last 24h for continuity' which suggests global context, so filtering completed may not be needed. If filtered, CompletedIssueSummary needs an agent field added.
5. For hotspots Vec<HotspotSummary>, these are structural graph properties (most-blocking nodes) — filtering by agent would lose their meaning. Skip agent filter on hotspots.
6. Compute PrimeCounts AFTER filtering so counts reflect what the agent actually sees
7. Update server.rs tool description to mention agent parameter

- CompletedIssueSummary has no agent field (prime.rs:188-204) — if we want to filter completed issues by agent, we need to add agent to that struct and populate it from Issue.agent during categorise_issues(). Decision needed on whether completed should be filtered.

- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/ready.rs:360 — filter_by_agent test as reference pattern
