- The From<http::Response<T>> impl on reqwest::Response requires T: Into<Body>. String implements Into<Body> so this works. Verified in reqwest 0.12.28 source (async_impl/response.rs:456).

title: Wire or remove empty_field_ids() dead-code helper to broaden project-field vtable coverage
description: The helper `empty_field_ids()` at `crates/unblock-mcp/tests/dyn_dispatch.rs:115` is annotated `#[allow(dead_code)]` and is not exercised by any test. Currently, handlers silently skip project-field updates when `field_ids()` returns `None`, which keeps mocks small but leaves the `field_ids = Some(...)` code path untested across `setup`, `claim`, `close`, `update`, and `depends` handlers. The refactoring-supervisor skipped resolution per the global no-unilateral-simplification rule.
design: The helper already constructs a fully populated `ProjectFieldIds` with empty option maps, so wiring it in is low-effort. Broadening coverage here would validate vtable dispatch through the project-field mutation path, which is currently a gap in the dyn-dispatch test suite.
acceptance_criteria: Either wire `empty_field_ids()` into one or more tests that exercise the `field_ids = Some(...)` branch for at least the project-field-update-capable handlers (setup/claim/close/update/depends), or delete the helper if the team decides the coverage is not worth the complexity. The chosen path must be justified and reflected in a comment or commit message.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: The helper empty_field_ids() at dyn_dispatch.rs:84-98 constructs a ProjectFieldIds with empty option maps and is annotated #[allow(dead_code)]. It is not used by any test. Currently, mock field_ids() returns None by default (mock.rs:453 unwrap_or(None)), so all handlers skip the project-field update branch (the if-let-Some(field_ids) blocks). This means the dyn-dispatch tests never exercise the field_ids=Some(...) code path for claim, close, depends, create, or update handlers.

Files:
- crates/unblock-mcp/tests/dyn_dispatch.rs:84-98 — the dead helper
- crates/unblock-mcp/tests/dyn_dispatch.rs:309 — claim is the only test asserting field_ids() call count (expects None)
- crates/unblock-github/src/mock.rs:402 — push_field_ids() stub method
- crates/unblock-github/src/mock.rs:446-454 — field_ids() impl returning None by default
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:890 — claim handler field_ids branch
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:1031 — close handler field_ids branch
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:1275 — depends handler field_ids branch
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:1515 — create handler field_ids branch
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:1767 — update handler field_ids branch (guarded by has_project_updates)

Approach:
RECOMMENDATION: Wire it in rather than delete. The cost is low and the coverage gain is real.

1. For claim, close, depends, create: push mock.push_field_ids(Some(empty_field_ids())) PLUS push_resolve_project_info(Ok(...)) and push_get_project_item_id(Ok(item_id)) to enter the Some(...) branch fully. Since empty_field_ids() has empty option maps, update_field() will NOT be called (options.get() returns None), keeping mocks minimal.

2. For update: the current test passes all None params so has_project_updates=false and field_ids() is never reached. To test the Some branch, add a variant test (e.g., update_with_project_fields_dispatches_through_dyn_vtable) that passes priority=Some or story_points=Some and stubs field_ids+resolve_project_info+get_project_item_id. story_points would actually call update_field since it does not use option maps.

3. For setup: NOT applicable — setup calls set_field_ids(), not field_ids(). The acceptance criteria mention setup but it does not consume field_ids().

4. Assert call counts: assert field_ids()=1, resolve_project_info()=1, get_project_item_id()=1 in each wired test. For update with story_points, also assert update_field()=1.

5. Remove #[allow(dead_code)] from empty_field_ids() once wired.

Risks:
- The mock uses a queue for field_ids (pop_front), so the push must happen before the handler call. Handlers that call field_ids() multiple times (e.g., close with cascade) would need multiple pushes.
- close handler has two field_ids() call sites: one for the main issue (line 1031) and one for cascaded unblocked issues (line 1117). The cascade branch is only entered when closing actually unblocks something, which the current close test does not trigger (empty graph). So only one push needed for the existing close test.
- update handler guards field_ids() behind has_project_updates, so the existing no-op update test would NOT exercise it at all — a new test variant is needed.

Related tests:
- crates/unblock-mcp/tests/dyn_dispatch.rs — all affected tests are here
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/reconcile.rs:1206-1292 — reconcile tests already exercise field_ids=None path with assertions (good reference pattern)

Root cause (cosmetic): Manual Debug impl for ServerState at crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:156-169 prints the github field as the static literal "<dyn GitHubApi>". This conveys nothing about the concrete type behind the trait object (production GitHubClient vs test MockGitHubClient vs future backends). Because Debug is intentionally not a supertrait of GitHubApi (crates/unblock-github/src/api.rs:43 — '#[async_trait] pub trait GitHubApi: Send + Sync'), std::fmt::Debug cannot be forwarded through the trait object; the placeholder was the minimum viable solution chosen in unblock-uzo.

Approach options (DO NOT pick unilaterally — present to user):

Option A — Add 'fn debug_label(&self) -> &'static str' on GitHubApi with default impl
  - Add to the trait (crates/unblock-github/src/api.rs) a new required-with-default method:
      fn debug_label(&self) -> &'static str { std::any::type_name::<Self>() }
  - std::any::type_name works for non-'static? No — it requires 'Self: ?Sized' is fine but type_name::<Self>() on a trait method where 'self: &Self' and Self is the concrete impl type resolves to the concrete name at each impl site. This gives "unblock_github::client::GitHubClient" / "unblock_github::mock::MockGitHubClient" automatically without per-impl work.

  - SEMVER: additive (default-method addition on a public trait). Note 'API:' in commit body.

Option B — Add required 'fn debug_label(&self) -> &'static str' WITHOUT default
  - Each implementor must return a stable, curated label (GitHubClient -> "GitHubClient", MockGitHubClient -> "MockGitHubClient").
  - PROS: stable, curated strings; no reliance on type_name's unstable format.
  - CONS: BREAKING for any downstream impl of GitHubApi (none today outside the workspace, but the trait is 'pub' in unblock-github — CLAUDE.md requires BREAKING CHANGE footer for 'incompatible' changes; adding a required method without a default is breaking). Two-line edit in both impls.
  - SEMVER: breaking.

Option C — DebugLabel wrapper type carried on ServerState itself
  - Add 'pub github_label: &'static str' (or 'Cow<'static, str>') to ServerState, set at construction time in main.rs (crates/unblock-mcp/src/main.rs:43) to "GitHubClient" and in test helpers to "MockGitHubClient".
  - Debug impl reads self.github_label.
  - PROS: no change to unblock-github's public API (lower semver blast radius); label is explicit and controlled by the constructor; no dependency on std::any::type_name.
  - CONS: every ServerState construction site gains a new required parameter (main.rs:34-49, server.rs:2195-2210 in-file test helper, crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs test helper, crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/reconcile.rs test helper, crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/prime.rs test helper, crates/unblock-mcp/tests/common/mod.rs); forgetting to update one would fail to compile (acceptable). Label can drift from the actual concrete type.
  - SEMVER: ServerState is in the binary crate (unblock-mcp) so no semver concern per CLAUDE.md Pub API Change Tracking scope note.

Option D — Debug-print the Arc's inner vtable pointer or strong count
  - Use Arc::as_ptr(&self.github) as a raw address plus strong_count.
  - PROS: trivial; no API change anywhere.
  - CONS: not runtime-useful as described in the bead ('the actual concrete type behind the trait object, or a meaningful marker' — a pointer is not a marker).
  - REJECT unless user explicitly asks for pointer output.

Recommendation: Option A is the smallest-touch solution and matches the bead's first suggested option verbatim ('Include a type tag or marker string that indicates the concrete type when known, e.g. using std::any::type_name'). However, per CLAUDE.md 'Never do a decision to simplify the solution' and 'Mandatory: No Unilateral Decisions', the supervisor MUST surface A/B/C to the user and let them pick before implementing.

The current ServerState Debug impl at crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:161 prints '&self.config' unredacted, meaning any '{:?}' of ServerState leaks the token to logs. This is a pre-existing issue unrelated to this bead's 'cosmetic' scope, but any supervisor touching Debug for ServerState should ask the user whether to also file/fix a token-redaction issue. title: Consider zero-copy borrow in TracingCapture::output() to avoid buffer clone
description:
File: crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs, line 2094

TracingCapture::output() currently clones the entire captured buffer via String::from_utf8(). For current test usage this is fine, but if the helper is adopted more widely (e.g. capturing large output or called many times in a single test run), the clone will allocate a new String on every call.

A zero-copy alternative would return a &str borrow over the internal buffer instead of an owned String, avoiding the allocation entirely. This would require the return type to carry a lifetime tied to &self, but that is a straightforward change given the helper is only used in test code.

title: Add exit-code assertion before stdout check in subprocess tests
description:
File: crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/prime.rs, lines 1207-1227

The two subprocess tests do not assert output.status.success() before inspecting stdout. If the subprocess fails for an unrelated reason (e.g., binary not found, env issue, panic), stdout is empty and the assertion fails with a misleading error message that gives no signal about the actual failure root cause.

Adding an explicit exit-code check before the stdout assertion — for example:

    assert!(output.status.success(), "subprocess failed: {:?}", output);

— would surface the real failure immediately and improve debuggability. Not a blocker: the current assertion already includes stdout content in its error message, so failure is recoverable, just noisier to diagnose.

title: Empty string agent filter not validated in prime.rs and ready.rs
description:
When the agent filter parameter is set to an empty string (""), no validation rejects it in either prime.rs or ready.rs. An empty string would match no issues since no issue has agent=Some(""), resulting in silent empty results rather than an error or all-issues behavior.

This is consistent across both files:
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/prime.rs lines 311-324
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/ready.rs lines 149-155

The behavior is functionally harmless but may confuse callers who expect either a validation error or all-issues fallback when no agent filter is meaningfully provided. Two remediation paths are available:
1. Treat empty string as None (filter disabled, return all issues) — consistent with most CLI/API conventions
2. Document explicitly that agent="" always returns an empty set — acceptable if intentional

Both files should be updated consistently since they share the same filtering logic.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: The agent field on PrimeParams (prime.rs:56) and ReadyParams (ready.rs:36) is Option<String>. Serde deserializes agent:"" as Some(""), not None. No validation rejects or normalises empty strings. In prime.rs:375-379, the retain() calls compare s.agent.as_deref() == Some(""), which matches nothing since no issue carries agent=Some(""). In ready.rs:149-155, the is_none_or() closure activates because the Option is Some, and again matches nothing. Result: silent empty output instead of error or all-issues fallback.

Files:
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/prime.rs:42-57 — PrimeParams struct, agent field definition (no serde attribute or validation)
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/prime.rs:293-315 — existing validation block for stale_threshold_hours and max_per_category (pattern to follow)
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/prime.rs:375-379 — agent filter application via retain() (the code that silently filters everything out)
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/ready.rs:23-43 — ReadyParams struct, agent field definition (same gap)
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/ready.rs:149-155 — agent filter in filter_ready_set() via is_none_or() (same gap)

Approach (recommended: treat empty as None):
1. In prime.rs handle_prime(), after the existing stale_threshold_hours/max_per_category validation block (~line 315), add: let agent = params.agent.as_deref().and_then(|s| if s.trim().is_empty() { None } else { Some(s) }); Then use this local agent variable instead of params.agent at line 375.
2. In ready.rs filter_ready_set(), normalise the agent filter the same way before applying it at line 149. Could extract a tiny helper fn normalise_filter(opt: &Option<String>) -> Option<&str> to DRY.
3. Consider applying the same normalisation to the other string filters (issue_type, priority, milestone, label) for consistency — they have the identical gap. This is optional scope expansion.
4. Add unit tests: (a) prime_params_agent_empty_string_treated_as_none, (b) ready_filter_agent_empty_string_returns_all. Mirror existing agent_filter_none_returns_all and filter_by_agent tests.

Risks:
- If any caller intentionally passes agent="" expecting empty results, this changes behaviour. Extremely unlikely since that would be useless.
- Normalising other string filters (issue_type, priority, milestone, label) is the same pattern but expands scope. Recommend doing it in the same PR for consistency but can be a follow-up bead if preferred.
- Using .trim() means whitespace-only strings like " " also become None — this is the right behaviour.

title: ClientDetector: skip env fallback when clientInfo.name is empty
description:
File: crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:1965

ClientDetector::resolve(Some(&agent_client)) is called even when client_info.name is empty. This means the env-based fallback detection path is never reached when clientInfo is present but has an empty name string.

Current behavior: returns Unknown("") instead of potentially detecting the agent kind via environment variables.

Suggested fix: guard the resolve call with an is_empty() check on client_info.name, so that when the name is empty, the code falls through to env-based detection.

This is not a blocker — the current behavior satisfies the acceptance criteria wording of the reviewed task. However, the guard would make the detection more robust for clients that send a clientInfo object with a blank name field.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: In ClientDetector::resolve_with (detection.rs:119), when mcp_client is Some but name is empty, AgentClient::kind() calls from_client_name("") which returns Unknown(""). The .map() wraps this in Some(Unknown("")), so .or_else() never falls through to env-based detection. The env fallback path is unreachable whenever clientInfo is present, regardless of whether the name is meaningful.

Files:
- crates/unblock-core/src/detection.rs:115-123 — resolve_with contains the short-circuit logic; the .map() on line 120 unconditionally converts Some(client) into Some(kind), blocking the or_else env fallback
- crates/unblock-core/src/client.rs:53-68 — from_client_name returns Unknown(name) for unrecognised names including empty string
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:2011-2017 — initialize handler builds AgentClient from request.client_info.name without checking for empty, then passes Some(&agent_client) to resolve

Approach:
1. In resolve_with (detection.rs:119-123), add a filter to skip empty client names before mapping. Change line 119 from mcp_client.map(AgentClient::kind) to mcp_client.filter(|c| !c.name.is_empty()).map(AgentClient::kind). This keeps the fix at the detection layer where the resolution logic lives, rather than in server.rs.
2. Add a test in detection.rs: resolve_with(Some(empty_name_client), env_with_claude) should return ClaudeCode (env fallback), not Unknown("").
3. Add a test in detection.rs: resolve_with(Some(empty_name_client), no_env) should return Unknown("unknown") (the standard unknown sentinel), not Unknown("").

Risks:
- Minimal risk. The filter only changes behavior when name is empty, which is already a degenerate case returning Unknown("").
- Downstream code that pattern-matches on Unknown("") specifically would break, but no such code exists in the codebase.
- The existing test resolve_with_mcp_unknown_overrides_env (line 269) uses a non-empty name so it is unaffected.

Related tests:

title: Document string-sort invariant on closed_at in prime completed category
description:

An inline comment should be added at the sort expression explaining that the string comparison is valid because `closed_at` values are guaranteed to be UTC RFC3339 formatted timestamps. This prevents future maintainers from misreading the sort as a bug, and provides an early warning if the timestamp format were ever to change.

title: reconcile: resolve_repair_context does not cache resolution failures
description:
In `crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/reconcile.rs`, the `resolve_repair_context` function does not cache resolution failures. When a repairable drift item fails to resolve (e.g., a failing API call), subsequent repairable drift items will retry the same resolution path rather than short-circuiting.

This is harmless in practice since failing API calls return fast, but it is a missed optimisation opportunity. The failure result could be cached so that repeated retries are skipped for the same context key within a single reconcile run.
close_reason: QA passed: tests/build/lint clean, all acceptance criteria met, minor suggestions tracked as unblock-b6b.146 and unblock-b6b.147

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/reconcile.rs:212-230 resolve_repair_context() only memoizes success. On failure it pushes an error to report.errors and returns None without recording the failure in ctx. The next repairable drift item in apply_repairs (lines 252-...) calls resolve_repair_context again, which re-invokes state.client.field_ids().await and state.client.resolve_project_info().await, and pushes another duplicate error string into report.errors. Result: O(N) redundant API calls and N duplicate error messages where N = number of repairable drift items in a single reconcile run.

Files:
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/reconcile.rs:212-230 — resolve_repair_context, the function to change. Current signature returns Option<&'a (ProjectFieldIds, ProjectInfo)> with ctx: &'a mut Option<(...)>.
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/reconcile.rs:247 — repair_context binding in apply_repairs; type must change to a tri-state (Unresolved | Failed | Resolved).
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/reconcile.rs:259, 285 — call sites that must handle the new tri-state and not push duplicate errors.

Approach:
1. Introduce a small private enum RepairContext { Unresolved, Failed, Resolved((ProjectFieldIds, ProjectInfo)) } in reconcile.rs (do NOT collapse to Option<Result<...>> just to be terse — this is a chore/optimisation, keep it explicit).
2. Change repair_context binding at line 247 from Option<(...)> to RepairContext::Unresolved.
3. Rewrite resolve_repair_context to:
   - return Some(&(field_ids, project_info)) when Resolved,
   - return None when Failed (without re-running API calls and without pushing a duplicate error),
   - on first Unresolved attempt: try field_ids + resolve_project_info; on success transition to Resolved and return Some; on failure push the error exactly once, transition to Failed, return None.
4. Update both call sites (lines 259, 285) — signature stays the same (Option<&(...)>), so the match arms in apply_repairs are unchanged.
5. Add or extend a unit test in reconcile.rs tests covering: a reconcile run with >=2 repairable drift items where the mock client fails field_ids/resolve_project_info, and assert that (a) field_ids/resolve_project_info are called exactly once and (b) report.errors contains the failure message exactly once.

Risks:
- Behavior change: today report.errors gets N copies of the failure string; after the fix it gets 1. Any caller/test that asserts on the count of error messages must be updated. Worth confirming with the user whether the de-duplication is desired (it almost certainly is, but it is an observable change).
- The 'Failed' state is per reconcile run only — repair_context is a local in apply_repairs, so the next reconcile call still retries. That is the intended scope per the bead description ('within a single reconcile run').
- Lifetime: returning &'a (ProjectFieldIds, ProjectInfo) from inside an enum variant works with a match arm returning a reference to the tuple inside Resolved — straightforward but make sure the borrow checker is satisfied without cloning.

Related tests:
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/reconcile.rs — existing tests at the bottom of the file (search for #[cfg(test)] / mod tests) cover apply_repairs paths and use a mock GitHub client; the new test should live alongside them and reuse the existing mock infrastructure. No tests currently assert on the duplicate-error behavior, so nothing should break, but the new test must be added to lock in the fix.

title: snafu error type visibility widened to pub in errors.rs — track for future narrowing
description:
File: crates/unblock-mcp/src/errors.rs, line 22

The snafu-derived error type visibility was widened from pub(crate) to pub. This is acceptable today because unblock-mcp is a binary crate with no downstream consumers, so the public surface has no external reach.

If unblock-mcp is ever split into a lib + bin target (e.g., to enable integration testing via the library interface), the overly broad visibility could become part of an unintended public API. Track this so narrowing back to pub(crate) is not forgotten if that structural change occurs.
close_reason: Option B: documented rationale inline in errors.rs (lib/bin split requires pub visibility, zero external consumers). QA passed.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: crates/unblock-mcp already has BOTH a [lib] and [[bin]] target (Cargo.toml lines 15-22). main.rs is a thin bin wrapper that imports from the unblock_mcp library crate: 'use unblock_mcp::errors::{ClientInitSnafu, ConfigLoadSnafu, RuntimeSnafu, TransportSnafu}' (main.rs:19) and returns 'unblock_mcp::errors::BootstrapError' (main.rs:23). Because bin and lib are separate crates from the visibility standpoint, snafu selectors must be 'pub' — 'pub(crate)' would hide them from main.rs. So the structural precondition the bead anticipated has already occurred; the finding's premise ('acceptable today because unblock-mcp is a binary crate with no downstream consumers') is outdated. There are still no EXTERNAL downstream consumers of unblock-mcp (no other workspace crate depends on it, not published), so the practical leak risk remains zero.

Files:
- crates/unblock-mcp/Cargo.toml:15-22 — defines both [lib] (src/lib.rs) and [[bin]] (src/main.rs) targets, root cause of why pub is required
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/errors.rs:21-23 — '#[snafu(visibility(pub))]' on BootstrapError; selectors ConfigLoadSnafu, ClientInitSnafu, TransportSnafu, RuntimeSnafu are generated pub
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/main.rs:19,23,25,35,64,67 — bin-crate uses of the pub selectors and BootstrapError via the unblock_mcp:: library path
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/lib.rs — library entry point, exposes pub mod errors

Approach (options — DO NOT pick unilaterally, surface to user):
  Option A (narrow the surface): Move bootstrap into the library as a 'pub async fn run() -> Result<(), BootstrapError>' in lib.rs. Reduce main.rs to '#[tokio::main] async fn main() { unblock_mcp::run().await }' with BootstrapError -> process exit mapping. Then selectors can drop to 'pub(crate)' and BootstrapError itself can become 'pub(crate)' since main.rs no longer references it directly. This is the principled fix and also centralizes bootstrap for integration tests via the lib.
  Option B (accept + document): Leave 'pub' as-is, add a crate-level doc note in errors.rs explaining the bin/lib split rationale, and close the bead as wontfix. Justified because unblock-mcp has no external consumers and is not published.
  Option C (status quo): Keep the bead open as a future-tracking reminder (the original intent) but update the description to reflect that the lib/bin split has already happened.

Risks:
- Option A: moving tokio runtime bootstrap between main and lib must preserve behavior (tracing_subscriber::fmt().init() must still run on the real process; ServerState construction, signal handling, exit codes must be unchanged). Tests currently may not exercise run(); need to avoid regressing stdio transport wiring.
- Option A: tracing_subscriber::init() is global — if run() is also called from an integration test, double-init will panic. Gate with try_init or keep subscriber setup in main.rs.
- General: narrowing visibility is a small win here because there are no external consumers, so any refactor cost should be weighed against near-zero risk of leakage.

Related tests:
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/errors.rs:83-235 — unit tests for github_error_to_mcp; do not touch BootstrapError visibility and would not be affected by Option A.
- No existing integration test depends on lib bootstrap; none need updates for Option B or C.

Recommendation: surface the three options to the user before acting. Per project rule, do not unilaterally simplify by choosing wontfix.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
REVIEW:
Acceptance: PASS — the bead asked to track the pub visibility so narrowing is not forgotten if a lib/bin split occurred. Investigation revealed the split has already happened, making 'pub' structurally required. The commit documents this rationale inline in errors.rs (lines 22-33), pointing back to the bead. title: Replace format!("{:?}", ...) enum serialization with Display or serde in show tool
description:
File: crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs, lines 428-429

The show tool currently uses format!("{:?}", some_enum) to serialize enum values for agent-facing output. Rust Debug formatting produces output like SomeVariant rather than a stable, human-readable string.

If enum variants ever gain fields (e.g., Status::InProgress { since: DateTime }), Debug output will include field names and types in an ad-hoc format that agents cannot reliably parse.

Consider implementing Display or deriving serde::Serialize for consistent, contract-stable agent-facing output.
close_reason: QA passed. Display impls replace Debug-based enum serialization across show/ready/prime tools; wire format byte-identical; locking tests added. Minor exhaustiveness-guard follow-up tracked as unblock-b6b.171.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: The show tool (and several other tools) serialize enum values for MCP output using format!("{:?}", e), which relies on Rust Debug formatting. These enums (Status, Priority, ReadyState, IssueState in crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs lines 188-263) already derive serde::Serialize but do NOT implement std::fmt::Display. If a variant ever gains fields, Debug output silently changes shape and breaks the agent-facing contract. Note: bead description cites lines 428-429, but code has drifted — actual show-tool sites are crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:708,709,712,718 and crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/show.rs:133 (ShowRelatedIssue::from, state field).

Files:

- crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs:285+ — IssueType already implements Display; use the same pattern (match arms writing the canonical variant name).
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:708-718 — show tool builds ShowIssue using format!("{:?}", ...) for status, priority, ready_state, state.
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/show.rs:124-135 — ShowRelatedIssue::From<&RelatedIssue> uses format!("{:?}", r.state); the doc comment explicitly says 'produced by Debug formatting to preserve the exact byte shape' — update this comment when switching to Display.

- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/ready.rs:100-101,146 — same pattern; line 146 uses format!("{:?}", s.priority).eq_ignore_ascii_case(filter) for priority filtering, which demonstrates the contract (strings like "P0", "P1"). Display impl must preserve these exact tokens.
- crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/prime.rs:142-143,545,697-698 — same pattern; out of scope per bead title (show tool) but worth flagging for a follow-up since it shares the same contract risk.

Approach:
1. In crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs, add impl fmt::Display for each of Status, Priority, ReadyState, IssueState. Each match arm must write the exact variant identifier string currently produced by Debug (e.g., Status::InProgress => "InProgress", Priority::P0 => "P0", ReadyState::NotReady => "NotReady", IssueState::Open => "Open") so the wire contract is byte-identical.
2. Add unit tests in types.rs confirming Display output matches the current Debug strings for every variant, so future field additions will not silently drift.
3. Replace format!("{:?}", issue.{status,priority,ready_state,state}) at crates/unblock-mcp/src/server.rs:708,709,712,718 with issue.<field>.to_string() (or format!("{}", ...)).
4. Replace format!("{:?}", r.state) at crates/unblock-mcp/src/tools/show.rs:133 with r.state.to_string(); update the doc comment on ShowRelatedIssue::from (lines 125-128) — it currently says 'produced by Debug formatting to preserve the exact byte shape'.
5. Decide with the user whether this bead's scope covers ready.rs (lines 100-101, 146) and prime.rs (lines 142-143, 545, 697-698). Bead title says 'show tool' — per project rule against unilateral simplification, do NOT silently extend scope; flag it and ask.
6. Run cargo fmt, cargo clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, cargo doc --no-deps.

Risks:
- Wire contract stability: any Display string that differs even by case from the current Debug output will break agent integrations and the ready.rs priority filter at line 146 (eq_ignore_ascii_case mitigates case but not spelling). Mitigation: dedicated unit tests asserting exact string equality with the pre-change Debug output.
- Scope creep: fixing only show but leaving ready/prime creates inconsistent wire formats across tools sharing the same enums. Raise this with the user before acting.
- serde alternative: deriving #[serde(...)] + serde_json::to_string would pin the contract but produces quoted JSON strings ("\"InProgress\""). Display is the cleaner fit here; document the choice in the commit.
- Public API impact: adding Display impls to pub enums in unblock-core is additive — note 'API: Display impl added for Status/Priority/ReadyState/IssueState' in the commit body per CLAUDE.md Pub API Change Tracking.

description:
File: crates/unblock-mcp/tests/integration.rs, lines 190-265

The tests for include_deps=false and include_comments=false replicate the conditional branch logic inline rather than exercising the actual show tool handler end-to-end. As written, they verify that an if/else on a boolean works as expected, not that the handler correctly threads the flag through to the GitHub fetch layer.

This is an acknowledged trade-off: full handler invocation requires a live GITHUB_TOKEN. The gap should be documented so future contributors know these paths are not covered by the integration suite and can add targeted tests when a test-token environment is available.

Then call again with Some(true) and assert dependency_tree.is_some().
  5. Delete the two original tests (show_include_deps_false_* and show_include_comments_false_skips_comments) once the replacements pass — they currently provide zero coverage of production code.

title: Extract shared check_rest_response() helper in projects.rs and mutations.rs
description:
The rate-limit + error handling pattern for REST responses is repeated verbatim in multiple locations across the unblock-github crate:

- crates/unblock-github/src/projects.rs: detect_owner_type(), list_rest_fields(), and create_view()
- crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs (same pattern also present)

A shared check_rest_response() helper function should be extracted to reduce duplication and ensure consistent error handling across all REST call sites. Any future fix or improvement to error handling or rate-limit logic would only need to happen in one place.
close_reason: QA passed. Refactor extracted check_rest_response() helper, all tests/build/lint green. Suggested unit tests tracked in unblock-b6b.164.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: The 429 rate-limit + non-2xx error pattern is duplicated across ~14 REST call sites in unblock-github. Each site does: let status = response.status(); if 429 -> RateLimited; if !success -> read text + GitHubApi error. The repetition is verbatim except some sites add an extra branch (404 -> IssueNotFound, or 422 special-case).

Files (all under crates/unblock-github/src/):
- graphql.rs:382-401 — base GraphQL execute() also uses the same 429+non-success pattern (REST-shaped check on a graphql HTTP response). Already exposes pub(crate) parse_rate_limit_reset() at line 429 — the new helper belongs in this same module.
- projects.rs:990-1007 (detect_owner_type), 1066-1083 (list_rest_fields), 1156-1173 approx (create_view) — pure pattern, no extra status branches.
- mutations.rs:168-185 (create_issue) — pure pattern.
- mutations.rs:264-285 (close_issue), 323-345 (reopen_issue), 387-410 (update_issue title/body), 447-470, 505-, 576-, 641-, 700-, 765- — same pattern PLUS an extra '404 -> IssueNotFoundSnafu { number }' branch interleaved between the 429 check and the !is_success check.
- mutations.rs:1227, 1250-1253 — create_label flow with a 422 special-case (label already exists). Should NOT be migrated to the helper without preserving 422 handling.

Approach:
  1. In crates/unblock-github/src/graphql.rs (next to parse_rate_limit_reset), add:
       pub(crate) async fn check_rest_response(response: reqwest::Response) -> Result<reqwest::Response, Error>
     Behavior: extract status; if 429 -> RateLimitedSnafu via parse_rate_limit_reset; if !is_success -> read .text() and return GitHubApiSnafu { status, message }; otherwise return Ok(response) so callers can still .json() it.
  2. Migrate the pure call sites first (no 404/422 branches): graphql.rs:382 (self-use), projects.rs x3, mutations.rs:168 (create_issue). Replace ~17 lines per site with 'let response = check_rest_response(response).await?;'.
  3. For the close/reopen/update/etc. issue-mutation sites that have a 404 branch: do the 404 check FIRST (before calling the helper), since the helper would otherwise convert 404 into a generic GitHubApi error and lose the IssueNotFound semantic. Pattern becomes:
       let status = response.status();
       if status.as_u16() == 404 { return Err(IssueNotFoundSnafu { number }.build().into()); }
       let response = check_rest_response(response).await?;
     This is safe because 404 is not 429 and not 2xx; ordering only matters relative to which error variant wins.
  4. Do NOT migrate create_label at mutations.rs:1227/1250 — it has a 422 'already exists' branch that needs custom handling. Leave as-is or open a follow-up bead.
  5. Do NOT migrate graphql.rs execute() in the same commit if the goal is strictly REST — but the pattern is identical and the helper lives in graphql.rs, so it is a reasonable bonus dedup. Recommend including it.

Risks:
- Ordering risk on 404 sites: if helper is called before the 404 check, IssueNotFound becomes GitHubApi(404). Mitigation: explicit 404 check before helper call (step 3).
- Response consumption: reqwest::Response is move-only and .text() consumes it. The helper must take 'response: Response' by value and return Ok(response) on success so callers can still parse JSON. Do not try to borrow.
- Visibility: helper should be pub(crate) (matches parse_rate_limit_reset). It is not part of the public API surface.
- Tracing/spans: existing sites do not log inside the error branches; the helper preserves that. No #[instrument] needed on the helper.
- Pub API: this is internal refactor only — no library pub API changes, no API: footer required per CLAUDE.md.

Related tests:
- crates/unblock-github/src/errors.rs already covers RateLimitedSnafu and GitHubApiSnafu construction (lines 195-310). No changes needed there.
- Any integration tests that exercise mutations/projects against mocked HTTP (search for 'mockito' or 'wiremock' under crates/unblock-github) should still pass unchanged because the externally-visible error behavior is preserved.
- Recommend adding a focused unit test for check_rest_response covering: (a) 200 returns Ok(response) with body still readable, (b) 429 returns RateLimited with reset_at parsed, (c) 500 returns GitHubApi with text body, (d) 404 returns GitHubApi (i.e., callers wanting IssueNotFound must branch before calling).

title: Derive REQUIRED_FIELD_NAMES from REQUIRED_FIELDS to eliminate drift risk

title: Optimize allocation in fetch_existing_fields()
description:
File: crates/unblock-github/src/projects.rs

fetch_existing_fields() contains a small allocation that is not on a hot path but could be optimized. The allocation is not a correctness issue and carries no runtime risk at current usage levels, but is worth addressing as a low-priority cleanup to keep allocations lean across the GitHub client.

This finding was surfaced during code review of unblock-467.6 (Projects V2 field management implementation).
close_reason: QA passed. All 3 target clones eliminated, quality gate green.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: fetch_existing_fields() in crates/unblock-github/src/projects.rs contains several avoidable allocations in the per-node parsing loop (lines 657-685). Three categories:

1. projects.rs:663 — `serde_json::from_value(node_value.clone())` clones the entire JSON subtree for each field node before deserializing. The clone exists because the outer iteration borrows `nodes` (`&Vec<Value>`) via `fields_connection.get("nodes").and_then(as_array)`, so `node_value` is `&Value`. The clone is the largest allocation here (clones id, name, dataType, nested options array with id+name strings).

2. projects.rs:672-676 — inner loop clones `opt.name` and `opt.id` because `field.options` is iterated by reference (`for opt in options` over `&Vec<OptionNode>`). These clones exist only because `field` is not destructured/moved.

3. projects.rs:679 — `field.name.clone()` used as the HashMap key because the struct-literal below still references `field.id` and `option_map`. `field` is only partially consumed, so `name` must be cloned. Avoidable with a destructuring let.

Files:
- crates/unblock-github/src/projects.rs:608-700 — fetch_existing_fields(), the target function
- crates/unblock-github/src/projects.rs:326-344 — FieldNode and OptionNode definitions (both derive Deserialize, fields are owned String)

Approach:
1. Take ownership of the nodes array by using `fields_connection["nodes"].take()` or by matching on a mutable reference and calling `Value::take()` per node. Simplest: bind `let response = self.graphql(...).await?;` already owned, then do `let nodes = response["data"]["node"]["fields"]["nodes"].take();` — but since response subfields aren't mutable by default through indexing, use `response.pointer_mut("/data/node/fields/nodes")` or restructure to navigate with `get_mut`. Alternative and cleaner: serde-deserialize the full page into a typed struct (FieldsPage { nodes: Vec<FieldNode>, page_info: PageInfo }), eliminating manual Value walking entirely and avoiding all per-node clones.
2. In the loop, destructure the owned FieldNode: `let FieldNode { id, name, options, .. } = field;` then build option_map by consuming `options`: `for opt in options.unwrap_or_default() { option_map.insert(opt.name, opt.id); }`, and insert with moved `name`: `fields.insert(name, FieldMeta { field_id: id, options: option_map });`.
3. Preserve existing null-skip and parse-error-warn behavior. For the typed-page approach, null/union variants are handled by `#[serde(default)]` + `Option` plus tolerating unknown fields; unparseable individual nodes would fail the whole page, so if that behavior must be preserved, keep per-node deserialization but take ownership of each Value (`nodes.into_iter()`).

Recommendation: Go with option (1-alt) — deserialize the page into a typed struct. It is the cleanest and eliminates every clone in the hot portion of this function. If the reviewer wants to preserve per-node error tolerance, instead take the nodes array by value (`nodes: Vec<Value>`) and iterate with `into_iter()` so `serde_json::from_value(node_value)` no longer needs a clone, then apply the destructuring fix for (2) and (3).

Risks:
- Behavior change around unparseable nodes: current code logs a warning and continues. A full typed-page deserialization would fail the entire page on one bad node. Per-node error tolerance should be preserved — confirm with reviewer before choosing the typed-page variant.
- Null node entries from union types (projects.rs:659) must still be skipped; serde with `Option<FieldNode>` in a `Vec<Option<FieldNode>>` handles this naturally.
- FieldNode.data_type is #[allow(dead_code)] and preserved for future validation — must remain in the struct after refactor.
- Pagination loop (cursor/hasNextPage after line 694) must remain untouched.
- This is explicitly NOT a hot path per the bead description; the change is cleanup, not perf-critical. Do not over-engineer.

Related tests:
- crates/unblock-github/tests/ integration tests covering setup_fields: `setup_fields_creates_all_seven_fields`, `setup_fields_is_idempotent`, `field_ids_cached_on_client_after_setup` — these exercise fetch_existing_fields indirectly and must continue to pass.
- No direct unit test for fetch_existing_fields (it is private async and depends on live GraphQL); coverage is via setup_fields integration tests which require GITHUB_TOKEN + UNBLOCK_PROJECT.
- Run: cargo test -p unblock-github, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --check.

title: Make integration test cleanup panic-safe using a drop guard or scopeguard
description:
File: crates/unblock-github/tests/integration.rs, lines 294-298 and 507-511

Test cleanup is not panic-safe. In both test cases the close_issue call that removes test issues from GitHub is placed inline after assertions. If any assertion panics before reaching that cleanup call, the test issues remain open on GitHub, polluting the repository state.

Applying a drop guard or the scopeguard crate (scopeguard::defer!) would ensure the cleanup closure runs unconditionally on scope exit, even when a panic unwinds the stack. This is the same pattern called out in the E2E test design (unblock-45a.12) and should be applied consistently to all integration tests that create real GitHub resources.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text: DECISION: Used a custom CloseIssueGuard drop guard instead of adding the scopeguard crate as a dependency. The async cleanup requires tokio block_in_place + block_on which scopeguard::defer! cannot express without the same manual plumbing. A custom struct avoids adding a new dependency for no real benefit.

title: Optimize add_issue_to_project: include node_id in CreateIssueResponse to avoid extra REST call
description:
File: crates/unblock-github/src/mutations.rs, lines 299-397

title: Add unit test for multi-page pagination loop in fetch_graph_data()
description:
File: crates/unblock-github/src/graphql.rs — fetch_graph_data() pagination loop

No unit test exercises the multi-page pagination path with mocked responses. The INVESTIGATION planned this but it was not implemented.

Requires mocking infrastructure for multi-page HTTP responses (e.g., a mock HTTP layer or a trait-based client abstraction that can simulate paginated GitHub GraphQL responses across multiple pages).

Integration tests provide adequate coverage for now, but a dedicated unit test would catch regressions in the pagination loop logic without requiring a live GITHUB_TOKEN.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: The fetch_graph_data() pagination loop (graphql.rs:247-301) has no unit test for multi-page iteration. All existing tests for this file test individual parsing functions (parse_graph_issue, extract_blocking_edges, etc.) but never the pagination loop itself. The only coverage is the integration test (tests/integration.rs:131-219) which requires a live GITHUB_TOKEN and a repo with enough issues to trigger pagination (>100 open issues).

Files:
- crates/unblock-github/src/graphql.rs:242-310 — fetch_graph_data() method containing the pagination loop under test
- crates/unblock-github/src/graphql.rs:325-380 — graphql() method that sends HTTP requests (the seam that needs mocking)
- crates/unblock-github/src/graphql.rs:483-545 — parse_graph_issue() pure function already unit-tested
- crates/unblock-github/src/graphql.rs:552-569 — extract_blocking_edges() pure function already unit-tested
- crates/unblock-github/src/graphql.rs:121-180 — FETCH_GRAPH_DATA_QUERY constant (the query shape determines expected JSON structure)
- crates/unblock-github/src/client.rs:23-36 — GitHubClient struct (concrete reqwest::Client, no trait abstraction)
- crates/unblock-github/tests/integration.rs:131-219 — existing integration test for fetch_graph_data (requires GITHUB_TOKEN)
- crates/unblock-github/Cargo.toml — no mock libraries currently in dependencies

Approach:
1. Add wiremock as a dev-dependency in crates/unblock-github/Cargo.toml — it integrates natively with tokio and reqwest, no trait refactoring needed. It starts a local HTTP server that the reqwest client can hit.
2. Create a helper function (e.g., make_test_client_with_base_url) in the test module that constructs a GitHubClient pointing at the wiremock server URL instead of api.github.com. The client.rs already has make_test_client in its #[cfg(test)] mod — follow that pattern but accept a custom api_base_url.
3. Write a test that mounts two wiremock handlers: first request returns page 1 (hasNextPage:true, endCursor:'cursor1', 2 issue nodes), second request (with cursor='cursor1') returns page 2 (hasNextPage:false, 1 issue node). Assert fetch_graph_data() returns all 3 issues and correct edges across both pages.
4. Write a second test for the infinite-loop guard (graphql.rs:289-298): mock a response with hasNextPage:true but endCursor:null, verify the function returns the partial results without looping.
5. Optionally write a test for a single-page response (hasNextPage:false on first request) to verify no extra requests are made.

Risks:
- The graphql() method (line 325) builds the URL via self.graphql_url() which derives from api_base_url. The test client must set api_base_url to the wiremock server URL so requests route correctly.
- The graphql() method checks for GraphQL-level errors in the response JSON (errors array). Mock responses must not include an errors key or the method will return Err before the pagination loop processes data.
- The GitHubClient struct fields are private, so the test helper needs to construct the struct directly (like make_test_client in client.rs:653-661 does) — this only works within the crate's #[cfg(test)] modules, not in tests/. The test should go in graphql.rs's existing mod tests block or a new #[cfg(test)] module in graphql.rs.
- wiremock request matching needs to distinguish page 1 (cursor: null) from page 2 (cursor: 'cursor1') by inspecting the JSON body. wiremock's body_json or body_partial matchers can handle this.

Related tests:
- crates/unblock-github/src/graphql.rs mod tests (line 794) — existing unit tests; new tests go here
- crates/unblock-github/tests/integration.rs:131-219 — integration test for fetch_graph_data (no changes needed)

3. Create crates/unblock-core/benches/cache_bench.rs with:

- graph_build benchmark provides baseline comparison (build cost vs read cost)
- Arc::clone benchmarks should show O(1) constant time regardless of N (proving the Arc wrapping works)
- Concurrent reader benchmark validates no contention under load

- The async benches need a tokio runtime -- criterion's async_tokio feature handles this via b.to_async(tokio::runtime::Runtime::new().unwrap())

title: Track clone cost of get_ready_set and get_graph for large graphs
description:
get_ready_set() and get_graph() in GraphCache clone data out of the RwLock on every call. For graphs approaching 1000+ issues, the clone cost may become noticeable, particularly under high-frequency polling by multiple agents.

File: crates/unblock-core/src/cache.rs

This is acceptable for the v1 target (typical graphs are well under 1000 nodes), but there is no benchmark or monitoring in place. A future mitigation could be Arc-wrapping the cached value to allow cheap reference-counted clones instead of deep copies. This issue tracks the risk so it is not forgotten during a performance pass.
close_reason: QA passed. Arc-wrap cache implementation complete and validated.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: get_ready_set() (cache.rs:80-86) clones Vec<IssueSummary> and get_graph() (cache.rs:128-134) clones DependencyGraph on every call. Both are deep clones behind a tokio::sync::RwLock read guard.

Clone cost breakdown:
- IssueSummary contains 5 heap-allocated Strings (title, url, agent, milestone) + Vec<String> labels. At 1000 issues, ready set clone copies ~5000+ String allocations.
- DependencyGraph contains DiGraph<u64, ()> (petgraph arena + edge list), plus 3 HashMaps (node_map, issue_status, issue_state). At 1000 nodes the HashMap clones alone allocate ~3000 entries.
- Combined: a single get_ready_set()+get_graph() pair at 1000 issues involves O(thousands) of heap allocations.

Files:
- crates/unblock-core/src/cache.rs:80-86 (get_ready_set clones Vec<IssueSummary>)
- crates/unblock-core/src/cache.rs:128-134 (get_graph clones DependencyGraph)
- crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs:179-202 (IssueSummary struct - 5 Strings + Vec<String>)
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:28-39 (DependencyGraph struct - DiGraph + 3 HashMaps)
- crates/unblock-core/src/cache.rs:18-34 (CacheEntry holds both)

Current state: No benchmarks exist. No criterion/bench setup in Cargo.toml or benches/ directory.

Arc-wrapping approach:
1. Change CacheEntry to store Arc<Vec<IssueSummary>> and Arc<DependencyGraph>
2. get_ready_set() returns Option<Arc<Vec<IssueSummary>>> -- Arc::clone is O(1) atomic increment
3. get_graph() returns Option<Arc<DependencyGraph>> -- same O(1) clone
4. update() wraps new data in Arc before storing
5. Public API change: callers receive Arc<T> instead of T. If callers need mutation they call Arc::unwrap_or_clone() (rare path)
6. Alternative: wrap entire CacheEntry in Arc and return Arc<CacheEntry> from a single method

Benchmark recommendations:
1. Add criterion as workspace dev-dependency and create crates/unblock-core/benches/cache_bench.rs
2. Bench get_ready_set() and get_graph() at N=10, 100, 500, 1000, 2000 issues
3. Bench both current (deep clone) and Arc-wrapped (ref-counted) implementations
4. Include concurrent reader benchmark (multiple tokio tasks reading simultaneously)
5. Measure allocation count if possible (use dhat or similar) not just wall time
6. Add a graph build benchmark as baseline comparison (build cost vs clone cost)

Risks:
- Arc-wrapping changes the public API signature -- callers must adapt
- If any caller mutates the returned data, Arc prevents direct mutation (need Arc::unwrap_or_clone)
- MCP tool handlers are not yet implemented (only mod.rs exists), so API change impact is minimal right now -- ideal time to make the change
- The v1 target (well under 1000 nodes) means this is genuinely low priority

Related tests: crates/unblock-core/src/cache.rs mod tests (lines 137-393) -- all tests use get_ready_set/get_graph and would need signature updates if Arc-wrapped

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text: DECISION: Arc-wrapped individual fields (ready_set, graph) inside CacheEntry rather than wrapping the entire CacheEntry in Arc, because individual wrapping allows the two accessors to return independent Arc handles — a caller reading only the ready set does not pin the graph in memory.

title: Align tokio dependency in unblock-core to use workspace = true
description:
File: crates/unblock-core/Cargo.toml, line 19

The tokio production dependency is declared with a literal version = "1" instead of workspace = true with a feature override, which is the pattern used by all other workspace dependencies. This is a minor consistency concern that can drift over time as the workspace tokio version is updated — unblock-core would not automatically track the workspace-pinned version.

comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: In crates/unblock-core/Cargo.toml line 19, the production tokio dependency uses a literal version (version = "1", features = ["sync"]) instead of workspace = true. All other workspace crates (unblock-github, unblock-mcp) and all other deps in unblock-core itself use workspace = true. The workspace declares tokio with features = ["full"], which is a superset of "sync". If the workspace tokio version is bumped, unblock-core's production dep would not track it.

Files:
- crates/unblock-core/Cargo.toml:19 — the offending line: tokio = { version = "1", features = ["sync"] }

- crates/unblock-core/src/cache.rs:13 — only production usage: use tokio::sync::RwLock

Approach:
1. Replace line 19 in crates/unblock-core/Cargo.toml with: tokio = { workspace = true, features = ["sync"] }
   This inherits the workspace version while declaring the minimal feature set needed for production.
   Note: using just { workspace = true } would also work since "full" includes "sync", but explicitly listing features = ["sync"] documents the minimal requirement.
   Alternative: use simply { workspace = true } to match the pattern of other deps. The "full" feature from workspace already includes "sync". This is simpler but pulls more features than needed into production.
2. Run cargo check -p unblock-core to verify compilation.
3. Run cargo test -p unblock-core to verify tests pass.
4. Run the full quality gate (fmt, clippy, test, doc).

Risks:
- Very low risk change. Using workspace = true with features = ["sync"] is additive — Cargo merges the workspace features ("full") with the crate-level features ("sync"), so the resolved feature set is identical to just "full".
- No behavioral change whatsoever since "full" is already a superset of "sync".

comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: TraversalDirection enum (types.rs:212) only has Upstream and Downstream variants. ARCH §6.4 (unblock-architecture-github.md:402-406) specifies a third 'Both' variant for bidirectional traversal. The dependency_tree() method (graph.rs:319-360) uses a match on TraversalDirection with two arms (lines 329-334) that maps to petgraph Direction. Adding Both requires a different BFS strategy — running BFS in both Outgoing and Incoming directions from the root and merging results.

Files:
- crates/unblock-core/src/types.rs:212 — TraversalDirection enum definition, add Both variant here
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:319-360 — dependency_tree() method, update match to handle Both
- crates/unblock-core/src/graph.rs:329-334 — the match block that converts TraversalDirection to petgraph Direction (cannot simply map Both to a single Direction)
- docs/unblock-architecture-github.md:402-406 — ARCH §6.4 spec showing Both variant and DependencyTree struct

Approach:
1. Add Both variant to TraversalDirection enum in types.rs:212 with doc comment: '/// Follow both directions — upstream blockers and downstream dependents.'
2. Update dependency_tree() match in graph.rs:329-334. For Both: run BFS twice (Outgoing then Incoming) from the same root, using a shared visited set to avoid duplicates. Merge results into a single Vec<(u64, usize)>.
3. Update the DEVIATION comment at graph.rs:313-317 to remove the reference to unblock-b6b.21 (Both variant now implemented).
4. Add tests: (a) dependency_tree_both_returns_upstream_and_downstream, (b) dependency_tree_both_deduplicates_shared_nodes, (c) dependency_tree_both_respects_max_depth, (d) serde roundtrip for TraversalDirection::Both.

Risks:
- The match in dependency_tree() currently maps to a single petgraph::Direction. Both cannot map to a single direction — requires refactoring the BFS loop to iterate over both directions. Two approaches: (a) run BFS twice with shared visited set, (b) single BFS that follows neighbors in both directions at each step. Option (b) is cleaner and more consistent with BFS depth semantics.
- No consumers outside unblock-core currently use TraversalDirection (not referenced in unblock-github or unblock-mcp), so this is a safe additive change.
- The existing exhaustive match on TraversalDirection in dependency_tree() will cause a compile error when Both is added, which is exactly what we want — forces the implementor to handle it.

title: Harden GitHubUnavailable test against IPv6-disabled CI environments
description:
File: crates/unblock-github/src/errors.rs, line 109

The GitHubUnavailable test constructs a real reqwest::Error by attempting a connection to `[::1]:1` (IPv6 loopback) so that the error variant is exercised with a genuine transport error. On rare CI environments where IPv6 is disabled (e.g., some Docker-based runners or stripped-down VMs), this connection attempt may not produce the expected error or could behave differently, potentially causing a flaky test.

The risk is very low in practice, but the assumption is undocumented and a silent failure mode exists if IPv6 is unavailable.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: The test github_unavailable_display (errors.rs:106-119) uses http://[::1]:1 (IPv6 loopback port 1) to provoke a reqwest::Error. On CI environments where IPv6 is disabled at the kernel level, this may not produce a connection-refused error — it could yield a different error type or hang. The assumption that IPv6 loopback is available is undocumented.
Files: crates/unblock-github/src/errors.rs:106-119 — the test that needs hardening; .github/workflows/ci.yml:28-35 — CI runs on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest (both typically have IPv6 enabled, so current risk is low)
Approach: 1. Replace the IPv6 address [::1]:1 with the IPv4 address 127.0.0.1:1 as the primary target — IPv4 loopback is universally available and port 1 is reliably refused. 2. Alternatively, try IPv4 first and fall back to IPv6, but that adds unnecessary complexity — just use IPv4. 3. Update the comment on line 107 to document why 127.0.0.1:1 was chosen (port 1 is reserved/privileged, connection refused is guaranteed on all platforms). 4. Run the quality gate to confirm the test still passes.
Risks: Port 1 on IPv4 could theoretically be open if something is listening (extremely unlikely on CI or dev machines). If paranoia is warranted, try multiple ports (1, then 2), but this is overkill. The main risk is negligible — 127.0.0.1:1 is as reliable as it gets.
Related tests: crates/unblock-github/src/errors.rs — the test is inline in the module (github_unavailable_display at line 106). No other test files reference this pattern.

title: Validate UNBLOCK_LOG_LEVEL against known tracing levels at config load time
description:
File: crates/unblock-core/src/config.rs:166

UNBLOCK_LOG_LEVEL currently accepts any string without checking it against the set of valid tracing directive levels (error, warn, info, debug, trace). An invalid value may cause a silent fallback to a default level or a panic when the tracing subscriber is initialized, with no clear indication of which env var caused the problem.

Validation at config load time — checking the value against the known level set before passing it to the subscriber — would give the user an immediate, clear error message referencing UNBLOCK_LOG_LEVEL and listing accepted values.

Root cause: In config.rs:189, UNBLOCK_LOG_LEVEL is read as a raw string with no validation against the known tracing level set. The value is stored as String and will eventually be passed to tracing-subscriber's EnvFilter or LevelFilter. Invalid values (e.g., 'verbose', 'DEBUG2', typos) would either silently fall back to a default or panic at subscriber init time — far from where the config was loaded.

  - crates/unblock-core/src/config.rs:189 — log_level read without validation (just unwrap_or_else)

  - crates/unblock-core/src/errors.rs:107-111 — ValidationSnafu used for other config validation errors
  - crates/unblock-mcp/src/main.rs:17-20 — main() stub where tracing subscriber will be initialized

  4. On invalid value, return ValidationSnafu with message: 'UNBLOCK_LOG_LEVEL must be one of: error, warn, info, debug, trace; got: <value>'

title: Derive Hash for AgentKind and AgentClient when hash-key usage arises
description:
File: crates/unblock-core/src/client.rs -- AgentKind (line 27) and AgentClient type definitions.

The bead description for unblock-b6b.116 cites HashMap/HashSet use as the motivation for adding Eq to AgentKind and AgentClient, yet Hash was not derived in the same change. Using a type as a HashMap or HashSet key in Rust requires both PartialEq + Eq and Hash. Without Hash, neither type can actually serve as a hash-map key today, which is inconsistent with the stated motivation.

No current code uses AgentKind or AgentClient as hash keys, so this is not a blocking gap and is intentionally deferred. title: Proptest cycle-filtering loop rebuilds full graph per candidate edge
description:
File: crates/unblock-core/src/reconcile.rs, lines 898-913

The cycle-filtering loop inside the proptest strategy rebuilds the full dependency graph for every candidate edge it evaluates. At the current test bounds (30 nodes, 60 edges) the cost is acceptable, but the approach is O(E * V+E) — as bounds grow the overhead will compound linearly with the number of candidate edges.

An incremental topological sort (e.g., maintaining a topological ordering and only re-checking affected vertices when a new edge is considered) would scale better and keep proptest shrinking fast even at higher bounds.

No action needed now. Flag for revisit if proptest bounds are increased or if slow test runs are observed.
